I want to go on an adventure like you! Can I come next time? When I'm bigger?
I lost my shoe. Then I found it. It was on my foot.
My friend {friend} can wiggle their ears! I'm practicing.
I put a worm in my pocket. Mum found it. Mum screamed.
I like the sound of rain on the roof. It sounds like clapping.
I'm making a map of the village. The bell is in the middle and it's very big.
I can count all the cows. There are lots. Lots and lots.
Do you have a pet? I want a pet. A wolf! A tame one.
I had a dream that I could fly. I flew over the whole village!
I'm not crying, my eyes are just leaking because I bumped my knee.
The tavern smells like apples. I'm not allowed in yet. When I'm big!
I found a really good stick. It's a sword. And a wand. And a fishing rod.
I'm going to build the biggest sandcastle ever. Out of real sand blocks!
When the bard plays, I dance! Like this! Wheee!
My teacher says I'm clever. My teacher says I'm also loud.
I tried to ride a sheep. It didn't work.
Why is the sky blue? Nobody knows. I asked everyone.
I gave the golem a hug. It's very cold and very hard. Still nice.
I'm going to stay up until midnight tonight. Maybe. Probably not.
The best day is Market Day. There's honey cake!
I found a robin's egg! Well, a blue rock. But it looked like an egg!
I want to be just like you when I grow up, {player}.
My sister and I had a race. I won! She says she let me. She didn't.
I hid a cookie under my pillow for later. Then I forgot. Then the cat found it.
There's a monster under my bed. It's actually my slipper. But it might be a monster.
I can jump over the fence! Okay, the little fence. The very little one.
I'm learning to whistle. Pheeeew! Close enough.
My favorite food is everything with honey on it.
I've decided to be a scholar. I'm going to know every single thing.
I like when you visit. You're fun for a grown-up.
The goats are funny. They yell for no reason!
I sang a song for the chickens. They liked it. I think.
I've got a loose tooth! Wanna see? Wiggle, wiggle!
I'm going to marry a frog. A nice frog. When I'm older.
Grown-ups worry too much. I don't worry. I play.
I made mud pies! Don't eat them. I learned that the hard way.
The moon follows me when I walk at night! Everywhere I go!
I collected all the feathers in the chicken coop. Now I'm part chicken.
Today was the best day ever! Yesterday was also the best day ever.
I'm going to grow up to be the tallest villager in the whole world.
Shh, I'm a ninja. You can't see me.
I fed the fish in the pond. Some of them waved. Fish can't wave. These ones did.
I wrote my name in the dirt. It's a bit wobbly. The rain washed it away.
I'm going to train a parrot to say my name. And "cookie."
The well echoes! Hello! Hello! Hello! See?
I pretended to be a zombie and scared my brother. Then he cried. Then I said sorry.
Why do grown-ups drink coffee? It smells nice but tastes like burnt dirt.
My favorite animal is a llama. Because they spit! Ew! But funny!
I want to see the ocean one day. Is it really really big?
I'm brave. I walked past the dark barn all by myself. Fast. But by myself.
I found a mushroom! Don't worry, I didn't eat it. This time.
The baby next door can't talk yet. I'm teaching her words. She says "ba."
I've got a secret clubhouse. The password is "potato."
I'm a very good helper. I helped carry ONE apple today.
Stars are tiny holes in the sky's blanket. My grandpa said so.
I'm going to be a painter! I already painted the dog. He didn't like it.
baby.work: When I grow up I'm going to be a farmer and grow the biggest pumpkin ever!
I want to be a librarian so I can read all the books. ALL of them.
I'm going to be a knight and fight a dragon! A small one first.
I'll be a baker and make cookies every day. Cookies for breakfast!
I'm practicing being a fisherman. I caught a stick! It counts.
I want to be a cartographer and draw maps of everywhere!
When I'm grown I'm going to be a bard and sing all day.
I'm going to work at the sawmill! Saw saw saw!
My mum says I can be anything I want. Even a llama. Especially a llama.
I'd like to be an apothecary. I already know which flowers smell nice.
I'm going to be the golem's helper. Do golems need helpers?
I want to be a painter! I'll paint the whole village purple.
I'm going to be a cook! I can already make toast. Mostly burnt.
When I grow up I'll have a trade and an apron and everything!
I'm practicing my serious trading face. Hrrmm. Hrrmm!
I'm going to be the tavern keeper so I can have all the cider.
I'd be a shepherd! I love sheep. They're like clouds with legs.
I want to be an archer! I can already hit the barn. It's a big barn.
I'm going to be a tailor and make clothes for the cats.
When I'm big I'll be a scholar and know everything about everything.
I help my dad at work. I hold things. Very important job.
I want to be a mason and build a castle. A real one.
I'll be a cleric and make potions that turn things blue.
I'm going to work so hard and then take a nap. Like the nitwit.
Being a grown-up looks hard. You have to work AND be tired.
I made a workstation out of a box. It's a cookie workstation.
I'm going to be a carpenter! I already made a stick. It's a wooden stick.
I'd be a toolsmith and make a pickaxe made of cake.
I want to be everything! Can I be everything?
Grown-ups go to work and come home smelly. I can't wait!
I'll be a fletcher and make arrows out of chicken feathers! The chickens won't like that.
I'm going to be an adventurer like you. That's a job, right?
I'd be a leatherworker and make boots for every animal in the village.
I'm going to be a butcher. No, wait, I like the animals. A vegetable butcher!
I watched the smith hammer all morning. Clang clang! I want to clang!
When I'm big, I'll have a workstation right next to the bell.
I already know how to sweep. That's basically a job.
I'll be a painter and paint your portrait. You'll be very handsome. Or pretty. Very square.
My dream job is cookie taster.
I want to work at the market selling honey cakes. And eating the leftovers.
I'm going to be the bell ringer! Ding dong! Is that a job?
I'll be a guard and protect everyone. Even the cranky ones.
Every day I'm going to work and then play. Work then play. Perfect.
When I'm a farmer, I'll grow carrots for every rabbit in the world.
I'm learning about stars so I can be an astronomer. What's an astronomer?
baby.adventure: Did you fight a dragon? Was it big? Was it this big? Bigger?
Tell me about the scariest monster you ever saw!
Have you been to the bottom of the ocean? Are there mermaids?
When I'm bigger, I'm going on an adventure. Just like you!
Did you find treasure? Real treasure? Gold and diamonds?
Is it true that endermen steal blocks? Why do they want blocks?
I went on an adventure to the end of the garden. I found a snail.
Have you ever ridden a horse? A really fast one?
What's the farthest you've ever walked? Farther than the well?
Do zombies have friends? Do they play together?
I want to see a polar bear! Are they soft? Can you hug them?
Have you been in a cave? Is it dark? Are there bats? I love bats!
Did you sleep outside? Under the stars? With the monsters?
I went exploring in the barn. I found three eggs and a very angry chicken.
Is the Nether hot like soup? Or hot like the sun?
Have you seen a panda? I want to see a panda more than anything!
I'm going to sail a boat across the whole ocean someday.
Did you ever get lost? What did you do?
I want to find a dungeon. A friendly one. With friendly skeletons.
Have you been to the End? Is it really the end? What's after the end?
I made a treasure map of the village. X marks the cookie jar.
Can you take me on an adventure? Just a little one? To the river?
Are there villages like ours far away? With kids like me?
I want to climb the biggest mountain and wave at everyone.
I found a cave behind the waterfall! Okay, it's a dent in the rock. But it's MY cave.
Have you ever met a wandering trader's llama? Did it spit at you?
I'm going to tame a wolf and call him Sir Woofington.
Tell me a story about your adventures. A long one!
When I grow up I'll explore the whole world and come back and tell you about it.
Is it scary being an adventurer? I'd be brave. Mostly.
Have you seen the ocean? Is it blue all the way down?
I want to ride a pig! With a saddle! Into battle!
Did you ever fight a creeper? Did it go boom? Did you go boom?
I'm saving my pebbles for a big adventure. Pebbles are very useful.
Do you have a sword? Can I see? Ooh! Shiny!
Have you been to the jungle? Are there monkeys? There should be monkeys.
I went on an adventure in my dreams. I flew to the moon on a chicken.
What's the coolest thing you ever found?
I want to see snow! Lots of snow! A whole mountain of snow!
Promise you'll take me exploring when I'm grown up!
Is the world flat? My brother says it's square. Like everything.
I heard there's a mansion full of baddies in the forest. Did you go in?
I want to find a geode. They're like rocks with sparkly insides!
Do fish sleep? Have you seen a fish sleep?
When I go adventuring I'm bringing my whole rock collection.
baby.joke: Why did the chicken cross the road? To get to the other side! Hee hee!
Knock knock! Who's there? Banana. Banana who? Knock knock! Who's there? Orange. Orange you glad I didn't say banana!
What do you call a cow with no legs? Ground beef! My uncle told me that one.
Why did the cookie cry? Because its mother was a wafer so long! Hee!
What's brown and sticky? A stick! Ha ha ha!
Why can't a nose be twelve inches long? Because then it'd be a foot!
What do you call a sleeping dinosaur? A dino-snore! Zzzzz!
Why did the teddy bear say no to dessert? It was stuffed! Hee hee!
What's a pig's favorite color? Mud! Okay, mud's not a color. It should be.
Knock knock! Who's there? Boo. Boo who? Don't cry! It's just me!
Why do cows wear bells? Because their horns don't work! Moo!
What do you call a funny chicken? A comedi-hen!
Why did the zombie go to school? To get smarter! Grrr! Brains!
What do you call a fish with no eye? A fsh! Fsh! Get it?
Why did the golem cross the road? To pick up the flower! It's true, I saw it!
Knock knock! Who's there? Cow says. Cow says who? No silly, cow says MOO!
What do you call a bear with no ears? B! Hee hee!
Why are frogs so happy? They eat whatever bugs them!
What did the sheep say to the other sheep? Baaa! That's it. That's the joke. Baaa!
Why don't skeletons go to parties? They have no BODY to go with! Hahaha!
What has four legs and goes boo? A cow with a cold!
What's the fastest vegetable? A runner bean! Zoom!
Why did the banana go to the doctor? It wasn't peeling well!
What do you call a rabbit that tells jokes? A funny bunny! Hop hop!
Knock knock! Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold!
Why did the egg hide? It was a little chicken!
What do you call a duck that gets all A's? A wise quacker!
What do you call a cat that's a beach? A sandy claws! Hee hee!
Why did the creeper cross the road? Hssssss! BOOM! ...I don't know the end.
What's a ghost's favorite fruit? Boo-berries!
What's a pirate's favorite animal? An aaaaardvark! Arrr!
Why couldn't the pony sing? It was a little horse!
Why did the bee go to school? To get a little buzz! Bzzz!
What's a snake's favorite subject? Hiss-tory!
What do you get when you cross a snowman and a vampire? Frostbite! Grrr!
Knock knock! Who's there? Interrupting cow. Interrupting c- MOO!
Why did the tomato go red? It saw the salad dressing! Hee!
What's a cat's favorite dessert? Mice cream!
I told the golem a joke. It didn't laugh. Golems don't have funny bones.
What do you call a dog that does magic? A Labracadabrador! My favorite!
baby.weather.rain: Rain! Puddles! I'm going to jump in every single one!
Mum says I have to stay inside. The puddles are calling me!
I caught a raindrop on my tongue! It tasted like sky!
The worms are coming out! Hello, worms!
Rain sounds like a hundred tiny drums.
I'm a frog! Ribbit! Frogs love rain!
I made a boat out of a leaf and it sailed down the path!
I'm all wet and I don't even care!
The rain made a river in the road! It's MY river.
When it rains, the flowers drink. Glug glug glug.
baby.weather.thunder: The thunder's so loud! Is the sky angry?
I'm not scared of thunder. I'm just hiding under the table for fun.
Every time it flashes, I count! One, two, BOOM!
My dog is hiding under my bed. I'm hiding with him.
Is lightning hot? It looks hot.
Mum says thunder is just the clouds bumping heads.
I hope the golem's okay out there.
I'm being brave. Look how brave I'm being. Eek!
When it booms, I squeeze my cat. She doesn't like it.
I want the storm to stop so I can go play.
baby.weather.snow: SNOW! It's snowing! Snow snow snow!
I'm going to build a snow golem! A really big one!
I made a snow angel! Look! It's me but flat!
My nose is cold but I don't care! Snow!
Can I eat the snow? Mum says no. I already did.
I threw a snowball at my brother and he threw one back. War!
The snow's so deep it's up to my tummy!
Everything's white and sparkly! It's like the world's covered in sugar!
I want to slide down the hill on a boat! Is that allowed?
I wish it snowed every day forever!
baby.weather.clearing: Did you see the rainbow? I'm going to find the end of it!
Everything smells like wet grass! I love it!
The snails are out! I'm racing them.
I'm going to splash in every puddle before they dry up!
baby.weather.hot: It's so hot! I want to swim in the river!
My ice melted. Well, my snowball. It was a snowball from yesterday.
I'm hiding in the shade with the cats.
Can we have cold milk? It's so hot!
The sand's too hot for my feet! Ouch! Ouch!
I'm going to dig a hole and sit in it. It's cooler in holes.
baby.routine.wake: I had the best dream. There were cookies. Big ones.
I'm still sleepy. But I don't want to miss anything!
Morning! Is breakfast ready? Is it porridge?
I woke up before everyone! Even the rooster!
baby.routine.breakfast: I'm eating breakfast! It's porridge. With honey!
I have a milk mustache. Look!
Breakfast is my favorite meal. Then lunch. Then supper. Then snacks.
I ate all my bread and the crusts. The crusts make you brave!
Mum says I have to finish breakfast before I can play. I'm eating SO fast.
Can I have cookies for breakfast? No? Okay. Porridge.
baby.routine.play: We're playing tag! You're it! No tag-backs!
I'm hiding! Count to ten! No, twenty!
We're building a fort out of hay! Want to come in? Password's potato.
I'm a dragon! Rawr! I'm going to eat the village! Not really. Rawr!
Race you to the bell! Go!
We're playing village and I'm the golem. Clank! Clank!
I'm on a quest to find the shiniest pebble in the whole world!
Look at me jump! I'm jumping!
baby.routine.lessons: We're doing lessons! I'm learning about bees!
Shh, the teacher's talking. She's telling us about the stars.
I know my letters! A, B, C... um... bell!
We learned that sheep can be different colors! I want a purple one!
I'm learning numbers. Sixty-four is a whole stack!
Lessons are fun today. We're drawing maps!
baby.routine.lunch_home: I'm having lunch at home! Bread and cheese!
Mum made soup. I'm blowing on it. Whoosh!
Lunch! I'm so hungry I could eat a whole cow. A small one.
I'm eating my carrots first so I can have dessert.
Lunch is short! I have to eat fast and go play!
I shared my lunch with the cat. She ate the cheese.
baby.routine.market: It's Market Day! I got a copper! I'm buying a honey cake!
There are so many stalls! I want everything!
Market Day is the best day! There's music and cake!
I saw a llama at the market! It looked at me funny!
I traded my best pebble for a ribbon. Good trade!
Mum says I can have ONE treat. I'm choosing very carefully.
baby.routine.supper: It's supper time! We're having stew. We're always having stew.
I have to eat my vegetables. I'm hiding them under my bread.
Supper with everyone is the best!
I'm so full! My tummy is round like a pumpkin!
Dad told a funny story at supper. Milk came out my nose!
After supper I get a story. Then bed. Booo, bed.
baby.routine.evening: I'm getting ready for bed. Do I have to?
Mum's reading me a story. It's about a brave chicken.
I'm in my pajamas. They have bells on them!
The stars are coming out! I'm counting them! One, two, lots!
I'm not tired. I'm just resting my eyes. Very hard.
Can I stay up five more minutes? Please? Five?
baby.routine.sleep: I'm supposed to be asleep. Shh, don't tell!
I'm so sleepy... but I want to talk to you...
Goodnight! Will you be here tomorrow?
I sleep with my wooden sword. In case of monsters.
Night night! Don't let the spiders bite!
baby.routine.shelter: I have to stay inside because of the rain. Boooring!
I'm watching the rain from the window. Drip drip drip.
Can I go out? Just for one puddle? Please?
I'm building a fort out of blankets until the rain stops.
The rain's making music on the roof!
I'm drawing pictures of rainbows to make the rain stop.
baby.routine.storm: I'm hiding! The thunder's too loud!
Mum's holding my hand. I'm not scared. She is. A little.
The lightning made the whole room white!
I'm under the table with my dog. We're very brave.
When will the storm stop? Soon? Now? Now?
I'm counting the booms. Seven so far!
baby.routine.snowed_in: We're stuck inside because of the snow! Can we go play in it?
I'm warming my toes by the fire. They're toasty now!
Mum made hot cocoa! It's the best thing ever!
I'm drawing snowflakes on the frosty window!
The snow's so high it's covering the door!
I want to go out and make a snow golem!
baby.routine.rain_walk: I'm splashing in puddles! Splash! Splash!
I'm a duck! Quack! Ducks love rain!
I'm soaking wet! Mum's going to be so mad. Worth it!
Look how big this puddle is! It's an ocean!
I'm dancing in the rain! Come dance!
baby.routine.snow_play: I'm building a snow golem! He needs a pumpkin head!
I made a snow angel! It's the best one ever!
I'm sliding on the ice! Wheee! Ow. Wheee!
My mittens are soaked but I don't care!
I'm making a snow fort! It's going to be HUGE!
baby.time.dawn: It's so early! The roosters are still yawning.
The sky's pink! Like a strawberry!
Shh, everyone's still asleep. Except me!
I got up to see the sunrise! It was worth it!
baby.time.morning: I've already found two beetles and a snail this morning!
The morning sun is warm on my face!
It's morning! The whole day is ahead! So much playing to do!
baby.time.noon: The sun's right on top of us! I can't find my shadow!
Noon means lunch, and lunch means food!
I'm hungry. Are you hungry? I'm always hungry.
baby.time.afternoon: The afternoon's the best for playing tag!
I'm not tired! Okay, a little tired.
The shadows are getting long! Mine's taller than me!
Afternoon is when the cats nap. I don't nap. I'm too busy.
baby.time.evening: The sun's going down! It's all orange!
Mum says I have to come in soon. Five more minutes!
The fireflies are coming out! I'm going to catch one!
It's getting dark! Time for stories!
baby.time.night: I'm supposed to be in bed! Shh!
The stars are out! I'm making wishes on them!
Night is spooky. I like spooky. A little.
Are there monsters out there? The golem will protect us!
baby.time.late: I can't sleep! There's too much thinking in my head.
It's so late! I've never been up this late! I'm so grown up!
I heard a noise. Was it a ghost? It was probably the cat.
I'm only up because I needed water. And to see the moon.
baby.market: It's Market Day! Everything smells like honey cake!
Mum gave me a copper to spend. I'm going to spend it so carefully.
There's a juggler at the market! Well, the bard juggling apples. Badly.
I saw so many stalls! Toys and ribbons and cakes!
On Market Day nobody makes me do chores!
I want to buy a wooden sword. And a cake. And a llama.
greet.dawn: You're up early! The roosters haven't even finished complaining.
Morning already? The sky's still deciding what color to be.
Ah, a fellow early riser. The dew's still on everything.
Good dawn to you. I always think the first hour belongs to whoever's awake for it.
Shh, the village is still yawning. Hello, though!
Up with the sun, are we? Or did you never go to bed?
The bread isn't even in the oven yet, and here you are.
Look at that sky. Pink and gold, like someone spilled a pie.
Hello! I'm only half awake, so be gentle with me.
Early bird, are you? The worms are terrified.
The well water's coldest at dawn. Very good for waking up. Very bad for my toes.
Good morning! Or very late night, depending on how you look at it.
You caught me before my first cup of anything. Hello!
The mist's still sitting on the fields. I love this hour.
Well, good dawn, {player}. You look like someone with plans.
Mornings like this make the whole village smell of woodsmoke and wet grass.
Hello! I just watched the sun come up over the rooftops. Free show, every day.
The golem's on its first round of the day. So am I.
greet.morning: Good morning! The day's still full of possibilities.
Hello there! The village is properly awake now.
Good morning. Everything smells like fresh bread at this hour.
Ah, morning visitors. My favorite kind.
Hello! The bell's already rung twice and I've already lost my gloves once.
Morning! I've got the whole day ahead and absolutely no idea what to do with it.
Good morning! You've got that "going somewhere" look.
Hello, hello! The chickens are out and so are we.
A fine morning to you. The air's crisp and the gossip is fresh.
Good morning! If you're looking for trouble, try somewhere else. If you're looking for company, here I am.
Morning! The shadows are long and the queue at the well is longer.
Hello! I always feel braver in the mornings.
Morning, friend of the village! What brings you by?
Good morning. Mind the puddle by the path, it's deeper than it looks.
Hello! It's {time} and I've already had three conversations about turnips.
Morning! I love how the light comes through the window at this hour.
Good morning, {player}. The day's young and so am I, in spirit.
greet.noon: Midday already? My stomach noticed before I did.
Hello! Perfect timing, I was just thinking about lunch.
Noon, and the sun's right on top of us. Nowhere to hide from it now.
Hello there! The shadows have all gone for their break.
Good day! It's the hour when everyone in {village} smells of somebody's soup.
Ah, hello! The bell's about to ring for lunch, I can feel it.
Midday greetings! Half the day's gone and I've done about a quarter of it.
Hello! It's warm enough for the cats to stop moving entirely.
Hello! Join me in pretending I've been productive all morning.
Noon! The perfect time to stand still and talk to someone.
Hello! Have you eaten? You look like you haven't eaten.
Good day, {player}. The sun's at its highest and so are my spirits.
Hello! I was halfway through a sandwich in my head.
Midday already. Where does the morning go? Somewhere nicer than here, probably.
Hello! The market stalls are busy and the gossip is busier.
greet.afternoon: Good afternoon! The day's settled into itself now.
Hello! Afternoons are for slow walks and long talks, I always say.
Afternoon, {player}! The light's gone all golden.
Ah, hello! The busy part of the day is over and the nice part's begun.
Good afternoon. I've done my share for today, so I'm all yours.
Hello there! The bees are out in force this afternoon.
Afternoon! The bread's long gone but the company's still good.
Hello! It's the sleepy part of the day. Talk to me so I don't nod off.
Good afternoon! You've caught me in a thinking mood.
Hello! The shadows are starting to stretch. I like that.
Afternoon greetings! The village feels lazy and warm today.
Hello! It's {time} already. The day's sneaking away from me again.
Good afternoon. If you hear snoring from the hayloft, no you didn't.
Hello! I always feel chatty in the afternoon.
Afternoon! The children are out of lessons and the noise level is climbing.
Good afternoon, friend. The sun's on its way down but it's in no hurry.
greet.evening: Good evening! The lanterns are going up one by one.
Evening, {player}! Supper smells drift all over {village} at this hour.
Hello! The sky's going orange. Sit a while?
Good evening. Everyone's heading home, but I'm glad you stopped.
Evening already? The day went past like a startled rabbit.
Hello! The light's soft and the day's work is done.
Good evening! The bell's quiet and the crickets have taken over.
Evening, friend. This is my favorite hour for a chat.
Hello! I can hear the tavern from here. Can you?
Good evening. It's getting dark soon, so let's not dawdle too long.
Evening! The cows are complaining about dinner, same as every evening.
Hello there! The first stars are coming out.
Good evening, {player}. You'll want to be indoors before long.
Evening! The smoke from the chimneys goes straight up when it's this still.
Hello! I just lit my lamp and saw you through the window.
Good evening! It's been a long day. Make it a good ending.
greet.night: You're out late! Aren't you worried about the zombies?
Good evening, or should I say good night? It's very dark out.
Oh! You startled me. Not many visitors after dark.
Hello! Quietly, now. Half the village is asleep.
It's late, {player}. Stay close to the lamps.
Night visitor! I hope you've got a sword and a sensible reason.
Hello. The stars are out, and so are the skeletons, so mind yourself.
Good night to you! I was just about to turn in.
You're brave, walking around at this hour.
Hello! I heard something groaning near the fields. Probably the wind. Probably.
Oh, it's you. I thought you were a creeper for a moment. You're much less green.
Late, isn't it? The golem's doing its rounds, at least.
Hello! I can't sleep either. Want to listen to the frogs?
Evening, or night, or whatever this is. Hello!
It's dark as a cave out there. Did you bring a torch?
Shh. The baby next door just fell asleep. Hello!
greet.late: Goodness, it's the middle of the night! Is everything all right?
Hello? It's {time}! Even the owls are tired.
You know it's past midnight, don't you? I'm only up because of the dog.
Oh! You gave me a fright. What are you doing up at this hour?
The middle of the night is no time for visiting, but... hello.
Can't sleep? Me neither. The moon's too bright.
Shh, shh. If my neighbor wakes up, we're both in trouble.
Hello, night owl. Mind the phantoms if you haven't slept in a while.
It's so late the stars are starting to look bored.
Ah, a midnight wanderer. You'd better have a good story.
Hello. I was dreaming about pie, so this had better be important.
Up at {time}? You and the zombies keep the same hours, it seems.
Oh, hello. I came out to check on the noise. It was a sheep.
Hush now, it's the quiet part of the night. What brings you?
greet.band.stranger: Hello, traveler! I'm {name}. I don't think we've met.
Oh, a new face! Welcome to {village}. I'm {name}.
Hello! You're not from around here, are you? I'm {name}.
Greetings, stranger. Are you lost, or just exploring?
Welcome! It's not every day someone new walks through {village}.
Hello there. I'm {name}, the {job} round here. And you are... {player}? Nice to meet you.
Oh! Hello. You'll have to forgive me, I'm not used to new faces.
Hello! If you're looking for the bell, it's in the middle. Everything here is in the middle.
A visitor! Mind the chickens, they don't trust anyone either.
Hello, stranger. You look like you've walked a long way.
Welcome to {village}. We're small, but we're friendly. Mostly.
Hello! I'm {name}. If anyone asks, I was very welcoming.
Ah, hello. I don't bite. The goat by the fence does, though.
Hello, {player}. I've heard about you. Good things, I think.
Oh, hello! Are you here to trade? Or just passing by?
Welcome, welcome! I'm {name}. Feel free to look around, just don't trample the carrots.
Good to meet you. Folks here call me {name}. You can too.
Hello! New faces always make the day more interesting.
Greetings! You've got a kind face. Kind of a square one, but kind.
Hello! Welcome to {village}. Tell me, what brings you all the way out here?
Ah, a visitor. The dogs didn't bark, so you must be all right.
Hello, I'm {name}. And before you ask, no, I don't know where the treasure is.
greet.band.acquaintance: Oh, it's you again! Hello, {player}.
Back again? You must like it here.
Hello! I remember you. You were the one with the very full pockets.
{player}! Good to see a familiar face.
Hello again. I was wondering when you'd pass through.
Ah, you're back. The village has been quiet without you.
Hello! Last time we talked, you said you'd come back. And here you are.
Oh, hello! I'm starting to recognize your footsteps.
Back in {village}, are you? Good, good.
Hello! You keep turning up. I'm starting to like it.
Ah, {player}! I was just thinking about our last chat.
Hello again! You're becoming part of the scenery. In a good way.
Oh, hi! You've got that "back again" look.
Welcome back! The chickens remember you too. They're pretending not to.
Hello! I told my neighbor about you. Only nice things.
Ah, good. I was hoping you'd stop by.
Hello again, {player}! What adventures have you had since?
There you are! I had a feeling it was a visiting sort of day.
Oh, hello! You look a bit more sunburned than last time.
Back already? Did you forget something, or did you miss us?
Hello! I saved a smile for you. Here it is.
Look who it is! Come in, come in. Well, there's no door, but you know what I mean.
greet.band.friend: {player}! My friend! Come here, sit a while.
There you are! I've got so much to tell you.
Hello, friend! The day just got better.
Oh good, it's you. I was hoping it would be you.
My favorite visitor! Don't tell the others.
Hello! I've been saving up stories for you.
{player}! You're a sight for sore eyes.
Ah, my friend's back in {village}. Everything's right with the world.
Hello, you! I was telling {neighbor} about you just this morning.
Friend! Did you eat? Have you slept? Tell me everything.
There's my favorite adventurer.
Hello, hello! The kettle's metaphorically on.
Oh, wonderful. I needed a friendly face today.
{player}! I knew it was you from all the way down the path.
Hello, friend. You've got dirt on your nose. No, other side. There.
Look at you! Back in one piece. That's my favorite kind of back.
Hello! I was just about to go looking for you. Not really. But I thought about it.
Ah, my friend the wanderer. Welcome home, or near enough.
There you are! The village didn't feel right without you.
Hello! I made a list of things to tell you and then I lost the list.
Friend! Come, come. The sun's nicer when you're here.
Oh, I'm so glad you're here. You always know what to say.
greet.band.close: {player}! My dear friend. Come here, let me look at you.
There you are. I always feel better when you visit.
Oh, I'm so happy to see you. Truly.
My dear friend! You've been gone ages. Or a day. It felt like ages.
Hello, you. I saved you the good seat. Well, the good patch of grass.
You're back! I worried about you, you know. Just a little.
{player}! I was hoping you'd come. I've missed our talks.
Ah, my good friend. Everything's a bit brighter now.
There's the face I was waiting for.
Oh, hello. You always turn up exactly when I need you.
My friend! Tell me everything. Leave out nothing. Especially the dangerous bits.
Hello, dear. You look tired. Sit a while with me.
You came! I knew you would.
There you are, my friend. {village} has been asking after you.
Ah! You. Come here. I've got something important to say. I'm glad you're here. That was it.
{player}, my friend. The days you visit are my favorite days.
Hello, you wonderful wanderer. Welcome back.
Oh good. I had a feeling today would be a good day, and here you are.
Dear friend! The well, the bell and I have all missed you.
Hello! Don't you dare leave without saying goodbye this time.
greet.band.best: My best friend! The whole village feels like home when you're here.
{player}! There you are. My favorite person in the whole Overworld.
Oh, my dearest friend. Come here. Sit. Stay as long as you like.
You! I'd know your footsteps anywhere.
Best friend! I've been counting the days. All right, I lost count. But I was counting.
There's my kindred spirit. Everything's better now.
Hello, my dear friend. I keep a little corner of every day for you.
{player}! I told everyone you'd be back. I was right, as usual.
My best friend in all the world! Hug? No? A very firm nod, then.
You're home! Well, you know what I mean. You're home to me.
Ah, there you are. Now the day can start properly.
My friend for life. Hello, hello, hello!
Oh, I've missed you so much. Tell me everything, and then tell me again.
{player}! I saved the best gossip just for you.
Hello, dearest. Whatever you need, I'm here.
There's my favorite face. Don't be gone so long next time.
Best friend! I baked a story for you. I mean, I have a story. I'm excited.
You came back! You always come back. That means a lot to me.
Oh, it's you! The day just turned golden.
My best friend's here! Somebody ring the bell. No, don't, it scares the cows.
greet.weather.rain: Come in out of the wet! Well, as in, out from under the clouds.
You're soaked! Did you walk all the way here in this?
Hello! Rainy days are for staying in and talking, I always say.
Oh, look at you, dripping. Stand under the eaves a moment.
Hello! The farmers are thrilled. Everyone else is damp.
Rain again! At least the crops are happy.
Hello, {player}. Don't mind the puddles, they're decorative.
What weather! The whole village smells of wet straw.
Oh, hello! I was just listening to the rain on the roof.
You brought the rain with you, I see. Or it followed you.
Hello! My hat leaks, but my spirits are dry.
Rain, rain. Lovely for the garden, terrible for my hair.
greet.weather.thunder: Get under cover! That thunder's close!
Hello! Did you hear that crack? It shook the windows.
You shouldn't be out in a storm like this! Stay near me.
Oh! I nearly jumped out of my boots. Hello.
Thunder! Everyone's hiding indoors. Smart people, every one of them.
Hello! Keep away from tall trees and the bell tower, please.
What a storm! The sky's having a terrible day.
Hello. If lightning strikes the pig pen again, we'll have a very confused pigman.
Oh, it's you! I thought it was the thunder knocking.
Hello! Stay close. I'm not scared, I'm just... cautious.
That storm's really rolling in, {player}. Let's keep this quick and dry.
Hello! Every flash makes the whole village go white for a moment. Eerie.
greet.weather.snow: Hello! Look at all this snow!
You must be frozen! Come stand by the fire.
Snowing again! The children are delighted. The rest of us are cold.
Hello, {player}! Your shoulders have snow on them.
Hello! Every roof in {village} is wearing a white hat today.
Brr! Hello! My nose has stopped working.
Hello! Mind the ice on the path, I've fallen twice already.
Snow! It makes everything so quiet.
Hello! I'd shake your hand but I can't feel mine.
Oh, a snowy visitor! Do you want something warm?
Hello! The snow's as deep as my boots and rising.
greet.weather.clearing: Hello! The rain's stopped. Smell that air!
Look, the clouds are breaking up! Hello!
Hello! Everything's sparkling after the rain.
Oh, hello. I came out the moment the rain stopped. Couldn't stay inside another minute.
The sun's back! And so are you. Hello!
Hello! Did you see the rainbow? It was right over the fields.
Mind the puddles, {player}. The children have been jumping in them all over.
Hello! The whole village is drying out like laundry on a line.
Everything smells green after rain. Hello!
greet.weather.hot: Hello! Phew, it's hot. Stand in the shade with me.
Hello! The sand's too hot to walk on barefoot. Don't ask how I know.
Hot one today. Hello! Do you have any water?
Hello! Even the lizards are hiding from this sun.
Scorching! Hello. Stay in the shade or you'll cook.
Hello! On days like this I envy the fish.
Hot enough to fry an egg on the wall. Somebody tried. It didn't work.
greet.market: Happy Market Day! The whole village is out.
Hello! It's Market Day, so mind your purse and your manners.
Market Day greetings! Have you been to the stalls yet?
Hello! It's Market Day, my favorite day of the week.
Market Day! No work, just talk and treats. Hello!
Hello! Everyone's at the bell today, trading and gossiping.
Ah, Market Day. The one day nobody asks me to work. Hello!
Hello, {player}! Come for the market, stay for the gossip.
Market Day! I've already bought three things I don't need.
Hello! The whole village smells of pies and wool today.
Market Day hello! Try the honey, if there's any left.
Hello! It's Market Day, so everyone's wearing their good hats.
Happy Market Day, {player}! The stalls are full and the jokes are terrible.
Hello! I love Market Day. Everyone's out, nobody's in a hurry.
Hello! The children have been running between the stalls all morning.
greet.personality.warmhearted: Oh, hello, dear! Come here, you look like you need a smile.
There you are! Have you eaten? You look peaky.
Hello, sweetheart. What can I do for you today?
Oh, it warms my heart to see you!
Hello, love! Sit down, sit down. Tell me how you are.
Welcome, welcome! Any friend of the village is a friend of mine.
Oh, my! Look at you. Come, I'll find you a snack.
Hello, dear one! I was just thinking of you.
greet.personality.thoughtful: Hello. I was just thinking about something. Several somethings, actually.
Ah, {player}. Hello. Have you ever wondered why bells are bell-shaped?
Hello. Forgive me if I'm distracted; my mind's halfway into a book.
Good to see you. I've been meaning to ask your opinion on something.
Hello. You arrived just as I was having a very interesting thought.
Ah, hello. Quiet days are good for thinking, but company's better.
Hello. I wrote down something clever earlier and now I can't read my own writing.
Hello, {player}. Do you think the stars know we're watching them?
greet.personality.playful: Hey hey! Look who it is!
Hello! Guess what I'm thinking. Wrong! It was pie.
Ta-da! Oh, it's just you. Hello! I was practicing my entrance.
Hello! I was just humming a tune. Want to hear it? Too late, here it comes.
Boo! Ha! Did I scare you? No? Rats.
greet.personality.adventurous: Hello, traveler! Where've you been? Anywhere exciting?
Ah, {player}! You've got the look of someone who's seen a jungle lately.
Hello! I was just planning a trip. In my head. Very detailed.
Hello! Tell me there's a dungeon in your story today.
Hey! Your boots are muddier than last time. Good sign.
Hello! I heard there's a shipwreck past the river. Want to go see?
greet.personality.meticulous: Hello. You're precisely on time. For what, I'm not sure, but on time.
Good day. Wipe your boots, please. Thank you.
Hello, {player}. I've just finished organizing my buttons by color.
Ah, hello. Mind the step; I swept it twice.
Hello. Everything's in order today, which makes me very happy.
Good day. Your collar's crooked. There. Better.
Hello. I've counted the chickens. All present. Hello to you, too.
greet.personality.steadfast: Hello there. Good to see you, same as always.
Morning or evening, I'm here. Hello, {player}.
Hello. Steady day today. I like steady days.
Ah, hello. Nice to see a reliable face.
Hello, friend. The garden's coming along. So's the day.
Hello. Same old me, same old village. Good to see you.
Hello there. Things are as they should be.
Hello, {player}. Sit if you like. I'm not going anywhere.
greet.personality.reserved: Oh, hello. I didn't hear you coming.
Hello. Quiet day. I like it that way.
Hi. ...Sorry, I'm not much of a talker. But I'm glad you're here.
Hello. You can stay a while, if you like.
greet.personality.imaginative: Hello! Did you know the clouds today look exactly like a flying sheep?
Oh, hello! I was just imagining a castle made of cake.
Greetings, wanderer from a faraway land! Or wherever you're from.
Hello! What color is your mood today? Mine's sort of teal.
Ah, {player}! You've arrived just as my daydream got good.
Hello! If you were a painting, you'd be a sunrise.
Hello! I've decided the moon is made of very shy cheese.
Oh, it's you! Hello! I was painting you in my head just now.
greet.personality.pragmatic: Afternoon. Or morning. Whatever it is, hello.
Hello, {player}. Make it quick, I've got wood to cut.
Hello. If you're here to talk, I'll listen while I work.
Right. Hello. What can I do for you?
Hello. Weather's fine, crops are fine, I'm fine.
Hello. Good timing; I just finished a job.
Hello. You've got a loose strap on your boot. Fix that before it trips you.
greet.personality.curious: Oh! Hello! Where did you come from? What's that? Where are you going?
Hello! Can I ask you something? Several somethings?
Hello, {player}! What did you find today?
Oh, hello! Have you ever seen the end of the world? The very edge?
Hello! I've been wondering about something and you look like someone who'd know.
Hi! What's in your pockets? Sorry. Hello first.
Hello! Is it true that some caves glow? I need to know.
Oh, it's you! Tell me something I don't know.
greet.personality.protective: Hello. Everything all right? You look a bit worn.
Hello. Anyone bothering you, you let me know.
Hello there. Watch yourself on the road out, it's been rough lately.
Hello. I keep an eye on things around here. You're welcome among them.
Good to see you in one piece, {player}.
Hello. Stay close to the village after dark, understand?
Ah, there you are. I was wondering if you'd made it back.
greet.personality.gentle: Oh, hello. It's lovely to see you.
Hello, {player}. The flowers are blooming beautifully today.
Hello, dear. Would you like to sit in the sun a while?
Oh, hello. You have a kind sort of quiet about you.
Hello. I hope your day has been gentle with you.
Hello there. I just watered the poppies. They say hello too.
Oh, how nice. A visitor. Hello.
Hello, {player}. Mind the little sprouts by the path.
home.plains: The plains go on forever. Grass and sky, grass and sky. I love it.
We get every kind of weather in the plains. Sometimes in one afternoon.
Out here you can see a storm coming from a day away.
Horses run wild across the plains. Beautiful to watch.
I like flat land. You always know what's coming.
Sunflowers grow in fields out here. They all turn to follow the sun.
Plains folk are simple folk. Bread, sheep, and a good fence.
The wind across the grass sounds like the sea, they say. I've never seen the sea.
Every plains village has a bell in the middle. Ours rings the loudest. I'm sure of it.
You can walk for miles here and only see rabbits.
Our soil's the best for wheat. Golden fields as far as you can see.
I was born under a sky this big. I'd feel squashed anywhere else.
The plains are gentle, mostly. Except for the zombies at night.
I like the smell of rain on the grass out here.
There's always a breeze in the plains. Good for drying washing.
We have the friendliest bees in the plains. Lots of flowers.
A plains sunset is the widest sunset there is.
Oak trees here grow round and lazy. Like they've got nowhere to be.
Travelers say plains villages all look the same. They don't look closely.
I've lived on the plains all my life. Every hill's a friend.
home.desert: The desert's hot by day and cold by night. You learn to love both.
Sand gets everywhere. In your boots, your bed, your bread.
We build with sandstone. Cool inside, even at noon.
Water's precious here. We never waste a drop.
The stars in the desert are the brightest in the world.
Cactus is good for green dye. And for not sitting on.
Husks wander the dunes at night. Like zombies, but sunburnt.
Desert folk wear their scarves high against the sand.
We grow sugar cane by the oasis and trade it for everything else.
The dunes shift every year. The village never moves.
I've heard the desert temples hide treasure. And traps.
The camels are my favorite. Tall, patient, a little smug.
In the desert, shade is a gift and a friend is a well.
Sandstorms are rare, but you never forget one.
We don't get rain here. When we do, everyone dances.
The heat makes everyone slow and kind.
Our houses have flat roofs. We sleep up there on hot nights.
The desert looks empty, but it's full of life if you look.
A good well's the heart of a desert village. Ours is deep and sweet.
Sunrise over the dunes turns everything gold.
home.savanna: The savanna's golden and wide. Acacia trees like umbrellas.
Our houses are acacia wood. Orange inside. Warm and bright.
Horses and llamas roam the savanna. Nobody owns them. Everyone loves them.
It never rains much here, but when it does, the grass turns green overnight.
The plateaus rise up like tables for giants.
The sunsets on the savanna are orange and pink and purple all at once.
We grow wheat on the flats and graze sheep on the hills.
Armadillos wander through sometimes. Little armored fellows.
The acacia trees lean every which way. I think they're dancing.
Savanna folk are tough. Hot sun, dry ground, big hearts.
At night you can hear the wind through the long grass.
Our village sits on a high plateau. Best view in the world.
The ground cracks in the dry season. We wait for the rains.
Every savanna house has a good shady porch.
I love the smell of dry grass in the heat.
Llamas come down from the hills to drink at our well.
The sky here is enormous. It makes you feel very small and very free.
We trade acacia wood for things we can't grow.
The cartographer says our plateau's on three different maps.
Living on the savanna teaches you patience. The rain comes when it comes.
home.snow: Winter lasts most of the year here. We're used to it.
Our houses are spruce and stone. Thick walls, warm hearths.
Snow's lovely to look at and terrible to shovel.
The polar bears wander close sometimes. We leave them alone.
We keep the fires going day and night in the cold months.
Ice spikes stand on the plains like frozen towers. Beautiful and dangerous.
Strays wander out here. Skeletons that shoot slowness arrows. Brr.
Snow villages are close-knit. You have to be, in the cold.
Nothing tastes better than hot stew after a day in the snow.
The frozen rivers are perfect for fishing through the ice.
We wear three layers and still feel the cold.
The quiet after a snowfall is the most peaceful thing I know.
Igloos dot the snowy plains. Some of them have secrets underneath, they say.
Our children learn to walk on ice before they learn to run.
Powder snow can swallow you whole. Mind your step.
The northern lights dance over us some nights. Or I dream they do.
Snow golems are the only golems that like it here.
We store food all summer for the long winter.
Every snow village has a good cobbler. Boots matter here.
When the sun comes out on fresh snow, it's like the world's made of diamonds.
home.taiga: The taiga smells of pine needles and woodsmoke.
Our houses are spruce, dark and sturdy. Built to last.
Wolves howl in the forest at night. They're mostly harmless. Mostly.
Sweet berries grow wild here. Prickly, but delicious.
The foxes come right up to the houses sometimes. Bold little things.
The spruce trees grow so tall you can't see their tops.
Taiga folk are quiet, steady people. Like the trees.
Ferns and mossy boulders everywhere. It's very green.
The rain here is soft and constant. Everything's damp and alive.
We chop spruce for houses and pinecones for the fire.
Mushrooms grow in the shade of the old trees. Some are tasty. Some aren't.
In winter, the taiga turns white and silent.
The old growth forest past the hill has trees older than anyone remembers.
Our pumpkin patches do well here. Cool weather, rich soil.
The foxes steal our chickens. We've come to an arrangement. They still steal the chickens.
A taiga village feels hidden. Safe, among the trees.
The smell of pine is the smell of home.
We trade spruce logs and furs for things from the south.
The forest is full of sounds if you listen. Owls, wolves, wind.
I like the dark of the forest. It's cozy, not scary.
home.jungle: The jungle's loud day and night. Birds, frogs, rustling leaves.
It rains here more than anywhere. Everything's green and dripping.
Parrots live in the trees. They copy every sound they hear.
Bamboo grows faster than you can cut it.
Cocoa grows on the jungle trees. Cocoa means cookies.
Ocelots slink through the undergrowth. Shy, beautiful cats.
The vines grow everywhere. On the houses, the trees, me, if I stand still.
They say there's a temple deep in the jungle with a puzzle inside.
The heat and the damp make everything grow huge. Even the melons.
Pandas wander in from the bamboo groves. They're very lazy. Very cute.
Jungle trees are so tall they make their own weather.
You can get lost in the jungle in three steps.
We build our houses up on stilts sometimes, away from the wet ground.
Melons grow wild here. Sweet and cool on a hot day.
The jungle never sleeps. Even at night it hums.
The leaves are so thick, the forest floor's always twilight.
I love the smell of the jungle after rain. Earthy and alive.
The parrots here know rude songs. Don't ask who taught them.
Jungle folk are cheerful folk. All this green is good for the spirit.
There's more life in one jungle tree than in a whole plains field.
home.swamp: The swamp's murky and misty. But it's home.
Frogs everywhere! Little ones, big ones, all singing at night.
Witches live in huts out in the water. We don't visit.
Slimes bounce out of the swamp on full moons. Squishy and annoying.
Lily pads make good stepping stones if you're careful.
The trees here grow right out of the water. Their roots hang like curtains.
Mud's a way of life in the swamp.
The mangroves tangle so thick you can barely row a boat through.
Swamp water's dark but the fish are fat.
At night the fireflies light up the whole marsh.
We build our houses on raised ground. Wet feet are no fun.
Mushrooms grow everywhere in the swamp. Brown ones, red ones.
The swamp smells of mud and growing things. You get used to it.
Swamp folk are tough and quiet. And very good at not slipping.
The frogs here change color depending on where they hatched. Isn't that something?
The fog rolls in every evening. Spooky, but pretty.
Bogged skeletons wander the marsh. They shoot poison arrows. Nasty.
Blue orchids grow only in swamps. My favorite flower.
I love the sound of rain on the swamp water. Like a thousand tiny bells.
The swamp's not pretty to everyone. It's pretty to me.
village.golem: The golem's standing right over there. Doesn't it look noble?
Our golem's been walking the same path for years. It knows every stone.
I gave the golem a poppy once. It held it all day.
The golem's cracked on one side. I hope someone has iron to patch it.
Don't hit any villagers near the golem. It takes that very personally.
The golem's the best neighbor. Quiet, strong, protective.
I feel safer with the golem nearby. Silly, but true.
The golem stopped and looked at the sunset with me last night.
When the golem's near, the zombies stay away.
The golem picked up the baker's son and spun him around. He laughed for an hour.
Did you know golems are made when villagers are scared together? Funny, a protector born of fear.
I polish the golem's head sometimes when it's not looking. It doesn't seem to mind.
village.cat: There's a cat nearby. Creepers hate cats, you know.
That cat's been following me all day. I think it wants my fish.
The village cats keep the phantoms away. Good kitties.
I've named that cat Biscuit. I don't know if it has another name.
Cats sleep on beds when you're not looking. And when you are.
That cat brought me a present this morning. A dead rabbit. Lovely thought.
A village with cats is a village without creepers. Mostly.
I like cats. They don't need you, but they choose you anyway.
That cat's got the right idea. Sun, nap, repeat.
The cats rule this village, really. We just live here.
village.trader: The wandering trader's in town! Mind the llamas, they spit.
That trader's got the strangest goods. Saplings from far away, glowing ink.
I always wonder where the wandering trader sleeps.
The trader's prices are steep, but sometimes they have something you can't get anywhere else.
Those llamas are nervous. Don't make any sudden movements.
The trader drinks a potion and goes invisible at night. Very mysterious.
I bought a strange flower from the trader once. It still hasn't bloomed.
The trader doesn't say much. Just "hm" and "hrm."
If you're looking for blue ice or sea pickles, the trader's your best bet.
The llamas chewed my washing line last time the trader came.
village.children: The children are out playing. Listen to them shriek!
Those little ones run around all day. Where do they get the energy?
Watch your step, the children are playing tag.
The children of {village} keep us all young.
One of those children asked me if the moon is made of cheese.
The kids are building something by the haystacks. A fort, I think.
I love hearing the children laugh. It's the sound of a happy village.
The children follow the golem around like ducklings.
Mind your ankles, there are small people everywhere.
When I was that small, I thought the bell was a giant's hat.
village.friends: You've become such a regular here. It's lovely.
The village feels different when you're around. Brighter.
Half of {village} knows your name now.
You're practically a resident at this point.
{neighbor} asked about you yesterday. You're popular.
We should get you a house here. Then you'd never have to leave.
You've got friends all over {village} now. I'm proud to be one.
People smile when they see you coming. That's a good sign.
village.newcomers: Everyone's curious about you. Don't mind the staring.
The children think you're a knight from a faraway land.
{neighbor} asked me who you were. I said a friend. Was that right?
Get to know a few of us and you'll feel at home in no time.
News travels fast here. By supper, everyone will know you visited.
The village takes a while to warm to new faces. I'm faster than most.
Say hello to the others too. We're a friendly lot, under it all.
I like meeting new people. We don't get many here.
joke.general: Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts.
What did the zombie say to the villager? Nothing. It just groaned. Zombies aren't great at conversation.
Why did the creeper go to the party? It heard it was going to be a blast.
What do you call a pig that knows karate? A pork chop.
Why did the chicken cross the road? To prove to the creeper it wasn't chicken.
How does a skeleton call its friends? On the tele-bone.
Why was the enderman so good at hide and seek? It kept teleporting before you finished counting.
What's a ghast's favorite food? Ghastly stew.
Why do cows wear bells? Because their horns don't work.
What did the iron golem say to the zombie? "Iron out your differences." Then it threw it.
Why did the sheep say "moo"? It was learning a second language.
How do you make a skeleton laugh? Tickle its funny bone.
What kind of music do mummies like? Wrap music. We don't have mummies, but I still like that one.
Why don't zombies ever get lost? They follow their noses. Mostly the smell of villagers.
What do you call a creeper that's always grumpy? A sour-puss. Hiss.
Why was the furnace so popular? It was always smelting with laughter.
What's a skeleton's least favorite room? The living room.
Why did the slime refuse to leave the swamp? It was too attached.
What did one ore say to the other? "Let's get mined."
Why did the miner bring a ladder? To reach new depths. Wait, no.
How do you know a spider is good at building? It's a natural webmaster.
Why did the bread never get lonely? It was always with its loaf-ed ones.
What's a librarian's favorite vegetable? Quiet peas.
Why did the bee get married? It found its honey.
What do you call a sleeping bull? A bulldozer.
Why don't villagers play cards in the jungle? Too many cheetahs. Well, ocelots.
What's the best way to talk to a creeper? From very far away.
Why did the cow go to space? To see the moooon.
What did the fish say when it hit a wall? Dam.
Why couldn't the enderman find a date? Every time it looked at someone, they screamed.
What do you call an iron golem with no flowers? Grumpy.
What's a zombie's favorite bean? A human bean. Oh dear.
Why are spiders such good web designers? Years of practice.
Why did the potato cry? It was baked too long and felt crusty.
What did the bell say to the villager? "Ring me sometime."
Why did the pumpkin go to the party alone? It had no body to go with.
How does a villager fix a broken pumpkin? With a pumpkin patch.
What's a ghost's favorite dessert? Boo-berry pie.
Why don't creepers get invited to parties? They always blow it.
What does a cow use to do math? A cow-culator.
Why was the bed always tired? It never got any sleep. People kept sleeping on it.
What did the wheat say to the farmer? "Stop stalking me."
Why did the villager stare at the orange juice? The label said concentrate.
What's an emerald's favorite saying? "Trade you for it."
Why did the arrow go to school? To get a little sharper.
What did the left eye say to the right eye? Between you and me, something smells. That's the nose.
Why do bees have sticky hair? They use honeycombs.
What do you call a dinosaur that's asleep? A dino-snore.
Why are fish so smart? They live in schools.
Why did the cookie go to the doctor? It was feeling crummy.
What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear.
Why don't eggs tell jokes? They'd crack each other up.
What do you get when you cross a sheep with a kangaroo? A woolly jumper.
Why was the math book sad? It had too many problems.
What did the ocean say to the beach? Nothing, it just waved.
Why can't a bicycle stand up by itself? It's two-tired. I don't know what a bicycle is, but the joke's still good.
What's brown and sticky? A stick.
Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field.
What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta.
Why did the golem cross the village? To get to the other side. And to throw a zombie on the way.
What do you call a sheep covered in chocolate? A candy baa.
How do trees get online? They log in.
What did the cobblestone say to the lava? "You're too hot to handle."
Why do witches fly on brooms? Vacuums are too heavy.
What's a skeleton's favorite instrument? The trom-bone.
What do you call a parrot that won't shut up? A villager.
Why did the torch go to therapy? It was burned out.
Why did the cat sit on the creeper? To make it purr-suade itself to leave.
How do you organize a party in space? You planet.
What did the sheep say to the other sheep? "You're looking baa-utiful today."
Why did the zombie go to school? To improve its dead-ucation.
Why did the villager plant light bulbs? To grow a power plant.
What has a bottom at the top? A leg.
Why did the musician get locked out? He couldn't find the right key.
Why don't you ever see elephants hiding in trees? Because they're really good at it.
What did the stone say to the pickaxe? "Leave me a lone."
Why don't mountains get cold? They wear snow caps.
What do you call a witch at the beach? A sand-witch.
Why was the chicken team bad at baseball? Too many fowls.
What do you call a deer with no eyes? No idea.
Why did the pig take a bath? The farmer said "hogwash."
What kind of shoes do ninjas wear? Sneakers.
Why did the cow cross the road? To get to the udder side.
What's the best day to go to the beach? Sunday, of course.
What did the triangle say to the circle? You're pointless.
Why do bees hum? They forgot the words.
What's orange and sounds like a parrot? A carrot.
Why did the tomato blush? It saw the salad dressing.
What did the big flower say to the little flower? Hi, bud!
Why did the student eat his homework? The teacher said it was a piece of cake.
What has four legs but can't walk? A table. Or a very lazy cow.
Why don't skeletons ever go trick or treating? They have no body to go with.
What's a pirate's favorite letter? You'd think it's R, but it's the C.
What do you call a snowman with a six-pack? An abdominal snowman.
Why did the coffee file a police report? It got mugged.
What did the zero say to the eight? Nice belt.
Why did the cleric's potion go to the party? To get bottled up with friends.
What do you call a nervous javelin thrower? Shakespeare.
Why don't oysters share? They're shellfish.
What did the grape do when it got stepped on? It let out a little wine.
Why did the gardener plant his money? He wanted his emeralds to grow.
What do you call an angry carrot? A steamed vegetable.
Why do we tell actors to break a leg? Because every play has a cast.
What kind of tree fits in your hand? A palm tree.
What did the nose say to the finger? Quit picking on me.
Why can't you hear a pterodactyl going to the bathroom? Because the P is silent.
What's a cat's favorite color? Purr-ple.
What do you call a sleepy brewing stand? Well rested. It's been stewing all night.
Why did the bell get detention? It kept ringing in class.
What do you call cheese that isn't yours? Nacho cheese.
How does the moon cut its hair? Eclipse it.
Why did the zombie villager refuse the golden apple? It wasn't feeling weak enough.
Why don't you ever see a llama tell a joke? Because they spit out the punchline.
What do you call a well-dressed wolf? Dapper dog.
Why did the miner get fired? He took too many breaks. Stone breaks.
Why was the dirt block depressed? Everyone walked all over it.
What's an axolotl's favorite game? Axolotl questions.
What do you call a sheep with no legs? A cloud.
Why did the redstone get promoted? It was a real live wire.
What's a creeper's favorite subject at school? Hiss-tory.
How did the farmer find his wife? He tractor down.
What did one wall say to the other? I'll meet you at the corner.
Why don't villagers trust stairs? They're always up to something.
What did the baby corn say to the mama corn? Where's pop corn?
Why do cows lie down when it rains? To keep a dry spot.
What's a frog's favorite drink? Croak-a-cola.
What did the pumpkin say to its carver? Cut it out.
What's a tree's favorite drink? Root beer.
Why did the golem bring a flower to the meeting? Just in case anyone needed cheering up.
What do you call a bee that can't make up its mind? A maybe.
What do you call an alligator in a vest? An investigator.
Why was the computer cold? It left its windows open. I don't know what a computer is either.
Why did the chicken join a band? It had the drumsticks.
What's a ghast's favorite game? Hide and shriek.
What did the slime say to the other slime? "Let's stick together."
Why was the broom late? It over-swept.
What do you call a can opener that doesn't work? A can't opener.
Why are ghosts bad at lying? You can see right through them.
What's a mushroom's favorite party? A fungi gathering. Because they're fun guys.
Why did the boat go to the doctor? It was feeling a little dinghy.
What do you call a guard with a sword and no armor? Brave. And soon, sore.
Why did the shepherd's dog go to school? To get a little more paws-itive.
What do you call a lazy kangaroo? A pouch potato.
Why did the stew go to school? To get a little more seasoned.
Why do pigs make terrible secret keepers? They squeal.
What do you get if you cross a cow and a duck? Milk and quackers.
Why are skeletons so calm? Nothing gets under their skin.
Why did the trader leave his llamas at home? They kept spitting out his prices.
What's the difference between a guitar and a fish? You can't tuna fish.
What did the hat say to the scarf? You hang around, I'll go on ahead.
Why don't eggs go to parties? They might get beaten.
What do you call a fish wearing a crown? A king cod.
Why did the sun go to school? To get brighter.
What do you call a dog magician? A labracadabrador.
What did one candle say to the other? Want to go out tonight?
Why was the tavern so cold? Too many draughts.
What do you call a bear in the rain? A drizzly bear.
What do you call a sleeping pizza? A piZZZa.
Why did the honey bee go to the doctor? It had hives.
Why was the nitwit holding a bucket of water? He heard the trade was liquid.
Why did the bread go to the doctor? It felt crumby. No wait, that was the cookie.
How do bees get to school? On the school buzz.
What do lawyers wear to court? Lawsuits.
Why did the lamp go to the party? It wanted to lighten up.
What did one plate say to the other? Lunch is on me.
What do you call a cow with no legs? Ground beef.
Why did the goat get kicked out of the library? It kept butting in.
Why did the baker stop making donuts? She got tired of the hole business.
What do you call a sad strawberry? A blueberry.
Why did the golden apple go to school? To get enchanted with learning.
What do you call a bear without ears? B.
Why don't skeletons play music in church? They have no organs.
How does a penguin build its house? Igloos it together.
What do you call a pile of cats? A meowntain.
Why did the guardian go to art school? It wanted to draw a laser line.
Why are mountains so funny? They're hill-arious.
Why did the hoe get an award? It was outstanding in its field. Like the scarecrow.
What do you call a dancing sheep? A baaa-llerina.
What did the drowned say to the fisherman? "Water you looking at?"
Why did the pickaxe go to the party? To break the ice.
How do you catch a squirrel? Climb a tree and act like a nut.
What's the friendliest building in the village? The library. It has the most stories.
Why did the anvil apologize? It was a little heavy-handed.
joke.warmhearted: Why did the bread go to the party? Because it was well-bred! Oh, I love that one.
What did the cookie say to the milk? "I'm crumbling without you."
Why did the soup always win at cards? It had a good stock. Ha!
What's the kindest vegetable? A sweet potato, of course.
Why did the oven get a compliment? It was really warm-hearted. Like me!
Why did the honey love everyone? It couldn't help being sweet.
What did the pie say to the plate? "Let's get together and be crust friends."
Why did I bake so many rolls? Because I'm on a roll! Ho ho.
What do you call a hug from a bear? A warm welcome. Very fuzzy.
joke.thoughtful: If a tree falls in a forest and nobody hears it, does the iron golem still pick up the flower?
Why did the philosopher refuse the bread? He didn't want to be in-loaf-ed in any arguments. Hmm. Workshop it.
I told a joke about paper once. It was tearable.
What's the hardest thing about learning to read? Turning the page on your old habits.
I wrote a book about anti-gravity. I couldn't put it down.
Why are books so cozy? They're full of covers.
I tried to write a joke about time travel. You didn't like it.
A sentence walks into a tavern. It's long and full of clauses.
I've been reading a book about glue. I can't stop.
joke.playful: Knock knock! Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's raining!
Knock knock! Who's there? Cow says. Cow says who? No, cow says moo!
Knock knock! Who's there? Creeper. Creeper who? Hssssss. BOOM. Okay, that one's not funny.
Why did the frog take a taxi? He was too tired to hop. Ribbit!
I tried to catch fog this morning. I mist. Ha!
What do you call a nervous chicken? A chicken. All chickens are nervous.
Knock knock! Who's there? Boo. Boo who? Don't cry, it's just a joke!
I tickled a ghast once. Kidding! Imagine, though.
Why did I bring a ladder to the tavern? I heard the drinks were on the house!
joke.adventurous: Why did the explorer bring two pickaxes? In case he struck out with the first one.
What's an adventurer's favorite letter? The one that says "treasure map inside."
Why did the map refuse to fold? It wanted to see the world.
What do you call an adventurer who stays home? Me. Ha. Ha. Ha.
Why did the boat get lost? It didn't have a sense of porpoise.
What does a mountain say when it's proud? "I peaked."
Why do explorers carry torches? Because they're in the dark about everything else.
What did the compass say to the explorer? "I'm pointing you in the right direction, stop arguing."
Why don't explorers ever get bored? Every day's a new horizon.
joke.meticulous: Why did the organizer break up with the calendar? Its days were numbered. Precisely.
What's my favorite shape? A perfect square. Like this world.
I told a joke about a ruler once. It was measured and well received.
Why was the chest so neat? It had its stacks together.
What do you call a perfectly sorted inventory? A dream come true.
Why did the clock get a promotion? It was very punctual.
How many librarians does it take to sort a shelf? One. If they're me.
Why are labels so confident? They know exactly what they are.
I'd tell you a joke about the alphabet, but I'd have to start at the beginning.
joke.steadfast: Why did the gardener plant a bell? He wanted a ringing endorsement. Hrm. Good one.
What do you call a reliable vegetable? A steady-bean.
Why don't oak trees panic? They've got deep roots.
What's a farmer's favorite month? Hay.
Why was the old fence so wise? It had seen a lot of things come and go.
I tell the same joke every year. It's a perennial.
What did the seed say when it finally sprouted? "Took long enough."
Why do I never rush? Because the carrots don't either.
How do you keep a promise? Same as a garden. Water it every day.
joke.reserved: ...Why did the fish blush? It saw the ocean's bottom. ...Sorry.
...I know one joke. What's a fish with no eyes? A fsh.
...Why do seagulls fly over the sea? If they flew over the bay, they'd be bagels. ...Never mind.
...What lies at the bottom of the ocean and twitches? A nervous wreck.
...Why was the river rich? It had two banks.
...I'm not funny. But the heron is. You should see it walk.
...What did the pond say to the frog? Nothing. Ponds don't talk.
...Why don't fish play tennis? Afraid of the net. ...Heh.
...What's a fish's favorite instrument? The bass. ...I like that one.
joke.imaginative: Why did the painter go to jail? She was framed!
What did the yellow paint say to the blue paint? "Let's mix things up and go green."
Why was the artist always calm? She knew how to draw the line.
What's a cloud's favorite painting style? Water-color, naturally.
Why did the moon skip dinner? It was already full.
What do rainbows do when they're bored? They take a bow.
Why did the easel go to school? To be a little more upright.
How does a painter say goodbye? "Brush you later!"
Why was the sunset so dramatic? It wanted to make a scene.
joke.pragmatic: Why did the carpenter refuse the job? It was too boring. ...Get it? Boring.
What's a hammer's favorite story? One with a lot of nail-biting moments.
Why did the plank feel lonely? It was board.
Want to hear a construction joke? I'm still working on it.
Why do I only tell short jokes? Time's money.
What do you call a nail that won't go in? A failure. Bend it straight, try again.
Why did the axe get promoted? It made the cut.
Here's a practical joke: wear a helmet in caves. Not funny, but smart.
Why did the saw get bored? Same old cut, every day.
joke.curious: Why do bees buzz? Nobody knows! Isn't that funny? Isn't it? I need to find out.
What did the scientist say when he found two isotopes of helium? "HeHe."
Why can't you trust atoms? They make up everything!
How does the moon stay up? It has a lot of support from its fans. I don't actually know how. Do you?
What's a star's favorite question? "Why do I shine?"
Why did the owl go to school? It had too many questions. Like me!
What's the most curious animal? A cat. Curiosity... well. Never mind that part.
Why do cows have hooves instead of feet? Because they lactose. I'm not sure that's how it works.
Why does the sun rise? To see what we're up to.
joke.protective: Why did the guard bring a pillow on patrol? In case he had to cushion a blow.
What's a knight's favorite fish? A swordfish, naturally.
Why did the shield go to the party? To block out the bad vibes.
What did the wall say to the zombie? "You shall not pass."
Why did the golem never get scared? It had nerves of iron.
How does a guard sleep? With one eye open. Very uncomfortable.
Why do I check the locks twice? Because once is a guess and twice is a guarantee.
What's the safest building in the village? The one I just checked.
Why was the fence so popular? It always kept everyone together.
joke.gentle: Why did the flower ride a bicycle? Its pedals were tired.
What did the bee say to the flower? "Hello, honey."
Why are daisies so happy? They're always in a good bloom.
What do you call a flower that runs on electricity? A power plant. Hehe.
Why did the rose blush? It saw the garden hose.
What did the little sprout say? "Leaf me alone, I'm growing."
Why are sunflowers so cheerful? They always look on the bright side.
What do you give a sad tulip? A little bud-dy.
Why did the bunny plant flowers? It wanted a hare-raising garden.
joke.job.farmer: Why did the farmer win an award? He was outstanding in his field.
What did the farmer say when he lost his tractor? "Where's my tractor?" We don't have tractors. Still funny.
Why don't carrots ever lie? They always get to the root of things.
What do you call a farmer who tells jokes? A corn-edian.
joke.job.librarian: Why did the librarian slip? She was in the non-friction section.
Where do books sleep? Under their covers.
What's a librarian's favorite sport? Shush-ball.
Why was the library so tall? It had a lot of stories.
joke.job.fisherman: What do you call a fish that wears a bowtie? So-fish-ticated.
Why did the fisherman put peanut butter in the sea? To go with the jellyfish.
Which fish can perform surgery? A sturgeon.
What did the fisherman say to the magic trick? "Pick a cod, any cod."
joke.job.fletcher: Why did the arrow fall in love? It was struck by cupid.
What's a fletcher's favorite saying? "Feather together, flock together."
Why are arrows good at relationships? They always get to the point.
I'd tell an arrow joke, but you'd see it coming a mile away.
joke.job.cleric: Why did the potion go to church? It needed a little brew-tiful blessing.
What do you call a nervous brewing stand? Bubbly.
Why did I light so many candles? I wanted a holy-day.
What's a cleric's favorite dance? The redstone shuffle.
joke.job.cartographer: Why did the map go to school? It wanted to be well-read.
What did the cartographer say to the mountain? "You're looking great from this angle."
Why are maps great listeners? They know where you're coming from.
What do you call a lost cartographer? Ironic.
joke.job.armorer: Why was the chestplate so confident? It had nothing to hide behind except itself.
What did the helmet say to the head? "I've got you covered."
Why did the knight go to the armorer? He needed to get suited up.
What's an armorer's favorite game? Chain tag.
joke.job.toolsmith: Why did the pickaxe get promoted? It always hit rock bottom first.
What did the shovel say to the dirt? "I dig you."
Why are hammers great friends? They always nail it.
What's a toolsmith's favorite music? Heavy metal.
joke.job.weaponsmith: Why did the sword break up with the shield? It needed space to swing.
What did the grindstone say to the blade? "Stay sharp."
Why are axes great at parties? They break the ice.
What's a weaponsmith's least favorite word? Rust.
joke.job.leatherworker: Why did the cow go to the leatherworker? To get its hide back.
What did one boot say to the other? "Let's step out together."
Why are belts so reliable? They hold everything together.
What's a leatherworker's favorite song? "Hide and Seek."
joke.job.mason: Why are masons so good at relationships? They know how to build a solid foundation.
What did one brick say to the other? "Let's stick together."
Why did the stone go to school? To get a little more polished.
What's a mason's favorite dessert? Rocky road.
joke.job.shepherd: What do you call a sheep that's good at karate? A lamb-chop.
Why did the sheep get a ticket? It made a ewe-turn.
What's a shepherd's favorite bedtime story? Counting sheep, obviously.
Why are sheep so good at parties? They know how to get woolly wild.
joke.job.butcher: Why did the sausage go to school? To be a little more well-done.
What did the steak say to the smoker? "You're making me blush."
Why are butchers great at tennis? They have a great chop shot.
What did the ham say to the smoker? "Cure me of my troubles."
joke.job.nitwit: Why do I never work? Because work's a four-letter word. So is "nap," which I prefer.
What's my favorite exercise? Lying down and then standing up. Occasionally.
Why did I go to the library? I heard they had a lot of shelves to lean on.
What do you call a nap after a nap? A good day.
joke.job.none: Why am I always looking for a job? I'm a professional job-hunter. Ha. Sort of.
What did the unemployed villager say to the workstation? "Is this seat taken?"
Why don't I have a job? The job didn't have me first.
What's my job? Telling jokes about not having a job.
joke.job.knight: Why did the knight take so long to get dressed? He had a lot of armor to put on.
What's a knight's favorite fish? A swordfish. I've said that before. It's still good.
Why did the training dummy get promoted? It always took a hit for the team.
What did the dummy say to the knight? "Is that all you've got?" Then I hit it harder.
joke.job.archer: Why did the archer break up with the bow? It was too high-strung.
What's an archer's favorite month? Arch. Arch-uary.
Why are targets so patient? They're used to people missing them.
How do archers say hello? "Arrow there!"
joke.job.cook: Why did the tomato turn red? It saw the salad dressing. A classic in the kitchen.
What do you call a cook who's always calm? Unflappable. Like a pancake that's done right.
Why did the stew win the contest? It was a hearty competitor.
What's a cook's favorite exercise? Whisking.
joke.job.tavern_keeper: Why did the cider barrel go to therapy? It was feeling a little empty.
What do you call a tavern with no customers? A bar-gain.
Why are mugs so friendly? They're always up for a cup.
What did the coffee say to the tavern keeper? "You mean a latte to me."
joke.job.apothecary: Why did the herb go to the apothecary? It was feeling a bit thyme-worn.
What do you call a nervous tonic? A bit shaken.
Why did the mint win the argument? It was very cool about it.
What's an apothecary's favorite flower? Mari-gold. Expensive and soothing.
joke.job.painter: Why was the paint so tired? It had too many coats.
What did the canvas say to the brush? "Stroke of luck you came along."
Why do painters make great friends? They always help you see the bigger picture.
What's a painter's favorite cake? Marble, obviously.
joke.job.bard: Why did the bard sit on the ladder? To reach the high notes.
What do you call a musician with problems? A trebled artist.
Why are lutes so friendly? They're always in a good tune.
What's a bard's favorite vegetable? Beets. Get it? Beats.
joke.job.tailor: Why did the tailor get an award? She was sew good at her job.
What did the needle say to the thread? "Let's get to the point."
Why are buttons so dependable? They always hold things together.
What's a tailor's favorite movie? Pants-ing Through Time.
joke.job.carpenter: Why did the carpenter refuse to work? It was too boring.
What did the saw say to the log? "I've got a bone to pick with you." Wait, wrong job.
Why are carpenters great at parties? They know how to raise the roof.
What's a carpenter's favorite game? Plank-ball.
joke.job.scholar: Why did the scholar bring a ladder to class? To reach higher education.
What do you call an old history book? A blast from the past.
Why are historians great at parties? They know how to make an old story new.
I'd tell you a history joke, but it's in the past.
joke.weather: What did the cloud say to the rain? "You're dripping with talent."
Why did the snowman call his dog Frost? Because frost bites.
What's a tornado's favorite game? Twister.
Why did the sun go to school? To get brighter. I tell that one every sunny day.
What did one raindrop say to the other? "Two's company, three's a cloud."
Why don't storms ever win arguments? They always end up blowing over.
What does a cloud wear under its raincoat? Thunderwear.
How do snowmen get around? They ride an icicle.
What's the weather like for a skeleton? Bone dry.
Why did the lightning bolt get grounded? It was acting out.
held.sword: Careful with that sword! Point it somewhere that isn't me.
