That's a fine blade. Use it to protect, not to bully.
You can put the sword away, {player}. Nobody here's going to bite you.
Is that {item}? Looks like it's seen a few fights.
Swords make me nervous. Even friendly ones.
A sword like that could keep a whole village safe. Keep it sharp.
Mind your swing near the chickens, please.
Our knights would admire a blade like that.
held.axe: Chopping trees? Leave a few for the birds.
An axe! The carpenter would love to borrow that.
That's a sharp-looking axe. Careful near my fence.
Plant a sapling for every tree you cut. That's the rule round here.
You look like you've been cutting wood all day. Smell of sap and everything.
Axes make good shields-breakers, I hear. Not that I'd know.
Going lumberjacking? The birch grove's to the north.
held.pickaxe: Off to the mines? Watch out for lava.
A pickaxe! Find any diamonds lately?
Is that {item}? Looks like it's been chewing through stone.
Never dig straight down. My grandfather's rule.
You've got stone dust all over you. Been mining?
Bring a torch for every pickaxe swing. Caves are dark.
If you find iron, the smiths will buy it.
Miners always come back with the best stories. And the worst dust.
held.shovel: Digging something up? Or burying something? I won't ask.
A shovel! Want to help with my garden?
Gravel, sand, dirt. The shovel's for the honest work.
Careful you don't dig up the path again.
Is that for making paths? The village could use a few more.
I once dug a hole so deep I had to call for help.
Shovels are underrated. Everyone loves a pickaxe, nobody thanks the shovel.
held.hoe: A hoe! Are you a farmer now too?
Come help with the harvest, if you're handy with that.
Till the dirt near water and it'll stay farmland.
Nice hoe. The farmer would approve.
Planting something? Carrots grow fast here.
Don't swing that near my flowers, please.
Farming's honest work. Glad to see you trying it.
held.bow: A bow! Our archers would like a look at that.
Careful with that string. It bites.
Is that {item}? Looks well cared for.
Shoot the archery target sometime. It'll tell you your score.
Bows are quiet. That's why the archers love them.
Mind you don't shoot the chickens. Or me.
held.trident: A trident! Did you take that from a drowned? Brave.
That's a strange weapon. It looks like it wants to swim.
Throw that in the rain and they say lightning follows. Don't, please.
Ooh, is that from the ocean? It smells of salt.
I've never seen one up close. Can I... no. I won't touch it.
A trident's a sailor's weapon. Are you a sailor now?
held.shield: A shield! Smart. Shields save lives.
That's a sturdy shield. Did the armorer make it?
Crouch behind that when the skeletons start shooting.
I like a person who carries a shield. Shows sense.
Is that your banner on the front? Very fancy.
Our knights swear by shields. So should you.
held.fishing_rod: Going fishing? The river's best in the morning.
A fishing rod! The fisherman would want to compare notes.
Catch me a salmon while you're at it?
Patience, a good rod and a quiet spot. That's all you need.
If you catch a boot, keep it. You never know.
The fish bite better in the rain, they say.
Fishing's my favorite way to waste an afternoon.
held.map: Is that a map? Can I see? Where have you been?
Maps are wonderful. Every corner a promise.
The cartographer would love to see your map.
Show me where {village} is on that. Is it there? We're famous!
That map's well worn. You've been places.
If you get lost, follow the river downhill. Rivers always find people.
Are you marking us on your map? Put a little bell where the village is.
held.compass: A compass! Which way's north? I always forget.
Does your compass point home, or somewhere else?
Clever little thing, a compass. Never lies.
I'd get lost in my own garden without one of those.
Is that a clock? Or a compass? I can never tell them apart from here.
Keep that close on your travels. It'll bring you back.
held.book: A book! What are you reading?
Ooh, is that enchanted? It's glowing a little.
The librarian would want to borrow that.
Books are the best company. Except you, of course.
What's the story about? Tell me without spoiling the ending.
Is that a journal? Do you write about us?
Reading's my favorite way to travel without moving.
Bring that to the archives if you want a copy of the village chronicle.
held.flower: Oh, a flower! Is that for me? No? Still lovely.
That's a pretty flower. Did you pick it in the meadow?
Flowers make everything better. Even swords. Maybe not swords.
A flower in hand is worth two in the garden. Or something like that.
The golem likes flowers. Did you know? It gives them to the children.
That color's beautiful. You could make a lovely dye from it.
held.emerald: That's a nice shiny emerald. Spend it wisely.
Emeralds make the village go round.
Careful flashing emeralds around. Not everyone's as honest as us.
Oh, I could do a lot with one of those. A new hat, for a start.
Are you rich, {player}? You look rich today.
The wandering trader's prices would make your emeralds weep.
held.diamond: Is that a diamond? A real one? Goodness!
Diamonds! Where did you find that?
Put that away before someone faints.
A diamond like that could buy half the village. Well, not the bell.
I've only seen a diamond once before. It was in a sword.
Make something strong with that. A pickaxe, maybe.
held.gold: Gold! The piglins would love you.
Gold's pretty, but it's soft. Don't make tools with it.
Is that real gold? It's so bright.
A golden apple needs a lot of gold. Just saying.
Gold armor looks lovely and breaks in a breeze.
Careful, the wandering trader's eyes just lit up.
held.torch: Good thinking, carrying a torch. Monsters hate the light.
A torch! The path's dark after sunset. Put one by the well?
Mind you don't set the hay on fire.
Light the way, {player}. Somebody has to.
Torches keep the zombies away. Mostly.
The more torches, the safer the village. That's my motto.
held.bucket: A bucket? Fetching water? The well's that way.
Is that lava? Please tell me that's not lava.
Milk! Is that milk? Fresh milk cures all sorts of nasty potions.
Water bucket! Very useful if you fall from somewhere high.
Careful not to spill that on my doorstep.
Buckets are the unsung heroes of the village.
held.crops: Seeds! Planting something? The farmer would be thrilled.
Carrots, potatoes, wheat. The good stuff.
Are you helping with the harvest? Bless you.
That's a lot of crops. Making bread? Stew? Both?
Plant them near water and they'll grow fast.
A sapling! Plant it somewhere it can grow tall.
You smell like a field. A nice field.
held.egg: An egg! Are you going to throw it? Please don't throw it.
Throw an egg and sometimes a chicken pops out. Strange, but true.
Eggs for cake! Do you bake?
Is that a turtle egg? Put it back on the beach!
Chickens lay eggs everywhere here. You're welcome to them.
held.totem: Is that a totem of undying? Hold onto that. Literally.
That totem looks ancient. Where did you get it?
They say a totem can cheat death once. Don't test it.
Evokers carry those. You fought an evoker? Goodness.
A totem! You must have been somewhere dangerous.
held.elytra: Wings! You can fly with those? Truly?
Is that an elytra? From the End cities? I've only read about them!
Fireworks and wings. What a way to travel.
Don't crash into the bell tower, please.
I'd be terrified to fly. And also thrilled.
held.tnt: Is that TNT? Put it down. Gently. Very gently.
Please don't light that near my house.
Explosives in the village? The golem won't like that.
I hope that's for mining. Far away from here.
That makes me more nervous than a creeper.
TNT and flint? You're a walking disaster, {player}.
held.potion: A potion! What does it do? Does it glow?
The cleric would want to know what's in that bottle.
Be careful what you drink, {player}. Not everything bubbling is friendly.
Is that a healing potion? Smart to carry one.
That color's interesting. Smells like nether wart.
Potions make me nervous. Last one I drank turned me invisible for a day.
held.treat: Is that cake? Are you sharing? You should be sharing.
A treat for me? No? A treat for you, then. Fair.
Sweet berries are lovely. Prickly to pick, though.
held.food: Hungry? You should eat that before it gets cold.
That smells delicious. Did you cook it?
Food's for sharing, they say. I'm just saying they say it.
Eat up! Adventurers need their strength.
Is that bread? Good bread? Let me see.
You've got a good meal there. The cook would approve.
Bring some of that to the tavern and you'll make friends fast.
held.raw_food: That's raw! You'll want to cook that first.
The cook's stove would have that sizzling in no time.
Raw meat? Smoker, furnace or campfire. Not your mouth.
That'll cook twice as fast on our kitchen stove.
Fresh catch? Or fresh from the field? Either way, cook it.
Don't eat that raw. I'm begging you.
held.music: The bard would love to hear you play.
Is that a lute? Play the music stand with it and listen to the sound.
A bell! Don't ring it, it'll start a panic.
Music makes the village feel alive.
held.pet: A name tag! Are you naming someone?
A lead? Do you have a pet? Is it a llama?
I'd name a pet something grand. Lord Fluffington.
Saddles are for horses, pigs and the very brave.
Tame a wolf and you'll never walk alone.
Every pet deserves a good name.
held.wool: Wool! The tailor could make something lovely from that.
Shears? Shearing sheep? Be gentle with them.
That wool's soft. Is it from our flock?
You could make a bed from that. Or a banner.
Bring wool to the sewing table and it'll unravel into string.
Colored wool brightens up any house.
held.wood: Logs! Bring them to the sawmill for extra planks.
Building something? I love building things.
The carpenter would get you six planks a log.
Is that oak? Or birch? I can never tell when it's not on a tree.
held.ore: Iron! The smiths will be glad to see that.
Raw ore? Smelt it before you trade it.
Copper's pretty when it's new. Goes green when it's old. Like me.
Bring that to the blast furnace. Twice as fast.
held.paint: A paintbrush! Are you an artist?
Dyes! You could finish the painting on the easel with those.
Colors in your hands. I like that.
Blue dye makes the sea, red makes flowers. On our easel, anyway.
Are you planning to paint the village? Paint my door blue.
player.hurt: You're hurt! Sit down a moment. Let me look at you.
Goodness, you're bleeding! Have you got any bandages?
You look like you lost a fight with a skeleton. Did you?
Rest before you go anywhere. Please.
The apothecary can patch you up. Or eat something. Food helps.
I don't like seeing you hurt, {player}.
Bandages, potions, a warm bed. You need all three.
player.hungry: You look hungry. When did you last eat?
Your stomach's growling louder than the bell.
Get something to eat, {player}. You can't adventure on an empty belly.
The cook's stove has a dish of the day, if they've been working.
Have some bread. You look peaky.
Hungry adventurers make mistakes. Eat something.
I can hear your stomach from here.
You need a good meal. The tavern does a lovely stew.
player.wet: You're soaked to the bone! Come out of the rain.
Look at you, dripping on my doorstep.
Did you swim here? You look like you swam here.
Stand by a fire and dry off before you catch a cold.
Your boots are squelching. I can hear them.
Rain got you, did it? It gets everyone eventually.
A hooded poncho would keep that off. The tailor makes lovely ones.
You smell like wet wool. No offense.
player.fire: You're on fire! Water! Somebody get water!
Stop, drop and roll! Or jump in the well!
Why are you smoking? Literally smoking!
Fire! You're on fire! Why are you so calm?!
Please don't stand near the hay.
Did you fall in lava? Get to water, quick!
player.riding: Look at you up there! What a fine steed.
Mind your animal doesn't eat my flowers.
Riding into the village like a hero. Very dramatic.
Is that comfortable? It looks comfortable.
Don't let it trample the crops, please.
player.pumpkin: Why are you wearing a pumpkin on your head?
Is that a pumpkin? Are you hiding from the endermen?
You look like a scarecrow with ambitions.
I can't tell if you're smiling under there.
The endermen won't stare at you, at least. Very sensible. Very silly.
Nice hat. Very orange. Very round.
Can you even see out of that thing?
You smell like pie, {player}. Is it the pumpkin?
player.elytra: You've got wings! Where did you get wings?
Is that an elytra on your back? Can you really fly?
Fly over the bell tower! Please! I want to see!
Wings and all. You really are an adventurer.
I've only read about elytras. Is it as wonderful as it sounds?
You must have been to the End. Nobody comes back with wings otherwise.
player.diamond: Look at that armor! You sparkle like a geode.
Diamond armor! You must be very brave. Or very rich.
I can see my reflection in your chestplate.
You look like a hero from a story.
That armor must have cost a fortune.
Nobody's going to mess with you in that.
Shiny! You'll scare the zombies just by glinting at them.
Is that netherite? It's so dark. Very serious-looking.
player.golden: Golden armor! Very fancy. Very soft.
You look like a king. Or a very confident piglin.
That gold's going to dent if you sneeze.
The piglins would love you right now.
Golden armor? Going to a party?
player.leather: Leather armor? Simple and sturdy. Good choice for a start.
You look like a proper traveler in that leather.
Leather's light. Easy to run in. Smart.
Did you dye that? It's a lovely color.
You've got the look of a hunter.
player.unarmored: No armor? Out in the wilds? You're braver than I am.
Where's your armor, {player}? The skeletons won't be gentle.
You should get some armor. The armorer can help.
Out and about with no armor. Bold.
Even a leather cap would help, you know.
I worry when I see you without armor.
player.dark: It's dark out. You should be inside, or at least near a torch.
Walking around at night? Stay near the lamps.
The night's full of things you don't want to meet.
Don't stay out too long, {player}. The zombies are about.
It's black as pitch out there. Mind your step.
Have you got a torch? You should have a torch.
Night walks are lovely until something groans at you.
The golem's on patrol, but you should still be careful.
remember.likes_rain: You told me you love the rain. I thought of you all through the last storm.
Rain-lover! I saved a puddle for you. It's by the well.
I walked in the rain yesterday because you said you liked it. You're right. It's lovely.
remember.fond_village: You said {village} was your favorite. I've been telling everyone. You're famous now.
I keep remembering what you said about {village}. It made us all a bit prouder.
You love it here. I can tell. And we love having you.
remember.trait_generous: You said you'd share your last loaf. I believe it. You've got a generous heart.
I told {neighbor} how generous you are. They didn't seem surprised.
Generous people like you make the world softer. Thank you.
remember.likes_fishing: You like fishing, don't you? The salmon are running this week.
I found a good spot by the river and thought of you. Bring your rod.
Fancy a fishing trip soon? You said you liked it. I haven't forgotten.
remember.likes_cats: You're a cat person! There's a new kitten by the bakery. You'd love her.
The village cats have been asking about you. Well, one meowed at me. Same thing.
I saw a cat sleeping on a pumpkin and thought of you.
remember.fond_bell: You said the bell was the best. I gave it a little polish in your honor.
Every time the bell rings now, I think of what you said.
The bell rang at noon and I said "that one's for {player}." The cleric gave me a look.
remember.drink_coffee: Strong coffee, you said! The tap's full this morning, if you've got a mug.
I tried my coffee strong like you. My hands haven't stopped shaking.
You're the coffee one! I remember. The tavern keeper does a lovely mug.
remember.drink_cider: Warm cider, wasn't it? The barrel's been freshly pressed.
You like cider. I'll save you a mug at the tavern.
The apples this year are perfect for your cider.
remember.drink_milk: Cold milk in the morning! You were right. I tried it. Very refreshing.
Milk-drinker! The cows have been very productive this week.
remember.dream_cottage: You dreamed of a cozy cottage. I saw a perfect spot by the stream. Just saying.
Still dreaming of that little cottage? Build it near us, would you?
I keep thinking about your cottage dream. It sounds like the nicest dream.
remember.dream_castle: How's your castle in the clouds coming along? I want a tower room.
You wanted to build a castle! Have you started? Do you need a bell for it?
remember.dream_farm: A giant farm, you said! The farmer's got opinions on how you should start.
You and your giant farm. You'd feed the whole Overworld.
remember.dream_redstone: Have you built your redstone machine yet? What does it do? Never mind, I'll just be impressed.
You and redstone! I still don't understand it. I still think it's wonderful.
remember.writes_journal: Did you write about today in your journal? Write something nice about me.
I've started a journal too, because of you. Mostly I draw cats in it.
Your journal must be enormous by now.
remember.why_see: You want to see everything. Have you seen something new since we last talked?
Still seeing the world? Tell me the best new thing.
remember.why_people: You said you travel for the people you meet. I hope I'm one of the good ones.
You travel for people. I keep thinking about that. It's the nicest reason.
I told {neighbor} why you travel. They said "for people? That's lovely." It is.
remember.why_build: You said you want to build something great. I hope you'll show us when it's done.
How's the great building project? Bigger than the church yet?
remember.wants_swim: You'd rather breathe underwater. I saw a turtle today and thought of you.
Still wishing you could swim like a fish? There's a potion for that, I've heard.
remember.wants_fly: You wanted to fly! Have you found wings yet? Elytra, they call them.
I watched the birds today and thought of you. You'd love it up there.
remember.wants_animals: You'd talk to animals if you could. The goat has been very chatty lately. Try him.
I'm sure the cats would tell you everything. You'd hear so much gossip.
remember.travels_wolf: How's your wolf? You said you travel with one. Give it a scratch from me.
Bring your wolf by sometime! The village dogs would love a new friend.
remember.travels_friends: Still traveling with friends? Bring them here sometime.
Adventures with friends are the best kind. You told me that.
remember.travels_alone: You said you travel alone. Take care of yourself out there. Someone here worries.
Lonely roads are long. Come back to us often.
remember.trait_trusty: You said you'd never tell a secret. So here's one: I'm glad we're friends.
I trust you. You keep secrets. That's rare.
remember.trait_tidy: You sort your chests by type! I still think about that. Wonderful.
Your chests must be the tidiest in the Overworld.
remember.trait_miner: You're a miner at heart. The old mineshaft east of here might interest you.
remember.trait_honest: You'd ask around about a lost emerald. That's why I trust you.
Honest folk are rare. You're one of them.
remember.trait_healer: You said you'd cure a zombie neighbor. That stays with me. Thank you.
I feel safer knowing you'd try to cure one of us. You know how. Weakness and gold.
remember.trait_farmer: How are your crops coming along, farmer?
A farmer at heart! The wheat's high this year. You'd be proud.
remember.trait_explorer: Where's the explorer been this time? Tell me everything.
You're always off somewhere new. Explorer through and through.
remember.trait_careful: You said you're careful. Good. Stay that way out there.
remember.trait_builder: How's the building going, builder? Need any planks? The sawmill's busy.
You're a builder. The carpenter's been asking about you.
remember.trait_brave: Brave as ever, I see. Just don't be too brave.
You told me you're brave. I believe it now. I've seen your armor dents.
remember.talent_cooking: You can cook! When are you cooking for me? I'm waiting.
I still want to taste your cooking. Bring something next time.
remember.song_jig: The bard's been working on your jig. It's very bouncy. You'll love it.
Your jig is nearly ready! The bard's been humming it all week.
remember.song_ballad: Your ballad's up to forty verses. The bard can't stop.
The bard sang a bit of your ballad at the tavern. Everyone cried. In a good way.
remember.sleeps_stars: Still sleeping under the stars? Watch for spiders.
I slept outside last night because you made it sound nice. A spider walked on my face.
remember.sleeps_bed: Still carrying your bed around? Very wise. Very heavy, I'd imagine.
A bed in your pack. I still think that's clever.
remember.season_winter: Winter's your season! I'll save you a spot by the fire when the snow comes.
You love winter. The first frost made me think of you.
remember.season_summer: Summer's your favorite! The river's warm enough to swim in now.
You love summer. Long days, warm nights. Enjoy them.
remember.season_spring: Spring's your time. The blossoms are coming out by the church.
You love spring. Everything new. Like you, every time you visit.
remember.season_autumn: Autumn, you said! The pumpkins are coming in nicely.
You love the harvest. You'd love our harvest festival. If we had one. We should.
remember.promise_garden: You said you'd plant something with me. I've saved the seeds. Whenever you're ready.
Our garden plan! I've marked out a little spot. It's waiting for us.
remember.promise_defend: You said you'd help if trouble came. I've told the guards. They're glad.
I sleep better knowing you'd come if the bell rang.
remember.promise_adventure: You said you'd take me on an adventure someday. I've packed. Twice.
Is today the day? For our adventure? No? Tomorrow, then.
I've been training for our adventure. I walked to the river and back. Twice.
remember.plays_tag: You played tag with me! You're it! Still! Forever!
Will you play again? You promised! Sort of!
remember.plays_snowball: I've been saving snowballs for our fight. Well, they melted. I'll make more.
Snowball rematch when the snow comes back! You're not getting away.
remember.plays_nap: The haystack's ready for our nap. Same time as usual?
Napping together was the best idea you've ever agreed to.
remember.pet_sir: How's Sir Barks-a-Lot? Have you found him yet? I keep imagining him.
If you ever get a wolf, I'm holding you to the name Sir Barks-a-Lot.
remember.pet_biscuit: Did you name a wolf Biscuit yet? I need to know.
Biscuit! I still think that's the cutest name ever.
remember.number_64: Sixty-four! A full stack. I see your lucky number everywhere now.
I counted sixty-four seeds today and thought of you.
remember.loves_ocean: You love the ocean. I hope you get to see it again soon.
I painted the sea after you told me about it. It's very blue. Mostly blue.
remember.loves_mountains: The snowy mountains, you said. I looked at the hills and imagined them taller.
Have you been back to the mountains? Tell me about the snow up there.
remember.loves_cherry: The cherry groves! I dreamt about them after you told me. Everything pink.
You love the cherry groves. I'd love to see one with you someday.
remember.likes_sweet: Something sweet for the sweet-tooth! The baker's got honey cakes today.
You're the cake person. I'll let you know when there's cake. There's always cake somewhere.
remember.likes_sunset: The sunset last night made me think of you. All orange and gold.
You're a sunset person. There's a good one coming tonight, I can feel it.
remember.likes_sunrise: I watched the sunrise this morning because you said you love them. You're right.
Sunrise person! You'd have loved this morning's. Pink everywhere.
remember.likes_sun: A fine sunny day, just how you like it.
Sunshine for the sunshine person! Enjoy it.
remember.likes_snow: You love snow! I'll make a snow golem for you when it comes.
I thought of you when the first flakes fell. You'd have been out in it.
remember.likes_savory: The stew-lover! The cook's made a big pot today.
You'd rather have stew than cake. I'll never understand it. I respect it.
remember.likes_parrots: Seen any parrots lately? I still want one that says my name.
You and your parrots! The jungle traders have one, I think.
remember.likes_music: You love a good jig. The bard's playing tonight. Come by.
The bard asked if the jig-lover was in town. That's you!
remember.likes_dogs: A dog person! The village dogs have been extra waggy since you visited.
I saw a puppy today and thought of you.
remember.likes_bread: The bread-lover! The bakery smells amazing this morning.
Bread, just bread. You were right. I had some plain bread today. Perfect.
remember.idea_wall: I told the guards your idea about the wall. They're considering it. Slowly.
Your wall idea came up at the meeting. Very heated debate.
remember.idea_tavern: Your bigger tavern idea is very popular. The bard's started a petition.
Everyone agrees with you about the tavern. The tavern keeper agrees the loudest.
remember.idea_snow: A first snow festival! I keep thinking about your idea. Lanterns in the snow.
Your snow festival idea! We'll do it this winter. I've decided.
remember.idea_lanterns: I mentioned your lantern idea. A few more lanterns went up by the well. Your doing.
More lanterns, you said. The path by the church has two new ones now.
remember.idea_harvest: A harvest festival! I've started planning. Pies. So many pies.
Your harvest festival idea has everyone excited. The farmer most of all.
remember.idea_golem: A festival for the golem! I gave it a poppy and told it your idea. It seemed pleased.
The golem doesn't know about its festival yet. Let's keep it a surprise.
remember.hours_late: Night owl! Make sure you sleep sometimes. The phantoms are watching.
Up late again? I could tell. You've got that night-owl glow.
remember.hours_early: An early riser like you would love the morning mist we had today.
Up with the sun, as always? Good for you.
remember.home_wanderer: Still wandering? You've always got a bed in {village}, you know.
Every wanderer needs somewhere to come back to. Let it be here.
remember.home_village: You said {village} was your home. I haven't stopped smiling about it.
Welcome home, {player}. You said it was home, so I'm saying it.
remember.home_built: How's the house you built? Any new rooms?
You built your own home. I'd love to see it someday. Or a painting of it.
remember.food_steak: The butcher's got good steak today. I thought of you.
A steak person! Well cooked, you said. I remember.
remember.food_pie: The baker made pumpkin pie this morning. I asked her to save a slice for you.
Pumpkin pie for the pie lover. It's in season.
remember.food_carrots: Golden carrots! Fancy as ever, I'm sure.
I saw a golden carrot at the market and thought, that's {player}'s favorite.
remember.fears_warden: You faced the warden. I still can't believe it. Brave, brave {player}.
I told the children you met the warden. They hid under the table for an hour.
remember.fears_endermen: Don't look any endermen in the eye this week, all right?
I wear a pumpkin in the garden now, because of what you said about endermen.
remember.fears_creepers: Seen any creepers lately? Watch your back, they're sneaky.
I got a cat because of your creeper stories. She's fierce.
remember.enchant_unbreaking: Hard to break, you said. That's you, I think.
Unbreaking. I keep thinking about your answer. It suits you.
remember.enchant_mending: Mending, you said. Healing as you grow. I think about that a lot.
Learning and mending. That's the best kind of life.
remember.color_red: Red, your favorite color! The poppies are blooming.
I painted my door red because of you. Well, partly because of you.
remember.color_purple: Purple! I found an amethyst shard and kept it for you.
Your favorite color's all over the sky at dusk tonight.
remember.color_green: Green, your color. The hills are so green this week.
Green, like the hills. And like creepers, unfortunately.
remember.color_blue: The sky's your color today. Lovely and blue.
I used so much blue in my last painting. For you.
remember.collects_gems: How's your gem collection? Anything new and sparkly?
I found a shiny pebble for your collection. It's not a gem. It's very shiny though.
remember.collects_friends: You collect friends, you said. I'm proud to be one.
How many friends in your collection now? I hope I'm near the top.
remember.collects_flowers: I pressed a flower for your collection. A cornflower. Very blue.
How's your flower collection? I saw a rare one by the river.
remember.collects_discs: Found any new music discs? I've never heard one play.
Your music disc collection must be wonderful.
remember.chronicle_yes: You're in the chronicle now! Right after the bit about the goat on the roof.
I've written about your last visit. It's a very flattering entry.
remember.cared_fed: Have you been eating properly since we talked? Truly?
I've got food for you again. I haven't forgotten my promise.
remember.birthday_today: Happy belated birthday! I've been thinking about it since you told me.
Birthday person! Did you do anything special? You should have.
remember.birthday_market: It's nearly your birthday! Market Day, remember? We agreed!
Every Market Day's your birthday now. That's the rule.
greet.routine.sleep: Mm? Oh, hello. I was just about to turn in.
Hello. It's my bedtime, but I can spare a minute.
Yawn... sorry. Hello! I should really be asleep.
Oh, you caught me in my nightcap. Hello.
Hello. Keep it short, my pillow's calling my name.
Hello! I'm officially off duty. Unofficially, I'm still nosy.
greet.routine.nap: Wha? Oh! I wasn't napping. Hello.
Hello... I was resting my eyes. Both of them. Very thoroughly.
Mm. Five more minutes. Oh, it's you. Hello!
Hello! You woke me from a very important nap.
Shh. I'm napping. Officially. But hello.
Hello. My afternoon nap is sacred, but you're allowed.
greet.routine.wake: Mmh. Morning. I'm still finding my feet.
Hello! I just got up. My hair's still deciding which way to go.
Oh, hello. Give me a moment, my eyes are only half open.
Good morning! I'm awake. Mostly. In theory.
Hello! I just washed my face in the cold water bucket. I'm VERY awake now.
Morning. Don't mind the yawning; it's not you, it's the hour.
greet.routine.breakfast: Hello! You caught me mid-breakfast. Want a crust?
Morning! I'm just finishing my porridge.
Hello! Breakfast first, then the world. Sit down.
Ah, hello. Mind the crumbs, I'm a messy eater before noon.
Hello! The eggs were good today. The chickens outdid themselves.
Hello! I always say nothing good happens before breakfast. Then you showed up.
greet.routine.prayer: Peace be with you. I was just finishing my morning prayers.
Hello, friend. The quiet hours are the best for reflection.
Ah, hello. I asked for a good day. Maybe you're the answer.
Hello. Forgive the incense smell; it gets in everything.
Good morning. I lit a candle for everyone in {village} today.
Hello. My prayers are said, my mind is clear. How can I help?
greet.routine.work: Hello! I'm at work, but I can talk while I do this.
Oh, hello! Don't mind me, my hands are busy but my ears are free.
Hello! Busy, busy. What can I do for you?
Ah, a visitor at the workstation. Hello!
Hello! You've caught me in the middle of something. That's always the way.
Hello, {player}. Mind your elbows, there are sharp things about.
Hello! It's a working day, but a chat never hurt anyone.
Hello! My workstation and I were just having a disagreement.
greet.routine.lunch: Hello! Lunchtime! Sit down, I'll share.
Ah, hello! I'm on my lunch break. Best part of the day.
Hello! The bell rang for lunch and I ran.
Hello, {player}! Want a bite? It's only a little squashed.
Hello! Everybody comes out to the bell at lunch. It's like a small festival every day.
Hello! I'm eating, so if I talk with my mouth full, forgive me.
greet.routine.lunch_home: Hello! I popped home for lunch. Nobody steals my soup here.
Oh, hello. I'm having lunch at home today. Quiet's nice sometimes.
Hello! Back home for a bite. Come in, come in.
Hello! My own kitchen, my own chair, my own sandwich. Bliss.
Hello! I always eat better at home. Fewer people asking for some.
Hello! I came home to eat and accidentally started cleaning.
greet.routine.lunch_tavern: Hello! I'm lunching at the tavern. The stew's good today.
Oh, hello! Pull up a chair. The tavern's busy but there's room.
Hello! I treat myself to a tavern lunch now and then.
Hello! You can smell the tavern kitchen from here, can't you?
Hello! Tavern lunch, best lunch. Don't tell my mother.
Ah, hello. Mind the bench, it wobbles.
greet.routine.hobby: Hello! It's my free time, so I'm doing what I love: {hobby}.
Oh, hello! You caught me enjoying a little {hobby}.
Hello! Work's done and now it's time for {hobby}.
Hello, {player}! This is my favorite part of the day.
Hello! I lose track of time completely when I'm {hobby}.
Hello! Don't mind the mess; hobbies are supposed to be messy.
greet.routine.social: Hello! Come join us, we're catching up by the bell.
Hello! This is when the whole village comes out to chat.
Oh, hello! You've arrived at the best hour for gossip.
Hello! The bell's the heart of {village}, and this is its busiest beat.
Hello! I just heard the most interesting thing. I'll tell you if you're nice.
greet.routine.market: Hello! The market's in full swing. Have you seen the stalls?
Happy Market Day! I'm out browsing.
Hello! I'm only here for the honey cakes. And the people. Mostly the cakes.
Hello! Market Day! The busiest, happiest day of the week.
Hello! Everyone's selling something, and I'm buying everything.
Hello! I've been haggling all morning. I lost.
greet.routine.supper: Hello! Supper's on the table. Join us?
Ah, hello. It's suppertime. Smell that?
Hello! I'm just sitting down to eat. You're welcome to the bread.
Hello! Supper's the best meal. It means the day's work is done.
Hello! Come in, there's enough stew for one more.
Oh, hello! I was just washing up the bowls.
greet.routine.evening: Hello! Just relaxing at home. Come in a moment.
Ah, hello. My feet are up and my day is done.
Hello! A quiet evening at home is the finest thing.
Hello, {player}. I was just reading by the lamp.
Hello! Evenings are for slippers and slow talks.
Oh, hello! I wasn't expecting company, but I'm glad of it.
greet.routine.tavern: Hello! Come in, come in, the tavern's warm and loud tonight.
Hello! Pull up a stool, {player}! The cider's good.
Ah, hello! Evening at the tavern. Best part of the week.
Hello! Shh, the bard's about to start. Or he's tuning. Hard to tell.
Hello! You'll want to try the cider here, it's pressed fresh.
Hello! Everyone in {village} ends up at the tavern eventually.
greet.routine.perform: Hello! I'm about to go on. Wish me luck!
Ah, an audience member! Hello! Any requests?
Hello! I'm warming up my fingers. And my nerves.
Hello! Tonight's the night. Every night's the night, really.
Hello! Sit close to the front. I sing better when I can see faces.
Hello! Don't clap yet, I haven't played anything.
greet.routine.night_watch: Hello. I'm on watch, so I'll keep my eyes on the dark while we talk.
Evening, {player}. All quiet so far. Let's keep it that way.
Hello. You're out late. Stay close to the torches.
Hello. Night watch. Long hours, cold hands, good stars.
Hello. Heard any groaning out by the fields? No? Good.
greet.routine.defend: Not now! They're coming. Stay close to the bell.
Hello, quickly! Have you got a weapon? We could use it.
Eyes on the treeline, {player}. They'll come from there.
Stand with us or get indoors. Either way, be quick!
Hold steady. We've got this village covered.
greet.routine.play: Hi! We're playing! Want to play?
Hello! I'm hiding! Don't tell anyone where I am.
Hi hi hi! I'm being a dragon! Rawr!
Hello! I've been playing since forever!
Hi! We're having a race! Are you fast?
Hello! I found a really good stick!
greet.routine.lessons: Hello! We're at lessons. Shh, the teacher's watching.
Hi! I'm learning my letters. Want to hear the alphabet?
Hello! Lessons are boring but don't tell anyone I said that.
Hi! We're learning about the stars today!
Hello! I already know all the answers. Mostly.
Hi! I'm supposed to be paying attention. Hello!
greet.routine.shelter: Hello! Come in out of the rain!
Oh, you're drenched! Come stand under the roof.
Hello! I ran home the moment it started pouring.
Hello! Rainy afternoon. Perfect for staying in.
Hello! I got caught halfway across the square. My shoes are full of water.
Hello! Inside's where all the sensible people are today.
greet.routine.storm: Hello! Quick, inside! That lightning's close!
You're out in this? Come in, come in!
Hello! I'm staying put until the sky calms down.
Hello! Every clap of thunder makes me jump. Don't laugh.
Hello! Shut the door, quick! The wind's fierce.
Hello. I'm counting between the flashes and the booms. It's getting closer.
greet.routine.snowed_in: Hello! Come warm your hands by the fire.
Oh, you're covered in snow! Stamp your feet before you come in.
Hello! I'm not going out in that. Not for all the emeralds in the world.
Hello! Cozy day by the hearth for me.
Hello! The snow's piling up against the door.
Hello! I've got a blanket and a warm drink and I'm not moving.
greet.routine.rain_walk: Hello! I love walking in the rain. Everyone thinks I'm odd.
Hello! Don't hide from it, the rain's lovely!
Hello! I'm soaked and happy about it!
Hello! Listen to it pattering on the leaves.
Hello! Puddle-jumping is very serious business.
greet.routine.snow_play: Hello! Snowball fight! Want to join?
Hi! I'm building a snow golem! It doesn't move yet.
Hello! Look how deep the snow is! It's up to my knees!
Hi! Catch a snowflake on your tongue! Like this!
Hello! My nose is frozen and I don't care!
Hi! I made a snow angel! It's a bit square.
routine.sleep: I really should be in bed by now. I'll say goodnight soon.
My eyelids are getting heavy. It's been a long day.
Bedtime, I'm afraid. Even the chickens have turned in.
I'm just about to blow out my lamp. The dark's coming down quick.
My bed's calling me. It's very persuasive.
I'll be dreaming soon. Hopefully about pie again.
I keep my bed by the window so the morning light wakes me. Bit of a trick, that.
Sleep's the best medicine. That, and soup.
I always sleep better after a good day. And today was a good one.
If you hear snoring, it's my neighbor. Definitely not me.
I count sheep to fall asleep. Real ones. There are eleven.
Goodnight soon, {player}. Don't wander too far in the dark.
routine.nap: A nap after lunch is the secret to a long life. Or at least a good mood.
I was in the middle of a lovely nap. I dreamed I was a cloud.
Napping is an art, and I'm a master.
Everyone works so hard. I nap so they don't have to. Balance.
A little rest and I'll be good as new. Or as good as I ever am.
Don't tell anyone I nap every day. It's my secret talent.
The hay in the barn makes the best nap spot. Itchy, but cozy.
I'll be up and about in a bit. Probably. Possibly.
Naps are like little holidays you take every afternoon.
I could nap anywhere. I once napped standing up.
My cat taught me how to nap properly. Find the sunbeam, curl up, ignore everyone.
Shh. The afternoon's for resting. That's the rule.
routine.wake: I just woke up. The world's a bit fuzzy around the edges.
I always wake up hungry. Is that normal? Don't answer.
I had the strangest dream about a flying pig wearing a saddle.
The roosters did their job. Unfortunately.
I like to lie still for a minute when I wake up and listen to the village.
First thing every morning I open the shutters and say hello to the day.
Morning stiffness. My back sounds like a creaky door.
I woke up before the bell today. A personal triumph.
My bed was so warm. Leaving it is the bravest thing I do all day.
The light comes through my window at just the right angle at dawn. That's my alarm.
I splash cold water on my face every morning. It's horrible. It works.
New day, clean slate. Let's see what happens.
routine.breakfast: Breakfast is the most important meal. Lunch is a close second. Supper's third. Snacks are fourth.
Bread, honey and an apple. Perfect start.
I eat breakfast slowly. The rest of the day goes too fast as it is.
My breakfast is cold because I've been talking. Worth it.
I fry an egg every morning. The chickens pretend not to notice.
Porridge again. It's always porridge. I love porridge.
I like to plan my day over breakfast. Then I ignore the plan.
Good bread and good company. That's the whole recipe for a good morning.
Breakfast tastes better when the window's open.
I always save a crust for the birds.
My neighbor makes the best jam. I have to trade for it. It's worth every emerald.
Toast is just bread with ambition, really.
routine.prayer: I start every day with a little quiet. It helps me hear what matters.
I pray for good harvests, safe travelers and fewer zombies.
The temple's peaceful at dawn. Just me, the candles and the brewing stand bubbling.
I always say a word for travelers. That includes you.
A few quiet minutes make a whole day gentler.
Some people say prayers. Some people say thank you. I say both.
The incense makes me sneeze, but I like the smell.
I keep a list of everyone in {village} and think of each of them. It takes a while.
Even the golem stands still while the morning bell rings. Respectful.
There's a stillness at dawn I can't find any other time.
routine.work: I'm right in the thick of it. Busy hands, happy heart.
Work's going well. Don't jinx it.
A good day's work is its own reward. Emeralds help too.
I'm halfway through today's tasks and all the way out of patience. Hello, though!
I love the rhythm of work. Thump, thump, thump. Like a heartbeat.
Work's work. It gets done because I do it.
I've been at it since morning. Can't stop now, I'm on a roll.
There's always one more thing to do. That's how you know it's honest work.
My workstation and I understand each other. Mostly.
Busy day. The whole village needs something from me.
I'll stop for lunch when the bell rings and not a moment before.
Hard work's easier when someone stops by to say hello.
I take pride in my work. Even the boring bits.
routine.lunch: Lunch by the bell is the best tradition {village} has.
I'm sharing lunch with everyone today. Pass the bread.
My lunch is mostly bread. My friend's lunch is mostly my bread.
Lunch is short, so I eat fast and talk faster.
The whole village comes to the bell at noon. It's like a family picnic every day.
I traded half a carrot for half a pie. Excellent deal.
I like eating outside. Food tastes better with sky above it.
Sit down! There's room on the bench.
Lunch is when all the real news gets shared.
I eat lunch with {friend} most days. We always end up laughing.
Midday sun, cold apple, good company. Perfect.
After lunch, I always want a nap. Don't let me.
routine.lunch_home: I like a quiet lunch at home. The bell gets loud at noon.
I came home for lunch. My own chair's comfier than any bench.
Lunch at home means I don't have to share my cheese.
Sometimes you just want your own kitchen, you know?
I made soup this morning. It's even better at lunch.
Home for lunch, back to work after. That's the rhythm.
I eat at home so I can take my boots off for an hour.
My kitchen's small, but it's mine.
I had lunch with my cat. She ate most of it.
routine.lunch_tavern: The tavern does a lovely midday stew. I'm a regular.
Lunch at the tavern! I've earned it this week.
The tavern's busy at noon. Everyone's swapping stories over soup.
I come here for the bread. The bread is a work of art.
Tavern lunches make me feel like a traveler, even though I live two doors away.
The tavern keeper knows exactly how I like my soup. That's friendship.
There's always someone new at the tavern at lunchtime.
I had the special. I don't know what it was. It was delicious.
Tavern food and tavern gossip. Both very filling.
I'm just having a quick bite. And a quick chat. And maybe a slow cider.
routine.hobby: Free time! I'm spending it on {hobby}, as usual.
This is the hour I live for. Work's done, the day's still bright.
I've been at my hobby since the end of work. I've lost track of time.
Everyone needs something they do just because they love it. Mine's {hobby}.
I'm not very good at {hobby}, but I'm very happy doing it.
My favorite spot for {hobby} is just past the houses, where it's quiet.
I've been trying something new with my {hobby} today. It's going... interestingly.
They say {hobby} is good for the soul. My soul's in great shape.
When I'm {hobby}, the world goes quiet. In a good way.
I could talk about {hobby} for hours. Should I? You look like you'd let me.
Afternoons are made for hobbies. That's my philosophy.
I lose myself in {hobby}. Then someone has to come and find me for supper.
routine.social: This is the best hour. Everybody's out and everyone's talking.
I came to the bell to catch up. You hear everything here eventually.
Neighbors, gossip and the last of the sunshine. Lovely.
I love this time of day. The whole village is one big conversation.
{friend} and I were just chatting about the weather. Riveting stuff.
Come sit with us! The bench is warm from the sun.
There's always someone to talk to by the bell.
I've had six conversations in the last hour. I'm exhausted. Happily.
The children run around, the grown-ups talk, the golem watches. Village life!
This is when you find out who's sweet on whom.
I like to stand by the bell and say hello to everyone who passes.
Gossip is just news with feelings in it.
routine.market: Market Day! I've bought a scarf, three apples and a wooden duck I don't need.
The stalls are full. Have you tried the honey?
I love haggling. I'm terrible at it, but I love it.
Everyone brings their best for Market Day. The bakers outdo themselves.
I saved up all week for Market Day. All gone now. Worth it.
The cartographer's selling maps. I don't go anywhere, but I like looking at them.
Market Day's the only day I see everyone in one place.
I sold two baskets of eggs. The chickens deserve a cut.
I could walk around the market all day. I probably will.
No work on Market Day. Just browsing, chatting and nibbling.
The children are running between the stalls. Somebody's going to knock over the pies.
I traded a song for a sweet bun. The baker has terrible taste in music, but I'm not complaining.
routine.supper: Supper's my favorite meal. Everyone's home and the day's done.
I made stew. It's always stew. Stew is a lifestyle.
Supper smells drifting through {village}... my stomach's growling.
We eat together as a family. Even when it's chaos.
Supper's simple tonight. Bread, cheese and good company.
I burned the carrots. Don't tell anyone.
After supper I'll do the dishes. Probably. Eventually.
The best part of supper is the talking, not the eating.
I always cook too much. Leftovers for breakfast!
Supper by the window. I can watch the sunset while I eat.
routine.evening: Just winding down for the night. Feet up, thoughts slow.
I like the evenings. Everything's soft and golden and quiet.
I'm sitting by the lamp, mending a sock. Exciting stuff.
Evenings are for small things. A good chair, a warm drink.
I watch the stars come out from my window most nights.
My house creaks in the evenings, like it's stretching after a long day.
I read a little every evening. Just a page or two before bed.
Quiet evenings are the reward for busy days.
I can hear the tavern from here. Sometimes I sing along. Badly.
I tidy up a little before bed. It makes the morning nicer.
routine.tavern: The tavern's the warmest place in {village} after dark.
I come here most evenings. The cider's good and the stories are better.
Someone's always telling a tall tale at the tavern. Tonight it's about a talking cow.
I've been here an hour and I've heard three songs and two arguments.
The tavern keeper knows everyone's business. And everyone's favorite drink.
I'm only staying for one cider. That was two ciders ago.
Tavern nights are when the village really relaxes.
The fire's crackling, the bard's singing, the mugs are full. What more could you want?
I lost at dice. Again. I always lose at dice.
Sit with us! There's always room at the tavern.
I come for the company. The cider's a bonus.
The tavern smells of woodsmoke and apples. I could live here.
routine.perform: I'm performing tonight! The tavern's packed.
I've been practicing a new song all week. Tonight's the debut.
My fingers are nervous. My heart's excited. My voice is undecided.
There's nothing like playing for a room full of friends.
I'll play the old favorites first, then something new.
Music brings the whole village together. Even the people who can't dance.
If they throw tomatoes, I'll make soup. Silver linings.
Every performance is different. That's the magic.
I wrote a song about {village}. I hope they like it.
The tavern goes quiet when I start. That's my favorite sound.
routine.night_watch: All quiet on the watch. The best kind of night.
I walk the edge of the village every hour. Torches lit, eyes open.
Night watch is lonely, but someone has to keep the zombies honest.
I've seen two skeletons and a very confused spider tonight.
The stars are bright. Good for spotting things in the dark.
I sleep in the day so I can guard at night. My schedule's upside down.
You get to know the night sounds on watch. Every creak and groan.
If you hear the bell ring at night, run indoors. That's my signal.
My lantern, my sword and my wits. All I need.
Nothing gets past me. Except bats. Bats get past everyone.
The golem and I have an understanding. It takes the north side, I take the south.
Long night ahead. Good thing I like the quiet.
We walk the watch in pairs now. Nobody walks the dark alone.
My partner takes the left side of the road, I take the right. We meet at every lamp.
routine.defend: Everyone else is hiding. That's how it should be. This part is our job.
We muster at the bell, then we go out to meet them.
Pillagers hit hard. Stay out of their crossbow range if you can.
If anyone falls, get them salts or a tonic. We don't leave our people on the ground.
The bell's rung. Swords out, bows strung.
I've drilled for this every morning. Let's see if it pays off.
Watch for the big beasts. Ravagers don't stop for anything.
routine.play: I'm a knight and this stick is my sword!
We built a fort out of hay bales. It's the best fort ever.
I'm hiding from my friends. They'll never find me here. Oops, you found me.
We're racing to the bell and back! Want to race?
I'm pretending to be a creeper. Hssss! Boom!
I found a frog! His name is Admiral Hop.
We're playing village. I'm the bell.
routine.lessons: We're learning about the stars! Did you know there's one shaped like a pickaxe?
The teacher says I'm very bright. Like a torch.
I'm learning my numbers. I can count all the way to sixty-four! That's a whole stack!
We're learning the names of every block. There are SO many.
Lessons are fun when there's drawing. Today there's drawing!
I wrote my name! It's a bit wobbly.
The teacher says if I pay attention I'll be a scholar someday.
We learned that creepers are afraid of cats. Is that true?
routine.shelter: I came inside the moment the rain started. My hat's still dripping.
Rainy days are for staying in, sipping something warm.
I don't mind the rain, as long as I'm watching it from inside.
Listen to it drumming on the roof. Lovely.
I got halfway to the bell and the sky opened up. So here I am.
The fields need the rain. My shoes don't.
I'll wait it out. The village will still be there when it stops.
Everyone's indoors. {village} looks like a ghost town from my window.
I'm using the rain as an excuse to do nothing. Highly recommended.
The rain smells so fresh. I'll go out the second it stops.
My roof only leaks in one spot. I put a bucket there. It's practically a fountain.
Rain makes the house cozy. Candles, blankets, the works.
routine.storm: Did you see that flash? I nearly dropped my mug.
The storm's right overhead. Stay away from the windows.
I don't like thunder. There, I said it.
The animals are all huddled up. Smart animals.
Every flash lights up the whole village like daytime for a blink.
Lightning hit a tree by the river once. It was never the same.
I'm staying inside until this blows over. You should too.
Listen to that wind! The shutters are rattling.
Storms remind me how small we are. And how cozy a roof is.
If lightning strikes a pig, you get something awful. I'm not going near the pens.
The golem stands out there in the storm like it's nothing. Brave thing.
Thunder rolls on and on. Like a giant's stomach.
routine.snowed_in: I've got the fire roaring and I'm not leaving it.
The snow's piled up against the door. I'm snowed in. Perfect excuse.
Warm socks, hot stew, a good book. That's how you beat winter.
I can see my breath, even inside. The fire needs more wood.
The cold gets into my bones. Into my soul, a little.
The children are out playing in it. They're tougher than me.
I'm knitting a scarf. It's mostly holes, but it's warm holes.
Snowy days are for staying in and telling stories.
My fingers are just starting to thaw.
Everything outside is white and silent. It's beautiful. From in here.
routine.rain_walk: I love the rain! Everyone hides, so I have the whole village to myself.
Rain on my face feels like the sky saying hello.
The puddles are perfect for jumping in. I'm a grown resident and I don't care.
The flowers drink it up. You can almost hear them saying thank you.
Most people run inside. I always stay out. It feels like an adventure.
The rain makes everything sparkle. Even the dirt.
I'm completely soaked and I've never been happier.
There's a little stream running down the path. I'm following it to see where it goes.
Rain smells like the earth waking up.
Why stay dry? Dry is boring.
routine.snow_play: I'm building a snow golem! I've named it Sir Frosty.
Snowball fight! I've already hit three people. And one cow.
I made a snow angel. It looks more like a snow potato.
Catch a snowflake! They taste like nothing, but it's fun!
The snow's perfect for sledding down the hill. No sled, though.
My toes are cold but my heart is warm!
I'm making a snow fort. Nobody's getting in.
I love snow! Everything's new and white and quiet.
weather.clear: Not a cloud in the sky. The kind of day that makes you want to go somewhere.
Clear skies today. Even the golem looks cheerful.
Fine weather! I hung my washing out and it dried in an hour.
Days like this, I almost forgive winter.
Beautiful day. The sort the old songs are about.
Clear and bright. You can see all the way to the mountains.
Sunshine's good for the crops and better for the mood.
The sky's so blue it looks painted on.
A gentle breeze, a warm sun. You couldn't order better.
Perfect drying weather. Everyone in {village} has their sheets out.
I love a clear day. The whole village seems to stand up straighter.
No rain, no wind, no trouble. Just a good, plain day.
The kind of day that smells like cut grass and warm stone.
Lovely out. Even the cows look like they're smiling.
A day this nice feels like a gift.
I opened every window in the house. Let the sunshine in.
Clear skies mean clear stars tonight. I'll be up late looking.
On days like this, everyone moves a little slower. In a good way.
Fair weather for working, fair weather for wandering.
Warm sun on my face and nowhere to hurry to. Lovely.
Good weather makes good neighbors. Everyone's out and friendly.
The bees are busy, the birds are loud and I'm happy.
A clear sky like this makes the whole world feel bigger.
There's a sort of hum in the air on a sunny day. Can you hear it?
Lovely weather for a walk. Or a nap in the sun.
I can see a hawk circling way up high. It's that clear.
Days like these, I'm glad I live in {village}.
Nothing but blue overhead. I'll take it.
The sun's out and so is the laundry. Watch your head.
Such a bright day. I keep squinting at everything like it owes me money.
weather.clearing: The rain's stopped! Everything's dripping and sparkling.
Smell that air! Nothing smells better than right after rain.
Did you see the rainbow? It ended right behind the barn. No pot of gold, though. I checked.
The clouds are breaking up. Blue sky's peeking through.
The puddles are full of sky now. I like that.
Everything's washed clean. Even the path looks new.
The rain's gone and the frogs are celebrating.
The whole village is coming back outside, blinking like owls.
After the rain, the flowers stand up a little taller.
I love how the stone shines after rain.
The gutters are still gurgling. Like the village is humming.
Everyone's shaking out their coats and hats. Very damp chorus.
The fields look greener already. Plants are quick learners.
The air's cool and fresh. Breathe it in.
The children are out puddle-jumping already. Their mothers are not pleased.
The sun's back, a little shy, but back.
Wet leaves, warm light. My favorite combination.
Now the mushrooms will pop up everywhere. Mind where you step.
I can hear the river from here. It's swollen with rain.
Clearing up nicely. Perfect for a walk, if you don't mind wet boots.
weather.rain: Rain again. The farmers are happy, at least.
I like the sound of rain on the roof. Very soothing.
My boots are soaked through. Every step goes squish.
The rain's good for the crops. Less good for my hair.
Everyone's indoors. The village sounds like it's holding its breath.
Rainy days are for stories and warm drinks.
The ducks are thrilled. Everyone else is grumbling.
Water's running down the path like a little river.
The rain makes the whole village smell like wet hay.
My cat's furious about the rain. She blames me personally.
I love watching rain from a window. Less so from under it.
Don't forget your hood if you're heading out. You'll be wet to the bone.
The bell sounds different in the rain. Muffled. Sleepy.
Rain, rain. It'll stop eventually. Probably.
The well's filling up nicely, at least.
Puddles everywhere! The children will be ecstatic.
I put a bucket under the leak in my roof. It's playing a little tune.
Wet weather means mud, and mud means everyone's tracking it in.
The sky's been weeping all day. Wonder what's upset it.
I don't mind a bit of rain. It makes the sunny days feel earned.
Rain drums on the leaves like a hundred tiny fingers.
The fishermen say fish bite better in the rain. They also say a lot of things.
Everything's grey and silver today. Pretty, in its way.
The sheep look twice their size when they're wet. And twice as grumpy.
If it rains much longer, the river will flood the low fields.
I had plans today. The rain had other plans.
Rainy days make bread rise slower. Or so the baker says.
There's something cozy about a whole village sheltering together.
The drip from the eaves is driving me mad. Drip. Drip. Drip.
My garden needed this. My laundry didn't.
I saw the golem standing in the rain like it didn't even notice.
The chickens all crammed into one corner of the coop. Sensible birds.
Rain hides all the noise. You can hear yourself think.
Somebody left their door open and now their hallway's a pond.
It's the kind of rain that can't decide if it's drizzle or a downpour.
Wet weather makes my knees ache. That's how I know it's coming.
I tried to dash between houses and got soaked anyway. Never works.
The roofs are all shiny. The village looks polished.
I like rainy evenings. Lamp lit, kettle on, rain outside.
Even the zombies hate the rain. Well, they don't burn in it, so maybe they like it.
weather.thunder: That thunder made me jump right out of my seat!
The storm's right on top of us. Stay away from tall things.
Every flash, I count. One, two... boom! It's close.
I've never liked storms. They feel personal.
The animals are all spooked. The cows are huddled like gossiping aunties.
Lightning lit up the whole village a moment ago. Bright as noon.
The wind's howling down the chimney. Sounds like a ghost choir.
Stay inside until it passes, {player}. Promise me.
Storms bring out strange things. Skeletons in daylight. Worse things.
I heard lightning can turn a creeper into something much worse. Charged, they call it.
The rain's coming sideways. Sideways! That's just rude.
I'm keeping my distance from the bell tower. Metal and lightning don't mix.
The sky's angry today. I hope it's not at me.
There's a crackle in the air. Makes my hair stand on end.
The bigger the flash, the more I want my bed.
When the thunder rolls, I always think of giants bowling.
Lightning hit the old oak by the river once. Split it right down the middle.
The candle keeps flickering. The house is trembling with every boom.
A storm like this, I'm glad of every stone in my walls.
They say lightning never strikes the same place twice. Lightning hasn't heard that.
The children are hiding under the table. I'm hiding behind the children.
Thunder makes the windows rattle. And my teeth.
Even the golem flinched at that last one. Or I imagined it.
I'm making tea to calm my nerves. And my neighbors' nerves.
What a racket. The sky's doing its spring cleaning.
Storms clear the air. That's what my grandmother said, every single storm.
If you have to go out, keep low and move fast.
Somewhere a farmer's watching his wheat flatten and crying.
I love the smell after a storm. Not the storm itself, though.
Booming, flashing, pouring. The sky's showing off today.
weather.snow: Snow! Everything's gone quiet and white.
I love the first snow. The world looks brand new.
My nose is so cold I can't feel it. Is it still there?
The snow's piling up on the roofs. Hope they hold.
Everything's muffled in the snow. Even footsteps.
The children have been building snow golems all day. None of them move, thankfully.
Snow on the fields, smoke from every chimney. Pretty as a painting.
I've got three scarves on and I'm still cold.
The path's slippery. I've fallen twice. Gracefully, both times.
Snowy days are for soup. Lots of soup.
I can see every animal's tracks in the snow. Rabbits, foxes, something big.
The well's frozen over. We have to break the ice every morning.
Snowflakes are all different, they say. I've looked. They look the same to me.
My breath makes little clouds. I pretend I'm a dragon.
Snow makes the nights brighter, did you notice?
The trees look like they've been dusted with sugar.
I spent the morning shoveling. My arms have filed a complaint.
Polar bears would love it here today. Please don't bring any.
The snow's too deep for the chickens. They refuse to go out.
A snowy village at dusk, lamps glowing. Nothing prettier.
I wear my thickest socks on snow days. Two pairs, actually.
The river's still running under the ice. You can hear it if you listen.
Snow makes everyone a little kinder. Everyone's cold together.
I made hot cider. Want some? It warms you right to the toes.
Watch out for powder snow. Step in it and you'll sink like a stone.
The goats are the only ones enjoying this. Goats are strange.
Every footstep crunches. I love that crunch.
The snow's lovely to look at and miserable to walk in.
My fingers are icicles. Ten little icicles.
Snow means the year's turning. Time for long nights and stories.
weather.hot: It's scorching! I've moved my work into the shade.
The heat's shimmering off the sand. Makes everything wobble.
Hot enough to bake bread on the doorstep. Somebody tried.
I'm drinking water like a sponge today.
Even the cactus looks thirsty.
The sun's merciless today. Wear a hat, {player}.
On days like this, I dream of snow. Then I remember snow and stop.
I sleep on the roof on hot nights. The breeze is better up there.
The camels don't seem to mind the heat. Show-offs.
The well water's warm. That's how you know it's a hot one.
Too hot to work, too hot to rest, too hot to complain. Almost.
I keep my clay jugs in the shade so the water stays cool.
Everyone's slow in the heat. Even the gossip moves slowly.
The husks shamble about in this heat like it's nothing. Creepy things.
Sunburn's no joke out here. My nose peels every summer.
When the sun goes down, the whole village comes back to life.
The shade of a palm tree is worth more than gold today.
It's so hot my sandals stuck to the path.
The air tastes like dust and sunshine.
Hot days, cool nights. That's the way out here.
time.dawn: Dawn's the quietest hour. Even the chickens are still deciding whether to bother.
The light's all pink and gold. It won't last, so look now.
I like being up before everyone else. The village feels like mine for a moment.
Dawn smells of dew and woodsmoke.
The roosters are warming up. Brace yourself.
The mist's lifting off the fields like a curtain going up.
Early hours are honest hours. Nobody's pretending yet.
I watched the sun come up over the hills. Same sun, new day.
The first bread's in the oven somewhere. I can smell it.
Dawn's when the zombies give up and the birds take over.
The world's still soft at the edges this early.
Even the golem looks peaceful at dawn.
I always feel hopeful at this hour. Silly, maybe.
The dew soaks my boots every morning. I keep forgetting.
At dawn you can hear the river all the way from here.
The stars are fading one by one. Goodnight, stars.
Early bird gets the worm. I'd rather get the bread.
This is the hour for quiet thoughts and warm hands.
time.morning: Mornings are for getting things done. Or at least starting them.
The village has a busy hum in the mornings. I like it.
Everyone's off to work. Hammers, hoes and hellos.
The morning light makes the whole place look freshly washed.
I like mornings. I've had my breakfast and I haven't made any mistakes yet.
There's a line at the well every morning. Best place for gossip.
The baker's already sold out of the good loaves.
Morning's when the smiths start banging away. You get used to it.
The children are dragging their feet to lessons.
I always plan to do a lot in the morning. Then I talk to people.
A good morning sets the tone for the day. This one's not bad.
The sun's climbing and so's my energy.
The morning air's cool and sharp. Wakes you right up.
Everyone moves with purpose in the morning. By afternoon, less so.
Morning is when the village decides what kind of day it'll be.
I love the clatter of shutters opening all over {village}.
The cats sit in the morning sun like little loaves.
time.noon: The sun's straight overhead. No shadows to hide in.
Noon! My stomach rings louder than the bell.
Midday's the laziest hour. Everyone's either eating or wishing they were.
The heat's settled in. Even the flies are slow.
Halfway through the day already. Where does it go?
At noon the whole village goes quiet for a moment, then everyone starts chewing.
The shadows are tucked right under our feet.
I always want a nap after lunch. Every single day.
Noon's when the market stalls do their best trade.
The bees are busiest at midday. They don't take lunch breaks, poor things.
High noon. Sounds dramatic. It's mostly sandwiches.
The well's crowded at noon. Everyone's thirsty.
Middle of the day, middle of the week. Feels like it, anyway.
I'm hungry. Are you hungry? Everyone's hungry at noon.
The sun at midday makes the bell shine like gold.
time.afternoon: Afternoons are slow and golden. My favorite.
The work's mostly done and the evening's not here yet. Perfect in-between.
Long afternoon shadows make everything look important.
The bees are drowsy, the cats are drowsy, I'm drowsy.
Afternoon's when the village slows down and starts chatting.
The children are out of lessons and running riot.
I do my best thinking in the afternoon. Or my best daydreaming.
The light gets honey-colored this time of day.
A cup of something warm and an afternoon off. Bliss.
The afternoon's when you notice the little things. The birdsong. The breeze.
It's {time}. The day's starting to stretch its legs toward evening.
Afternoon sun's the warmest. Find a wall to lean on.
I always lose track of time in the afternoon.
The fields look gold from here. The wheat's nearly ready.
The quiet part of the day. Everyone's busy or napping.
time.evening: The sun's setting. Look at those colors!
Evening's coming in. Lanterns going up all over {village}.
Everyone's heading home. Supper smoke from every chimney.
The cows are coming in from the fields, mooing about it.
I love the evening. The day's work is behind me.
The sky's turning purple. Night's not far off.
Evenings are short, so I savor them.
The crickets are starting up. Their evening concert.
When the sun goes down, the tavern lights up.
Golden hour. Everything looks like it's made of honey.
I should head in soon. The dark comes quick out here.
The swallows are swooping for their supper.
Evening is the village taking a deep breath.
Everyone's a little softer in the evening. Tired and kind.
The last light on the bell tower. Lovely.
Soon the zombies will be out. Let's enjoy the last of the light.
time.night: It's dark out. Stay near the torches, {player}.
The stars are out. So are the skeletons.
I don't go out after dark if I can help it. Too many groaning noises.
Night's peaceful, as long as you stay inside.
The village feels different at night. Smaller. Closer together.
The golem patrols at night. I sleep better knowing it's out there.
Listen to the frogs! They're louder than the tavern.
Night is for sleeping and for stories. Mostly sleeping.
I can see the glow of the torches all down the path. Like a necklace.
The moon makes everything silver tonight.
Strange how the whole world shrinks to the circle of your lamplight.
If you hear a hiss in the dark, run. Don't wait to see what it is.
Every night I check the door twice. Zombies can't open doors. Probably.
The night sky's full of stars. You'd never count them all.
Owls are out tonight. Hooting their little questions.
The dark makes small noises sound enormous.
time.late: It's the middle of the night. Everyone sensible is asleep.
The world's so quiet now you can hear your own heartbeat.
I couldn't sleep. Too many thoughts rattling around.
At this hour, even the zombies seem tired.
Midnight's a strange time. It belongs to nobody.
If you haven't slept in days, watch the sky. Phantoms.
The fire's down to embers. I should add a log. Or go to bed.
Late nights make for groggy mornings. I never learn.
Shh. Listen. That's the sound of a whole village dreaming.
The stars have moved since I last looked. They never stay put.
Only owls and night watchmen are up at this hour.
I like the night's silence. It's like the world's holding its breath.
Middle of the night thoughts are always the strangest thoughts.
The moon's high and the shadows are long.
moon.full: A full moon tonight. Everything's bright as a silver coin.
Full moon! They say slimes come up from the swamps on nights like this.
The full moon makes the whole village glow. Very romantic. For some.
I always sleep badly under a full moon. Too much light.
Full moon tonight. The monsters seem bolder. Stay close.
Look at that moon! Round as a wheel of cheese.
On full moon nights my grandmother said you could see the man in the moon. He's very square.
The full moon makes the river shine like a road.
moon.waning_gibbous: The moon's a little lopsided tonight. Like it's been nibbled.
Not quite full anymore. The moon's shrinking back.
The moon's still bright, but it's on its way out.
A fat moon, slowly slimming down.
The moon's half-hiding tonight. Shy, maybe.
Still plenty of moonlight to walk home by.
moon.last_quarter: Half a moon tonight. Like someone sliced it.
The moon's a half-circle. Cut neat as a pie.
Half moon. Half light. Half asleep, me.
The moon's in its quiet half tonight.
Only half a moon to see by. Bring a torch.
A half moon always looks a bit like a smile from the side.
moon.waning_crescent: Just a sliver of moon tonight. A fingernail in the sky.
The moon's nearly gone. Dark nights coming.
A thin little moon. Like a smile someone's trying to hide.
Crescent moon. Pretty, but it doesn't light much.
The moon's fading away. It'll be back. It always comes back.
Barely any moonlight tonight. Mind your step.
moon.new: No moon tonight. It's dark as the inside of a cave.
New moon. The stars get all the attention tonight.
You can't see your hand in front of your face out there. No moon at all.
New moon nights are the darkest. The monsters love them.
Without the moon, the stars look twice as bright.
The moon's hiding tonight. Taking a night off.
New moon. A good night for stargazing and a bad night for walking.
Pitch dark. Keep a torch in your hand tonight.
moon.waxing_crescent: A new sliver of moon tonight. It's growing back!
A thin crescent, low in the sky. Like a hook for hanging stars.
The moon's coming back, a little at a time.
Look, the moon's peeking out again.
A baby moon. It'll be big and round soon enough.
Just a curl of moon tonight. Pretty.
moon.first_quarter: Half a moon, growing fatter every night.
Half moon tonight. Halfway to full.
The moon's filling up like a bucket at the well.
A half moon, bright and sharp.
Half moon. Enough light to walk by, not enough to read.
The moon's halfway there. So am I, with everything.
moon.waxing_gibbous: The moon's almost full. One more night, maybe two.
Nearly a full moon. Can you feel the monsters getting restless?
The moon's swelling up. Full moon's coming.
The moon's plump tonight. Like a well-fed cat.
Almost full. The whole sky's getting brighter.
day.market: It's Market Day! Everyone's out trading and gossiping.
Market Day's the best day. No work, just stalls and treats.
I've been saving up all week for Market Day.
Have you seen the stalls by the bell? The cartographer has new maps!
Market Day always smells like fresh pies and new wool.
Everyone wears their good clothes on Market Day. Even the nitwit.
I traded six eggs for a ribbon. Bargain.
The children get a copper each on Market Day. They spend it on sweets in about a minute.
Market Day's when the village feels most like a village.
There's music by the bell. The bard plays for coins on Market Day.
I bought more than I meant to. I always do on Market Day.
The whole of {village} turns out on Market Day. You'll meet everyone.
Market Day rule: no talking about work. Only gossip and prices.
I'm going back for another honey cake. Don't judge me.
Somebody's selling knitted hats. I'm tempted. It's not even cold.
Market Day means the wandering traders sometimes stop by. Sometimes with llamas.
I love the noise of Market Day. Everyone haggling at once.
Market Day's a little holiday every week. Clever, whoever thought of it.
day.week: Another {weekday}. They do come round, don't they?
Happy {weekday}! Not that anything special happens on {weekday}s.
It's day {day} by my count. I count every one.
I always forget what day it is. It's {weekday}, someone told me.
Market Day's {market}. I'm already planning what to buy.
{weekday}s are for honest work and early nights.
Is it {weekday}? It feels more like a Hearthday to me.
Market Day's {market}, and I've got nothing to sell. Again.
The week goes Moonday, Bellday, Hearthday, Wellday, Lanternday, Hayday and then Market Day. I sing it to remember.
It's {weekday}. My favorite day is always tomorrow.
Day {day} in {village}. Feels like I've been counting forever.
Market Day is {market}. I can hold out until then.
work.farmer: The wheat's coming in tall this year. You can hear it whisper when the wind blows.
Carrots, potatoes, beetroots. Same rows every season, and every season it still feels like a small miracle.
The composter's my best friend. Rotten food in, bone meal out. Magic, really.
I talk to my crops. Don't laugh. The pumpkins grow bigger when I do.
Crows are the bane of my life. And rabbits. And the occasional cow.
I water the fields first thing, before the sun gets fierce.
A good farmer watches the sky more than the soil.
Farmland dries out if you're not careful. Keep water within four blocks. That's the trick.
Harvest week is the busiest week of the year. Everyone pitches in, even the nitwit. Sort of.
I've got calluses on my calluses.
Melons are tricky. They need space to spread. Like teenagers.
I swap my extra wheat for emeralds with anyone who'll have it.
Don't trample the crops! Jumping on farmland turns it right back to dirt.
I plant by the moon. My grandmother did. Can't hurt.
The beetroot this year is so red it looks embarrassed.
Bees love the flowers along my fields. More bees, more crops.
I rotate my fields every year. Keeps the soil happy.
Nothing tastes better than a carrot you grew yourself.
I bake my own bread from my own wheat. Field to table.
Pumpkins! I grew one so big last year the children carved a house in it.
A rainy week does more for my fields than a month of watering.
The golem watches over the fields at night. It's a fine scarecrow, honestly.
My hoe's been in the family for three generations. New handle, new blade, same hoe.
I grew sweet berries along the fence to keep the foxes out. Now the foxes come for the berries.
Every seed's a promise. Not every promise is kept, but most are.
I leave the edge of each field wild for the bees.
Sugar cane by the river's doing well. The baker wants it all for cakes.
Farming's honest work. The soil gives back what you put in.
Some mornings the mist sits on the fields like a blanket. Beautiful.
A good harvest means a good winter. Simple as that.
I once grew a potato shaped exactly like the cleric. We don't talk about it.
Up before the sun, done after it. That's farming.
The children help me pick the carrots. Half of them get eaten on the spot.
I've got dirt under my nails that's older than you.
The farmers in the desert grow cactus and sugar cane. Brave people.
work.librarian: Every book on my shelves has been read at least twice. Mostly by me.
I've been copying an old atlas. My hand's cramping, but the maps are beautiful.
Someone returned a book with a pressed flower inside. That's the best kind of late fee.
I have enchanted books for trade, if you're interested. Efficiency, mending, all sorts.
The lectern's where I do my best thinking. And my worst handwriting.
Quiet, please. Oh, it's just me here. Never mind. Hello!
Books are doors. Every one opens somewhere new.
I'm cataloguing the village's history. It's surprisingly dramatic for such a small place.
Paper's getting expensive. Sugar cane's in short supply. Tell the farmer.
I read to the children every evening. Their favorite is the one about the brave chicken.
A bookshelf around an enchanting table makes the magic stronger. Fifteen is the number.
I've been trying to read an old book in a language I don't know. Mostly I stare at the pictures.
Ink stains on my fingers, dust on my sleeves. Proper librarian.
Every word written down is a word that lives longer than the writer.
I traded for a book about the End. I read it twice and slept with a lamp on.
The best stories aren't on my shelves yet. They're still out there being lived.
Mending's the most precious book I have. Repairs your gear as you gather experience.
I rearrange the shelves by subject, then by author, then by color. It never sticks.
Books need care. Keep them dry, keep them out of the sun, keep them away from goats.
I'm writing my own book. It's about a librarian. Very autobiographical.
If you find any old books on your travels, bring them to me. I'll pay well.
Someone asked me for a book on how to be patient. It's on loan. Indefinitely.
Silence isn't empty. It's full of stories waiting to be read.
I learned to read before I could walk. I'm still a slow walker.
My lectern creaks when I lean on it. It's like it's listening.
The village archives go back over a hundred years. Births, weddings, the great cabbage blight.
I'll read anything. Recipes, maps, tombstones. Words are words.
I've lent my favorite book to {neighbor}. I check on it every day.
Knowledge is the only treasure that grows when you give it away.
Enchantments are tricky. Some stack, some don't. I keep notes.
The candle burns down while I read. I never notice until it's out.
I've got a book on every animal in the region. Even the ones I've never seen.
