Paper, ink and quiet. That's all a librarian needs.
Reading by the fire on a rainy evening. Is there anything better?
I once fell asleep reading and woke up with the book's words printed backwards on my cheek.
work.fisherman: The river's been generous this week. Cod, salmon, and one very angry pufferfish.
Patience is the whole trick. The fish come to those who wait.
The barrel by my door's always full of something wriggling.
Never eat a pufferfish. I learned that one the hard way.
Early mornings are best. The fish are hungry and the water's still.
I've caught all sorts. Boots, bowls, a saddle once. Sometimes even fish.
Rainy days are good fishing days. The fish don't mind getting wet.
I tie my own lures. This one's got a feather and a bit of string and a lot of hope.
The best fishing spot's my secret. I'd tell you, but then I'd have to move.
Nothing beats a fresh-caught salmon cooked over a campfire.
A good fisherman knows the water like his own hand.
My boat leaks a bit. I bail as I row. Good exercise.
I've been trying to catch the legendary big cod of the lake. I've seen its shadow. Huge.
I trade fish for emeralds. Cooked or raw, your choice.
Tropical fish are pretty, but you can't eat them. Well, you can. Don't.
The river teaches you to be still. Not many places do that anymore.
I fish with an enchanted rod. Lure and Luck of the Sea. Best investment I ever made.
Got a nibble! ...No. Just the wind.
I mend my nets every evening. Holes appear like magic. Bad magic.
Some days I catch nothing and still come home happy.
The drowned in the deep water frighten me. I stay near the shore after dark.
I can tell the weather by the way the fish bite.
Squid ink's useful. Turns paper black. The librarian buys it all.
I caught a fish so big once, it pulled me halfway into the lake. Nobody believes me.
The bobber goes under and your heart goes up. Every time.
My grandmother fished this same river. Same rock, same patience.
Salmon jump upstream in the spring. A sight to see.
Never fish where the guardians swim. That's not fishing, that's foolishness.
I sell my catch at the market. The cats follow me there. All of them.
A quiet morning, a still lake, a full basket. Perfect day.
I've caught enough cod to feed the whole village. And I have. Twice.
Kelp grows wild in the shallows. Dried, it's a decent snack. An acquired taste.
The water tells you things if you listen. Mostly it says "be patient."
I don't need conversation. I have the river.
The best part of fishing isn't the fish. It's the waiting.
work.fletcher: A good arrow needs three things: a straight shaft, sharp flint and true feathers.
I've been fletching all morning. Feathers everywhere. I look like a chicken.
Bows need care. Wax the string, check the limbs, never leave them strung overnight.
I make arrows for the guards and for hunters. Same arrows, different hopes.
The chickens give me feathers, the gravel gives me flint, the trees give me sticks. Teamwork.
My fletching table is the most organized surface in {village}.
I've been experimenting with tipped arrows. Potion-dipped. Slowness, poison, healing even.
A crossbow's slower but hits harder. Some swear by them. I'm a bow person.
Every arrow I make goes somewhere. I hope mostly to targets.
I can tell a good feather by the way it bends.
Spectral arrows glow and show where your target hides. Clever things.
The archers come to me first. I keep their quivers full.
I trade arrows by the stack. Sixty-four's a proper bundle.
Straight shafts are hard to find. I go through a lot of sticks.
I tested a new bow this morning. It sings when you loose. Beautiful sound.
The trick to a good arrow is balance. Front and back, like a good conversation.
The pillagers use crossbows. Poorly made ones, if you ask me.
Flint knapping is noisy work. My neighbors have learned to love it. Or ignore it.
Some people think fletching is simple. Those people have never fletched.
I made a bow for the children. It shoots arrows about four feet. Very safe.
I've got feathers in my hair, in my bed, in my soup.
An archer's only as good as the arrows they shoot. I take that seriously.
I watch the guards practice. I can tell which of my arrows fly truest.
I traded for a box of parrot feathers once. Beautiful arrows. Terrible flight.
I sand every shaft by hand. Smooth as river stone.
Good work takes time. Fast work takes twice the time to fix.
A fletching table, a sharp knife and a quiet afternoon. Bliss.
I sell to hunters, guards and the odd adventurer. Odd ones especially.
Feathers from white chickens make the prettiest arrows.
I can fletch a stack in an hour. Well, a nice slow hour.
There's poetry in a well-made arrow. I'm not a poet, but I see it.
The best compliment I ever got was an archer who never missed with my arrows.
I keep my flint dry and my feathers sorted. That's half the job.
I tried to make an arrow out of a carrot once. Don't ask.
Bowstrings come from spiders. I don't think about that too much.
work.cleric: The brewing stand's been bubbling all day. Healing potions, mostly.
I help where I can. A little prayer, a little potion, a lot of listening.
Redstone dust, glowstone, lapis. Strange things, holy things.
People come to me with their worries. I try to send them away lighter.
I've been brewing a potion of regeneration. It smells like a wet dog, but it works.
The church is quiet in the mornings. That's when I do my best work.
Rotten flesh, rabbit feet, bottles of experience. My trades are an odd lot.
I light candles for anyone who's sick. There are a lot of candles this week.
Healing isn't only about potions. Sometimes it's about a kind word.
I've been trying to brew something that cures loneliness. No luck yet.
Ender pearls are mysterious. Hold one and you can feel it humming.
I bless the fields every spring. The farmers like it. The crops don't seem to mind.
A potion of fire resistance saved an adventurer once. They brought me a cake. Lovely cake.
I don't preach. I listen. That's the job, mostly.
Nether wart's the base of almost everything. Strange that the best medicine grows in such a terrible place.
I've been studying the old texts. Some of them talk about the dragon at the end of the world.
The bell rings and I remember why I do this. To keep people together.
Golden carrots in a brew make you see in the dark. Fascinating.
I sit with the dying and I sit with the newborn. Both are holy.
People think clerics are serious. I laugh more than you'd think.
I keep the church open day and night. Nobody should be turned away.
Splash potions are useful in a hurry. Just don't throw them at your friends.
A potion of weakness and a golden apple can cure a zombie villager. Remember that.
Lapis lazuli is lovely stuff. Blue as a summer sky.
Every potion's a promise. I try to keep mine.
The incense makes me sneeze. Holy sneezes, I tell myself.
Faith's a kind of hope with good posture.
I trade experience bottles. Bottled wisdom, I call it. Very marketable.
The stained glass catches the morning light just so. Worth waking for.
I'm not a miracle worker. But sometimes I get close.
I've been teaching the children their letters on the church steps.
A cleric's door is never locked. That's an old rule.
I brew late into the night. The bubbling helps me think.
Turtle shells make a strange potion. Slow but strong. Like me.
Kindness heals more than any potion. But I'll make you a potion too.
work.cartographer: I'm drawing a new map of the region. There's a forest to the north I've never charted.
Every map I make is a little out of date by the time the ink dries.
I trade explorer maps. Ocean monuments, woodland mansions. Very exciting stuff.
My cartography table's covered in ink and compass needles.
An empty corner of a map is the most exciting thing in the world.
I measure distances in steps. My legs are very tired.
I've charted every river within a day's walk. They all end up at the sea eventually.
Banners make good landmarks. I mark them on every map I draw.
A locator map shows you where you are. A good one shows you where you should be.
I copied a map for a traveler yesterday. They're off to find a shipwreck.
Glass panes on a map lock it so nobody can change it. Very useful for finished work.
Did you know you can zoom a map out with more paper? Bigger world, same desk.
The world keeps going, past every edge I draw.
I dream in contour lines.
I once drew a map so detailed you could see individual sheep.
My favorite tool is a good compass. It never lies about north.
I'd love to map the Nether, but it's so hot the ink boils.
Maps are just stories about places.
I traded a map to a woodland mansion once. The buyer never came back to tell me about it.
Every village has a map of itself. Ours is on my wall. It's got a coffee stain shaped like a lake.
Rivers are the hardest to draw. They never sit still.
Some cartographers make maps for kings. I make them for neighbors. Better customers.
I keep spare maps for anyone who gets lost. People get lost a lot.
The coastline's hard. Every tide changes it a little.
I mark dangerous places in red. There's a lot of red to the east.
A good map can save your life. A bad one can end it.
I'm teaching my apprentice to read a compass. She keeps pointing at lunch.
I've been to the edges of three maps. Each one felt like a door.
Maps make the world smaller and bigger at the same time.
Cartography is careful work. One slip and a mountain becomes a lake.
I'd love to see a map of the whole world someday. It would need a very big wall.
I trade banner patterns too. Colors and crests for every taste.
I've been mapping the caves under the village. There are more than I thought.
The best maps are the ones made by people who walked every step.
When I finish a map, I always sign it with a tiny drawing of the bell.
work.armorer: The forge is hot and the hammer's heavy. Perfect day for armor.
Iron chestplates, chainmail, the odd diamond helmet. I make it all.
Good armor's the difference between a bad day and a last day.
I've been working on a chainmail shirt. Thousands of little rings. My fingers ache.
The blast furnace smelts ore twice as fast. I'd never go back.
I hammer out dents in the guards' armor every week.
Diamond armor's the best, if you can afford it. Most can't.
I keep the forge burning all day. The heat gets into your bones.
A breastplate should fit like it was made for you. Because it was.
I've got burns on my arms from the forge. Badges of honor.
Shields deflect arrows and creeper blasts. Don't leave home without one.
Every piece I make goes out the door with a little bit of me.
I'm experimenting with armor trims. Fancy patterns. Very fashionable.
The anvil sings when the metal's right. Ring, ring, ring.
I sell helmets cheap to adventurers. Head injuries are bad for business.
Netherite's the stuff of legend. I've only seen it once. It was black as midnight.
Armor's heavy, but it's lighter than regret.
I measure everyone who walks by. Habit. You'd be a medium, by the way.
Rust is my nemesis. Oil everything. Every week.
I made a tiny helmet for the baker's cat. It was a joke. The cat took it seriously.
The guards trust me with their lives. I don't take that lightly.
Leather's for beginners, iron's for workers, diamond's for heroes.
I've been at the forge since dawn. My arms are made of noodles now.
Hammer, tongs, bellows, anvil. My whole world.
A good armorer listens to the metal. Sounds silly. It isn't.
I've seen armor that's survived a hundred battles. Mine will survive a thousand. Hopefully.
The best armor is the kind you never have to test.
I trade armor for coal and iron. The forge eats a lot.
Quench in water and the steel hardens. Quench too fast and it cracks. Like people.
I'm proud of every rivet. Every single one.
If you come back with dents, I'll fix them. If you don't come back, I'll be sad.
The bellows breathe and the coals glow. Like the forge is alive.
I've got a scar for every year at the anvil.
Chainmail's lighter than plate and quieter too. Good for sneaking. Not that I sneak.
Smithing tables let you upgrade diamond to netherite. If you're very lucky and very rich.
work.toolsmith: A good pickaxe is a miner's best friend. Mine are the best friends you'll find.
I've been forging hoes for the farmers. Harvest season's coming.
Iron tools for most, diamond for the brave, stone for the frugal.
Keep your tools dry and your edges sharp and they'll outlive you.
The smithing table's where I do the clever bits.
I made an axe so sharp it split a log just by looking at it. Nearly.
Efficiency enchantments make a pickaxe sing through stone.
A dull shovel's a crime. I won't stand for it.
I've got a soft spot for golden tools. They break fast, but they're so shiny.
Every tool tells a story. That nick on the handle? A creeper, I bet.
I sharpen the village's tools for free on Hearthday. Bring yours.
The grindstone takes enchantments off if you need a fresh start. Useful.
A well-balanced hammer is a joy to hold.
I trade tools for iron and coal. Simple business.
Shears are the trickiest. Two blades that have to agree.
I tested a new pickaxe on the hardest stone I could find. Obsidian laughed at it.
Diamond pickaxes are the only things that mine obsidian. Remember that.
My workshop smells of hot iron and oil. Best smell there is.
Tools are extensions of your hands. They should feel like it.
I fix tools the anvil way. A bit of material, a bit of experience.
The farmers break more hoes than anyone. They're rough with them.
I'm working on a fishing rod for the fisherman. Even toolsmiths dabble.
Flint and steel's the oldest tool there is. Still the most useful.
A cheap tool costs you twice. Buy good, buy once.
I've made tools for every resident in {village}. Some of them twice.
I keep a spare pickaxe by every door. Old habit.
Unbreaking's the most underrated enchantment.
I tempered a blade wrong this morning. It's now a very expensive paperweight.
My apprentice made his first shovel today. It's lopsided. I'm very proud.
The forge never sleeps. Well, I do. The forge stays warm.
Copper tools? Someone asked me for copper tools. I told them to ask the lightning rod.
Respect your tools and they'll respect you.
I hear the miners singing in the ravine. Using my pickaxes, I hope.
I'd rather fix something than throw it away.
Steel and patience. That's the whole trade.
work.weaponsmith: I make swords and axes. Mostly I hope they stay on the wall.
The grindstone's turning all day. Edge, edge, edge.
A sword's a responsibility. I only sell to people I trust.
The guards need fresh blades every season. Monsters are hard on steel.
I've been forging a sword with a curved edge. Experimental. Very pretty.
Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods. I've seen them all on enchanted blades.
The weight of a good sword should feel like a handshake.
I made an axe that could cleave a shield in two. I keep it locked away.
Bells and swords are made the same way, you know. Hot metal, hard hammer.
I'd rather make plowshares, but villages need protecting.
Diamond swords are rare. I've made two in my life. Both still in service.
The trick is in the tempering. Too hard and it shatters. Too soft and it bends.
A knight came by and said my sword saved her life. That's why I do this.
I keep my blades oiled and wrapped. Rust is the enemy.
Every sword has a name, if you listen. That one's called Grace.
The forge glows red at night. Some think it's dragon breath.
I teach the guards to care for their blades. A well-kept sword lasts years.
Swords are for defending. Never for bullying. I tell every buyer that.
I trade blades for coal and emeralds. The coal goes fast.
I've been experimenting with axe heads. Heavier hits, slower swings.
Sweeping edge lets you hit a whole crowd of zombies. Very satisfying.
I hope one day the village won't need my work at all.
My grandfather made swords for a king. I make them for neighbors. I prefer neighbors.
The sound of a blade being sharpened is the sound of peace being kept.
Fire Aspect sets enemies alight. Don't use it near hay. I learned that.
A hilt wrapped in good leather never slips.
I test every blade on a hay bale. The hay bales are not fans of me.
I made a wooden sword for every child in {village}. Safer than mine.
Maces are back in fashion, I hear. Heavy things. For falling on enemies.
My hands know the shape of a good blade by heart.
I sleep better knowing the guards have good steel.
The best weapon's the one you never have to draw.
I forged through the night once to arm the village before a raid. Never again, I hope.
Iron, fire, hammer, water. Four things and a lifetime of practice.
Swords hang on my wall like sleeping dogs. Let them sleep.
work.leatherworker: Cow hide, rabbit hide, and a lot of scraping. Leatherwork's not for the faint of nose.
I've just finished a saddle. Smooth as butter. The horses will love it.
Leather armor's light and quiet. Good for hunters and the nervous.
I dye my leather. Red, blue, green. The adventurers love bright colors.
The cauldron's my best tool. Washing, dyeing, soaking.
I made a pair of boots that'll last ten years. Guaranteed. Mostly guaranteed.
Rabbit hide's soft enough for gloves. Rabbits disagree.
I've got a horse armor order. Leather barding for the knight's mount.
Bundles! I've been making bundles. Little leather bags for all your little things.
Scaly turtle leather makes the strangest helmets.
The tanning racks smell, but the leather's worth it.
I stitch every seam twice. Double stitching never fails.
A good belt's the foundation of any outfit.
I trade leather for emeralds and flint. Flint for cutting.
I made the cleric a book cover. Gold-tooled. Very fancy.
Leather breathes. That's why it's better than iron for long walks.
Everyone needs good boots. You'd be amazed how many people don't have them.
I can tell a cow's age by its hide. Strange skill. Useful, somehow.
I made a little leather pouch for {friend}. They keep buttons in it.
Leather horse armor's dyeable. Purple horses. Fashion.
My hands are tough as my hides.
I keep my needles in a pincushion shaped like a pig. Gift from my mother.
Waterproofing's the secret. Beeswax and patience.
A well-made saddle is the difference between a long ride and a long walk.
I made a tiny saddle for a pig once. The pig was very proud.
Some leather's for armor, some's for books, some's for shoes. All of it's useful.
I've got blisters from the awl. Nobody tells you about the awl.
The nicest thing anyone said to me: "These boots feel like home."
I smell like a cow. I've made my peace with it.
Leather's warm in winter and cool in summer. Perfect material.
I patched the farmer's apron four times this year. He's very rough on aprons.
Every scrap gets used. Off-cuts become laces, laces become bracelets.
I'm proud of my craft. It's old, quiet and honest.
I've been teaching the children to braid leather cords.
Good leather ages like a good friend. Softer and better every year.
work.mason: Stone's patient. You have to be patient with it.
I cut every brick in the church wall. Took me a summer.
The stonecutter makes clean cuts. Saves me hours of chiseling.
Terracotta, quartz, polished granite. I love all the stones.
Mortar's half the trick. The other half's knowing where to put it.
I've been building a new wall around the well. It's going to be lovely.
Glazed terracotta has the prettiest patterns. Fit four together and they make a circle.
I've got stone dust in my lungs and stone in my heart.
Chiseled stone bricks are my favorite. A little decoration never hurt anyone.
A good foundation's everything. Houses, friendships, villages.
I can tell where a stone came from just by its color.
Deepslate's tough to cut, but it makes fine tiles.
I'm building a little bridge over the stream. Arched. Very elegant.
The clay pits by the river are where I get my bricks. Muddy work.
A wall should stand for a hundred years. Mine will.
Sandstone crumbles. Granite lasts. Choose your stone wisely.
I trade stone and pottery for clay and emeralds.
Every brick I lay is a promise to the people inside.
I carve little faces into stones where nobody looks. My secret signature.
Mason's work is slow. That's the point.
I polish andesite until it shines like water.
The hardest part of building is waiting for the mortar to set.
I made a fountain for the square. It's not finished. It might never be finished.
Stone remembers. Every crack, every chip. Like an old face.
I'm teaching the young ones to lay bricks straight. It's harder than it looks.
Calcite's lovely and white. Rare round here.
A good mason never rushes. A bad mason rebuilds.
Bricks and mortar, rain and time. That's all a wall needs.
I patched the church steps. Again. People really stomp on those steps.
I'd like to build a tower someday. Tall enough to see three villages.
Stone's cold to touch but it holds the warmth of the sun all night.
I made pots for everyone's herbs. Terracotta, hand-pressed.
Some people see rocks. I see houses waiting to happen.
I've got stone chips in every pocket. I find them in my bed.
The old builders used mud bricks. I'm trying their recipe. It's very muddy.
work.shepherd: The sheep have been grazing on the east meadow. They're fat and happy.
I've sheared six sheep today. My arms are wool. Everything's wool.
Dyed wool's my specialty. I made a rainbow flock once. Pink one's my favorite.
The loom clacks all day. Banners, carpets, beds. It's all wool in the end.
Sheep are smarter than people think. Not much smarter. But a bit.
The wolves came sniffing last night. The golem chased them off.
Shearing doesn't hurt them. They grow it right back. Like magic.
I count my sheep every evening. It's soothing. Also it makes me sleepy.
Brown sheep, black sheep, white sheep. Every one's a friend.
I made beds for half the village. Wool and wood. Simple and warm.
Banners are fun to design. I made one with a creeper face. People hated it.
A good shepherd knows every sheep by name. I know mine by personality.
The lambs are adorable this year. Wobbly little things.
Sheep eat grass and grass grows back. A good arrangement for everyone.
I made a scarf from my own sheep's wool. It's itchy, but it's mine.
Dyeing a sheep is easier than dyeing wool. The color stays when it regrows.
I trade wool for emeralds and dyes. And paintings, sometimes.
The sheep wander off if you don't watch them. Like children.
Carpets are just very flat wool. Very comfortable flat wool.
I named one sheep Princess. She acts like it too.
Shears need sharpening every week. Wool's tough stuff.
I lie in the meadow with the sheep on sunny days. They don't mind.
I spun a whole bale of yarn this morning.
Purple sheep are rare. You need red and blue dye. I have three.
The loom's patterns are endless. I've only scratched the surface.
I lost a sheep last week. Found her on the church roof. Don't ask how.
Sheep follow you anywhere if you hold wheat. Useful trick.
The best bed in {village} is mine. Five layers of wool.
I sing to the flock in the evenings. They seem to like the low notes.
My dog helps me herd. Well, he barks. The sheep do the rest.
Winter's coming. Everyone's buying wool.
I can tell a good sheep by its fleece. Thick, soft, clean.
My hands smell of lanolin. Very good for the skin, apparently.
I made a wool blanket for the golem. It didn't want it. I left it anyway.
Shepherding's quiet work. Grass, sky, sheep, me.
work.butcher: The smoker's been going since dawn. Smell that? Ham.
I trade meat for coal and emeralds. Cooked meat, of course.
Rabbit stew's my specialty. Carrots, mushrooms, potato and love.
I've got sausages hanging from every beam. My house smells wonderful.
A good butcher wastes nothing. Nothing at all.
Cooked porkchops are the best food there is. Ask anyone.
The smoker cooks twice as fast as a furnace. Food only, mind.
I make jerky for the travelers. Lasts forever. Tastes like a boot. A tasty boot.
Salted fish for the winter, smoked meat for the summer.
My knives are sharp and my apron's stained. Hard work.
Sweet berries make a lovely glaze. Don't tell anyone my secret.
I feed the whole village on feast days. Biggest roast you've ever seen.
Kelp dries well in the smoker. Good snack, if you're desperate.
I'm careful with my knives. Ten fingers, still. Proud of that.
A butcher's job is to make sure nobody goes hungry.
I've been practicing a new stew. Mutton and beetroot. It's purple.
The dogs follow me everywhere. Can't imagine why.
I trade for sweet berries and coal. Coal keeps the smoker going.
My grandmother's recipe for roast chicken has been in the family forever.
I've got a cleaver older than my house.
Cooked salmon with a bit of honey. You'll never eat anything else.
Hunger's the worst enemy. Worse than zombies. I fight it every day.
The smell of my smoker brings people from three houses away.
I'm not just a butcher. I'm a cook, a trader, a feeder of families.
I give the scraps to the village dogs. They're very loyal.
Stew's best on cold nights. Sit by the fire with a bowl.
I've been smoking meat since I was a child. It's in my blood.
Good food makes good friends.
I can carve a roast in thirty seconds. It's my party trick.
Beef stew, mushroom stew, rabbit stew. I'm a stew person.
My hands smell of smoke. Permanently.
A full belly makes a happy village.
I hang garlic over the door. Keeps the bats away. And the visitors.
Feast days are my favorite. Everyone eats together.
I make sure the guards get the best cuts. They earn it.
work.nitwit: Work? I'm busy watching the clouds. They need someone to watch them.
I tried a job once. Didn't take. I'm more of a free spirit.
I'm a professional appreciator. Of sunsets, mostly. And naps.
Everyone else works so hard. Someone has to remind them to stop and look around.
I spent the morning lying in the meadow. Very productive meadow time.
I'm conducting important research into how many naps fit into one day.
People call me lazy. I call myself relaxed.
I don't have a workstation. I have a favorite haystack.
I help in my own way. Mostly by being cheerful.
I'm the village's official greeter. Unofficially. Self-appointed.
I tried farming. The carrots hated me. The feeling was mutual.
My job is to make sure the bench by the well is comfortable. It is.
I follow the cats around. They know all the best spots.
I'd work, but who'd keep everyone company?
I'm an expert in doing nothing. It's harder than it looks.
I have many talents. I'm still discovering what they are.
I asked the librarian for a job. She gave me a book on patience. I'm still reading it.
I'm the only one in {village} who's never in a hurry.
I hum. That's my contribution to society.
Every village needs someone who stops to smell the flowers. I'm that someone.
I tried to make bread once. The kitchen still smells of it. Not in a good way.
Work is for people who don't know how to enjoy a sunny day.
I guard the bench by the well. Nobody's stolen it yet.
I'm saving my energy for something important. I don't know what yet.
I watch everyone work and cheer them on. Very supportive.
I can name every cloud shape there is. That's a skill.
I'm the village's resident dreamer. It's a full-time position.
Somebody has to taste-test the baker's pies. I volunteered.
I collect interesting pebbles. That's a job, right?
Busy? Me? Never. And proud of it.
I've got a very important nap scheduled for this afternoon.
I tried to be a librarian but I kept falling asleep on the books.
My workstation is the sky. I'm very good at looking at it.
The children love me. I'm the only grown-up who plays tag.
I'm a philosopher, really. A lying-down philosopher.
work.none: I'm between jobs at the moment. Looking for the right workstation.
Nobody's built a workstation near me yet. I'm patient.
I'd love to be a librarian. If someone places a lectern, I'm there.
I help where I'm needed. Carrying things, mostly.
Without a job I've got time to think. Too much time, maybe.
I keep wandering past the workstations, hoping one calls my name.
I've been helping the farmer. Unofficially. He hasn't noticed.
A job's not everything. But it'd be nice to have one.
I'd like to work at a sewing table. Or an easel. Something with color.
I tried every workstation in the village. They're all taken.
If you build a new workshop, I'm your resident. Just saying.
I'm good with my hands. I just need something to put them to.
Every day I check if there's a free workstation. Every day there isn't.
I've been sweeping the square. Nobody asked. It needed sweeping.
Some people find their calling young. I'm still listening for mine.
I'd make a fine cook. Or a fine anything, really, given the chance.
Without a job, the days are long. But the evenings are lovely.
I'm learning a bit of everything while I wait.
If a cartography table appears, I'll be there before the dust settles.
I help the children with their lessons. That's a sort of job.
I'm not lazy. I'm just unassigned.
Maybe I'm meant to be an adventurer like you.
I'd take any honest work. Even shearing. Especially shearing, actually.
I fetch water for the old folks. Keeps me busy.
I've been offered a job as a scarecrow. I think it was a joke.
I keep my hands busy whittling. Maybe I'll be a carpenter.
I spend my days walking the village. I know every stone.
Someone told me if you put a blast furnace near me, I'll become an armorer. Fancy!
A workstation is like a home for your hands.
I'm ready for whatever work finds me.
I help out at the market. Unpaid. For the gossip.
I've been practicing my trading face. Very serious. Very honest.
One day I'll have a workstation and a trade and a proper apron.
I'm not worried. Work comes to those who wait. And walk past workstations a lot.
I'd be a bard if I could carry a tune. I can't, so I'm waiting.
work.general: Work's work. Some days it's a song, some days it's a grind.
I like being useful. It makes the day feel full.
Every job in the village matters. Even the small ones. Especially the small ones.
I'm good at what I do. That's not bragging. It's just true.
Honest work, honest pay, honest sleep.
Whatever we do, we do it for each other here.
Work's better when the sun's out and the bell's ringing.
I take pride in every job, big or small.
The village runs on all of us pulling together.
At the end of the day, tired hands are happy hands.
I learned my trade from someone wiser. Now I'm teaching someone else.
A day's work done right is a good night's sleep.
There's always more to learn, even after years at it.
I like my job. Not every day. Most days.
Work's how I say thank you to {village}.
The trades keep the village alive. Emeralds keep the trades alive.
I've had a busy week. Busy's good. Busy means people need me.
I could do my job in my sleep. Some mornings I nearly do.
Every workstation in {village} has a story.
The best part of work is finishing it.
I trade fair. Ask anyone. Well, most people.
My hands know what to do even when my head's elsewhere.
Good work speaks for itself. I just help it along.
Some jobs are fun. Some are necessary. Mine's both.
I'd rather be busy than bored.
work.on: I'm at my station right now. Watch and you'll see how it's done.
Work hours! Can't stop long, but I'm glad you're here.
This is the busiest part of my day. Pull up a stool.
I've been at it since the bell. Hands haven't stopped.
I'm in the middle of something. Talk to me while I finish it.
Right now? Working. Always working at this hour.
You've caught me mid-task. Perfect timing, actually. I needed a break.
My station's warm and my work's flowing. Good day for it.
Watch your elbows. Work in progress.
I'm right where I should be. At work, doing my bit.
I've done half today's work already. The other half's waiting impatiently.
Busy, busy. But never too busy for you.
The workday's in full swing. Can you hear it? Everyone's hammering, sawing, stirring.
Ask me anything about the trade. I'm in the mood to explain.
This is my favorite part of the day. Hands busy, mind clear.
work.off: I'm off duty now. Ask me tomorrow and you'll get the full speech.
Work's done for today. My station's tidied and my feet are up.
Don't make me think about work, it's my free time!
I'll be back at it in the morning. For now, I'm just me.
I clocked off an hour ago. Well, the bell clocked me off.
Off-hours! I've left work at work, where it belongs.
I think about work even when I'm not working. Is that bad?
The station will still be there tomorrow. So will I.
Work's finished. Now I'm just a neighbor like anyone else.
I'm resting my hands. They've earned it.
I never talk shop after hours. Except to you. And {friend}.
I put my tools away neatly. Ready for the morning.
It's not working hours, so I'm not working. That's the rule.
Ask me about work in the morning, when I'm fresh.
work.weather.rain: The rain slows everything down. Wet hands, wet tools.
Work goes on, rain or no rain.
Rainy days are good for indoor work. I've been catching up.
The rain gets into everything. My workbench is damp.
I don't mind working in the rain. It keeps the flies away.
Rain means half the village is indoors and my work's twice as quiet.
work.weather.thunder: I stopped working when the thunder started. Not worth the risk.
The storm's too loud to concentrate.
Nobody works through a storm like this. Not if they're sensible.
I covered my station and ran. It'll keep.
work.weather.snow: Cold fingers make for slow work.
I keep a brazier by my station in winter. Toasty.
Snowy days, everyone wants warm things. Good for business.
The cold makes the tools stiff. And me.
work.weather.hot: It's too hot to work hard, so I'm working slowly.
I wet my hat in the well every hour. Keeps my head cool.
In this heat, I do the heavy work at dawn.
The sun's brutal today. I've moved my station into the shade.
work.knight: I drill with the training dummy every morning. It never hits back, which is restful.
A knight's job is mostly standing still and looking alert. The rest is moments of terror.
I've been training the young ones with wooden swords. One of them's got real talent.
My armor needs polishing. It always needs polishing.
I patrol the village twice a day. Every path, every fence.
The dummy's taken a beating today. Poor thing has a pot for a helmet and still no fear.
A good shield is worth three swords. I'll stand by that.
I keep my sword sharp and my temper dull.
Every scar I have, I earned keeping this village safe.
Zombies come in the dark. I'm usually there to meet them.
I've been practicing my footwork. It's all in the feet, a fight.
The archers and I have a rivalry. I say a blade's more honest. They say I'm slow.
A raid's the worst thing that can happen to a village. I'm ready for one.
The tailor mends my padding when I'm on duty. Bless her quick fingers.
Discipline isn't glamorous. But it's what keeps people alive.
I sleep with my boots by the bed. Old habit.
My helmet's dented in three places. Three creepers. All defeated.
The children want to be knights. I tell them to be farmers. Farmers live longer.
I swing at that dummy until my arms burn. Then I swing some more.
Every morning I check the walls. Every evening I check them again.
A knight's oath is simple: protect the village, help the weak, don't run from spiders.
I gain a little more skill every day I train. The dummy's my best teacher.
I'm not the strongest, but I'm the most stubborn. That counts for a lot.
My grandfather was a guard. His sword hangs over my fireplace.
Courage isn't not being afraid. It's being afraid and standing your ground anyway.
I've been sparring with the dummy so long I've started apologizing to it.
Watch the treeline at dusk. That's where trouble starts.
I keep the peace. Sometimes that means a sword. Usually it means a kind word.
I've faced pillagers, vindicators and one very angry ravager. Still here.
The night watch is long, but the dawn makes it worth it.
Strike the dummy yourself if you like. It'll tell you how hard you hit. Humbling.
My shield arm's stronger than my sword arm. That says something about my job.
Every night I pray the bell stays quiet.
I'm a knight. I'm also a terrible cook. Nobody's perfect.
A good knight knows when not to fight.
work.archer: I've been at the target since dawn. Three bullseyes in a row this morning.
Draw, breathe, release. Draw, breathe, release. That's the whole art.
The archery target's my second home. I know every ring on it.
I can hit a skeleton at fifty paces. Before it hits me, ideally.
The fletcher makes my arrows. Best in the region. I'd never use anyone else's.
Wind's the archer's enemy. You learn to read it.
I keep watch from the rooftops. Best view in {village}.
A bow's quiet. That's what I like about it.
I've been practicing at the target. Practice arrows only; nothing sharp in the village.
The knights think arrows are cowardly. The knights also get bitten a lot.
My string snapped this morning. Mid-draw. Stung like a bee.
I can split a stick at thirty paces. Showing off, mostly.
Patience makes a better archer than strength.
The center ring's gold, then red, then blue, then black, then white. I aim for gold. I hit blue a lot.
I learned to shoot from my mother. She could hit a falling apple.
Every arrow you loose is a promise you can't take back.
I stand guard on the night watch with a quiver full of arrows and a pocket full of bread.
Shoot the target yourself, if you like. It'll tell you how close you got.
I count my arrows every evening. Archers who don't, run out.
Phantoms are the worst to hit. They swoop.
I'd rather shoot a target than anything alive. Targets don't flinch.
My fingers are calloused from the string. Ugly hands, good aim.
A good archer stands very still. I'm the stillest person in {village}.
Training gets you ready for the moment you hope never comes.
I painted my target myself. The bullseye's a little lopsided.
Spectral arrows make things glow. Very helpful at night.
I've been teaching the children to shoot. Blunt arrows, soft targets.
The best shot I ever made was one I didn't take.
I can hear a skeleton's bones rattle from across the field. Skill or paranoia? Both.
My bow's made of yew. It's older than me.
Morning practice keeps the eye sharp. Evening practice keeps the nerves calm.
I watch the treeline. Always the treeline.
A crossbow's for people who don't trust their arms. I trust mine.
Breathe out, then loose. Never hold your breath.
Some people meditate. I shoot.
work.cook: The stove's been lit since before dawn. Breakfast, lunch, and I'm already thinking about supper.
I make a dish of the day at my stove. Come by and you'll get a helping. One each, mind.
Bread on even days, stew on odd days. That's the kitchen's rhythm.
Hearty stew, fresh bread, steaming coffee. The holy trinity.
My stove cooks twice as fast as a campfire. Put your raw meat on it and watch.
A good cook never measures. A great cook measures and then ignores it.
I've been simmering this stew since sunrise. The longer, the better.
Carrots, potatoes, beef, a pinch of something secret. That's all I'll say.
The whole village eats at my stove eventually.
I burned my thumb on the stove this morning. Kitchens bite back.
Cooking's love you can taste.
I've been experimenting with a pumpkin soup. It's either brilliant or terrible.
The smell of baking bread is the best alarm clock in the world.
I cook for the guards before their night watch. Warm bellies, brave hearts.
Salt, fire and patience. That's cooking.
I trade bread and stew for wheat and emeralds.
My kitchen's small but my portions are large.
Somebody always comes sniffing around the stove at noon. Usually several somebodies.
The chimney smokes all day when I'm cooking. It's how everyone knows I'm open.
I've fed this village for years. Every face here has eaten my bread.
A meal shared is a meal doubled. That's kitchen mathematics.
I've got flour in my hair, sauce on my sleeve and a smile on my face.
Never trust a thin cook.
The kettle sings on my stove all morning.
Cooking for one is boring. Cooking for a village is an adventure.
I've got a new bread recipe with honey. People have been lining up.
The fire's the hardest part. Too hot, it burns. Too cool, it's raw.
My stove's my pride. I scrub it every evening.
Taste everything. Twice. That's the cook's privilege.
I can tell the bread's done by the sound when I knock on it.
On Market Day, I cook from dawn to dusk. Everyone's hungry on Market Day.
Rabbit stew's the hardest to get right. Rabbit stew is also the best.
If you've got raw food, bring it by. The stove's always hot.
A full pot is a happy pot.
I'll teach you a recipe someday. When you've earned it.
work.tavern_keeper: The barrels are full and the mugs are clean. Ready for the evening crowd.
I press cider from apples in the drinks barrel. Bring me apples and I'll pour you a mug.
The tap stand pours coffee. Cocoa beans in, steaming mugs out.
Running a tavern means knowing everyone's business and keeping it to yourself.
I restock the barrel every working day. Apples, berries, and a bit of muscle.
A warm fire, a full mug and a friendly face. That's what a tavern's for.
I've heard every story in {village}. Most of them twice. Some of them true.
Bring an empty mug and I'll fill it. That's the tavern way.
Somebody broke a stool last night dancing. Again.
The bard's been playing here every evening. The crowd loves it.
I sweep the floor three times a day. Taverns get muddy.
Every village needs a tavern. Where else would people complain about the weather together?
I know who likes their cider warm and who likes it cold.
The busiest hour is right after supper. Everyone wants one more drink and one more story.
I wipe down the counter so often it's worn smooth.
Tavern keeping is half pouring, half listening.
I keep a slate of everyone's tabs. Some of them are very long.
I make a special spiced cider for Market Day. People talk about it all week.
The fireplace is the heart of the tavern. I never let it go out.
My feet ache after a long night. But a full tavern's a happy one.
I've broken up three arguments this week. All about pie.
A tavern without music is just a room with chairs.
I open late and close later. My sleep's a mess.
Coffee in the mornings, cider in the evenings. Something for everyone.
Travelers always stop at the tavern first. I'm the welcome committee.
I've got the best seat in the house. Behind the counter, watching everyone.
I keep a spare blanket for anyone who's had a long night.
I can pour a mug blindfolded. I've done it. For a bet.
The cider barrel's the most popular resident in {village}.
I like a busy night. Laughter and clinking mugs. Music to my ears.
Every mug I pour, I hope it makes someone's day a little warmer.
I've been tavern keeper for years. I know every creak in the floor.
The apples this year are sweet. The cider's going to be special.
Tavern's open to everyone. Even grumpy folks. Especially grumpy folks.
I'll pour you a mug if you've got an empty one. That's a promise.
work.apothecary: I keep bandages and smelling salts ready. A little preparation goes a long way.
The press squeezes herbs into tonics. Three flowers and a glass bottle make an Herbal Tonic.
I tend to anyone hurt near my workstation. Scrapes, bruises, the occasional arrow.
Chamomile for sleep, lavender for nerves, poppy for pain.
The alchemical press is my pride and joy. You turn the bar and the herbs give up their goodness.
I've been gathering flowers all morning. My basket smells like summer.
Bring me berries, ferns or kelp too. All herbs have something to give.
A tonic a day keeps the cleric away. Don't tell the cleric I said that.
I've got remedies for coughs, colds, aches and broken hearts. Well, not hearts. I'm working on hearts.
The smelling salts can wake a fallen companion. Very useful on adventures.
I keep my bottles corked and labeled. Mixing them up would be a disaster.
Healing's slow work. Patience is the best medicine.
I sit with the sick and keep them company. That's half the cure.
The revival tonic's my best work. It can bring someone back from the edge.
Herbs, honey, hot water. That's my answer to most things.
I've been studying the old herbals. Some of them are pure nonsense. Some of them work.
I smell like a meadow all day. Not a bad thing.
I dabbed salve on three skinned knees this morning. Children are reckless.
The press needs a strong arm and a gentle heart.
I keep a cot ready for anyone who needs a rest.
Bandage wraps from paper and wool. Simple and effective.
Never mix poison with potion. Rule one of the apothecary.
My hands are always green from the herbs.
I grow my own mint behind the house. It's taking over the garden.
A good apothecary listens before she treats.
I make a cough syrup from honey and berries. The children pretend to cough to get it.
If you're hurt, come to my workstation. I'll patch you up.
I learned the old remedies from my grandmother. The new ones I'm learning from mistakes.
The press drips green when the herbs are fresh. That's how you know it's good.
I can tell what's wrong with most people just by looking at them. Except for grumpiness. That's incurable.
A dried flower in a book, a fresh one in a tonic. Both have their uses.
Prevention's better than cure. Eat your vegetables, wear your armor.
I've got a tonic for courage. It's mostly honey. It still works.
The best medicine is a good night's sleep and a friend to talk to.
I'll keep you in one piece, {player}. That's my job.
work.painter: My easel's set up by the window. The light's perfect this time of day.
I paint a new picture every day. Some days it's good. Some days it's a learning experience.
When a painting's finished, take it off my easel and hang it at home. I'll start another.
A dye or two on a blank canvas makes a sketch, then a picture. Try it yourself!
I've been painting the sunset all week. It keeps changing on me.
Blue for the sky, green for the hills, a dab of gold for the sun. That's most landscapes.
I paint portraits too. Sit still and I'll make you famous.
My fingers are every color today.
I wanted to paint the sea, so I mixed blue dye. Blue dye makes ships, apparently.
Mixing colors is like cooking. Too much of anything ruins it.
I've painted every building in {village}. Twice.
A painter sees the world differently. Everything's a shape and a shade.
I've got a painting of a creeper in a meadow. It's my most popular work. I don't understand people.
I sketch in charcoal first. Then the colors come.
My paintbrush has seen things. Mostly the sky.
Art takes patience. And a lot of dye.
I painted the village at night with all the windows lit. It made the cleric cry.
Every finished painting goes to whoever takes it home. Art should be lived with.
The paint pots on my easel tray are always running low.
Painting outdoors is best. Painting in the rain is not.
I'm trying to capture the light on the river. It won't hold still.
Some people collect emeralds. I collect sunsets.
A blank canvas is terrifying and exciting at the same time.
I painted the flowers in a vase this morning. The vase was empty. I imagined the flowers.
My work hangs in half the houses in {village}.
Colors have feelings. Red's angry, blue's calm, yellow's showing off.
I paint what I love. That's why there are so many paintings of bread.
Bring a paintbrush to a finished canvas and I'll show you how to start over.
The best painting I ever did was of my mother. She hung it upside down.
I get paint everywhere. My cat's slightly purple.
I paint best in the afternoons. Morning light's too sharp.
I'm working on a mural for the tavern wall. It's going to be enormous.
Painting is just looking very carefully and then telling the truth with color.
You can have any painting you find finished on my easel. That's a promise.
I see beauty everywhere. Even in mud. Especially in mud. Lovely browns.
work.bard: I play the music stand every evening at the tavern. Come and listen!
Music lifts the spirits. Literally. When I play, everyone works a little faster.
Play the stand yourself if you like. Everyone nearby gets a little spring in their step.
I know songs from every corner of the world. Well, three corners.
My lute's been with me for years. We've been through a lot.
A bard's job is to remember the stories and sing them back.
I'm working on a ballad about {village}. It has thirty verses. So far.
The tavern goes quiet when I start a sad song. That's the best feeling.
I can play "Greensleeves," "Frère Jacques" and a jig I wrote myself.
The children dance when I play. The adults pretend they're not tapping their feet.
I practice at my music stand in the mornings. The roosters harmonize, sort of.
Every song's a little bit of magic. I believe that.
I wrote a lullaby for the golem. It didn't fall asleep. It doesn't sleep.
A tavern without a bard is just a room full of people drinking quietly.
My fingers are calloused from the strings. Worth it.
I play for coins on Market Day. Mostly I get apples.
Music makes the long nights shorter.
Hold a lute and play the stand for a guitar sound. A bell for chimes. An amethyst for something magical.
I've been learning to play the flute. The neighbors have been learning to sleep with pillows over their heads.
Songs are how villages remember who they are.
I once played so long my fingers fell asleep.
Everyone hums my tunes. They don't know they're mine. I don't mind.
A good song can stop an argument mid-shout.
I play a quiet tune at dusk to call everyone home.
My sheet music's mostly scribbles only I can read.
Music is the only thing that sounds better shared.
I'm composing a song for each resident. Yours will have a lot of drums. Adventurous drums.
When the bell rings for a wedding, I play the procession.
Sometimes I just play to the empty square. The pigeons appreciate it.
A bard is a walking library of songs.
I'd play for the Ender Dragon if it'd listen.
I tune my lute every morning. It goes out of tune every afternoon. It's a moody lute.
I've got a new song about a brave chicken. It's a crowd favorite.
Music, stories and a warm mug. That's a bard's whole life.
Play a tune for the village. They'll love you for it.
work.tailor: Needle, thread, and a steady hand. That's tailoring.
Bring me torn leather or a frayed bowstring and I'll mend it at my sewing table. A bit of string, that's all.
Wool unravels into string at my table. Handy if you're out of thread.
I mend the guards' padding while they're on duty. They come back to it good as new.
I've been sewing a rain cloak. Waterproofed with beeswax. Very fashionable.
A good seam is invisible. That's how you know it's good.
I've got pins in my mouth half the day. Don't make me laugh.
Every coat in {village} has a stitch of mine in it somewhere.
Bolts of wine and mustard cloth. My two favorite colors.
I patched the farmer's trousers again. He kneels on everything.
A hooded poncho for every traveler. Rain or shine.
My spool of red thread is my most precious thing.
I measure everyone by eye. You're a size "adventurer," by the way.
I'm making a cloak for the knight. Blue with silver trim.
The trick to sewing is never rushing the last stitch.
Leather boots, wool cloaks, linen shirts. I make it all.
I can mend almost anything. Except a broken heart. Though I try with a nice scarf.
I've been embroidering flowers on the cleric's robes. Don't tell her yet.
Thimbles save fingers. I've learned that the painful way.
My sewing table's covered in scraps. Every scrap's a future patch.
Elytra need delicate mending. Very delicate. Very expensive.
I make uniforms for every trade in the village. Each one's different.
The bard wants a cape with stars on it. I'm on it.
I sew by candlelight in the evenings. Bad for the eyes. Good for the soul.
A well-made garment can last a lifetime.
I found a moth in my wool. We had words.
I'm teaching my niece to sew. She's better at it than I was.
Clothes make people feel like themselves. That's important work.
Fishing rods, bows, crossbows. All mendable with good string.
I've got a pincushion shaped like a tomato. It's very old. It's very loved.
I can tell a lot about a person from the state of their sleeves.
Bring me your worn things. I'll make them good as new.
I darn socks for the whole village. Socks wear out faster than anything.
Fashion comes and goes. Good stitching stays.
Every garment I make, I make it like it's for a friend.
work.carpenter: The sawmill cuts logs into half again as many planks as hand-crafting does. Bring me your logs.
I've been building benches for the village square. Sturdy ones. No more wobbling.
Measure twice, cut once. My father said it. I say it. My apprentice is sick of hearing it.
The saw sings when the wood's good. Squeaks when it's not.
I leave offcuts by the sawmill. Sticks are always handy. Help yourself.
I built half the houses in {village}. The other half I've repaired.
Oak's my favorite. Strong, honest, smells lovely.
Spruce for roofs, oak for floors, birch for furniture. Every wood has its place.
My hands are covered in splinters. Occupational hazard.
I made a rocking chair for my grandmother. She says it's the best chair in the world.
A good joint needs no nails. Just a snug fit.
I'm building a new bridge over the stream. Arched, of course.
Sawdust in my hair, sawdust in my boots, sawdust in my soup.
Planks into sticks, three to a plank at my sawmill. Much better than the crafting table.
I fixed the church door. It stopped creaking. The cleric's thrilled.
A carpenter's work is everywhere. Doors, floors, beds, barrels.
I can tell the age of a tree by its rings. That oak was older than the village.
I carved a little bird for the windowsill. It's mostly for me.
Sanding's the boring part. Also the most important part.
I built a treehouse for the children. They haven't come down since.
The sawmill's the best tool in my workshop. It saves me hours.
Every house in {village} needs fixing eventually. I'm never out of work.
I made a cradle for the newest baby. Smoothed every edge.
Wood breathes, wood moves, wood remembers. You have to respect it.
I've got a hammer for every job and a job for every hammer.
I'd like to build a ship someday. A real one. With a mast.
I mended the well's roof last week. Now it doesn't leak on people's heads.
A crooked shelf is a carpenter's nightmare.
I build things to last. My great-grandchildren will sit on my benches.
I keep a stack of planks by the door. You never know.
My workshop smells of sap and pine. Best smell in the world.
I made the notice board by the bell. Proudest work I've done.
Bamboo's strange wood. Grows fast, splits easy. Saws nicely, though.
Bring me a log and I'll show you what it wants to be.
Woodwork's slow, but it's honest.
work.scholar: I keep the village archives. Every birth, wedding and great event in {village}.
Bring a book to the archives and I'll copy out the village chronicle for you.
Study with me while I work at the archives. You'll learn a thing or two. Literally.
Every neighbor has a story worth keeping. Our archives help us remember where we came from.
I've been cataloguing the village's history. Did you know we once had a mayor who was a llama? Briefly.
Scrolls, ledgers, boxes of letters. The archives are a treasure.
I write down the news every day. Someday, someone will want to know.
History isn't dusty. It's people. People are never dusty.
I'm working on a history of the founding of {village}. Lots of goats in it.
The archives smell of old paper and candle wax. My favorite smell.
Right-click the archives with an empty hand and you'll read the village news. Hold a book to copy it all.
I've read every letter in the archive. Some of them made me cry.
A scholar's work is never done. History keeps happening.
I teach lessons by the bell some mornings. The children are better students than they think.
Knowledge kept is knowledge shared. Eventually.
I found a map in the archives showing a village that isn't there anymore.
I study everything. Plants, stars, people. Especially people.
My candle burns down every night. I go through a lot of candles.
I've been writing an encyclopedia of {village}. Volume one: the bell.
The past teaches us. If we listen.
I keep records of every wedding. The happiest pages in the archive.
Ink, quill and a good chair. All a scholar needs.
I've got questions no book can answer. That's what keeps me going.
The library's for books. The archives are for us. Our own story.
I record the weather every day. Patterns emerge. Slowly.
Every resident in the village has a page in my ledger.
I've been reading about the old kingdoms. They had bells too.
Scholars and librarians are cousins. We argue about filing systems.
I wrote down the bard's songs so they'll never be forgotten.
Curiosity is the scholar's only qualification.
I've been translating an old stone tablet. It's either a poem or a shopping list.
History is just yesterday's gossip with better handwriting.
The archives are open to everyone. Knowledge shouldn't be locked away.
I'd like to know what the first villagers dreamed about.
Every day is a page. I'm writing as fast as I can.
station.farmer: My composter turns scraps into bone meal. Feed it anything that rots.
Put a composter near any unemployed neighbor and you might make a farmer.
Fill the composter to the top and it'll give you bone meal. Spread that on your crops.
Bring me your rotten apples and old seeds. The composter's hungry.
A farmer's workstation is a barrel of muck. A very useful barrel of muck.
Composting is just patience in a bucket.
station.librarian: The lectern holds a book open so anyone can read it. Put a book and quill on it to share your writing.
A lectern near a free resident makes a librarian. Then bring them books.
The lectern gives off a little redstone signal when you turn the page. Clever, isn't it?
I keep my favorite book on the lectern. You may read it, but don't fold the corners.
Lecterns and bookshelves go together like bread and butter.
If you want enchanted books, a librarian with a lectern is your friend.
station.fisherman: The barrel by my door holds my catch. Sixty-four of anything per slot. Very roomy.
Give a free resident a barrel and they'll take up fishing.
My barrel keeps the fish fresh. Well, fresh enough.
A barrel's a good chest for small spaces. It opens even with something on top.
Barrels smell of fish after a while. All of them. Forever.
I trade fish for emeralds. My barrel's always stocked.
station.fletcher: The fletching table's for arrows and bows. Mostly arrows.
Put a fletching table near an unemployed resident and they'll learn to make arrows.
My fletching table's covered in feathers and flint. Organized chaos.
A fletching table is a sort of promise. Arrows when you need them.
The table's where I sort my feathers. White on the left, grey on the right.
Every good archer needs a fletcher, and every fletcher needs a table.
station.cleric: The brewing stand bubbles all day. Blaze powder fuels it; nether wart starts every potion.
A brewing stand near a free resident makes a cleric.
Put water bottles in the stand, add nether wart, then your ingredient. Magic.
My brewing stand's been in the church for generations.
The stand's three arms hold three bottles. Efficient.
Blaze powder burns slow in the stand. One rod lasts a long time.
station.cartographer: The cartography table copies and zooms maps. Paper makes them bigger.
A cartography table near a free resident makes a mapmaker.
Lock a map with glass at the table and it'll never change.
My cartography table's got compass marks scratched all over it.
Two maps in, one copy out. Perfect for travelers.
The table's the most useful thing in my house. And the most cluttered.
station.armorer: The blast furnace smelts ore and armor twice as fast. Only metal, mind.
A blast furnace near a free resident makes an armorer.
Melt old iron armor in the blast furnace and you'll get nuggets back.
My blast furnace roars all day. You get used to it.
Fuel it well and it'll smelt a stack before lunch.
The blast furnace is faster than a regular furnace, but it won't cook your supper.
station.toolsmith: The smithing table upgrades diamond gear to netherite and puts trims on armor.
A smithing table near a free resident makes a toolsmith.
The smithing table's for the clever work. Upgrades and decorations.
I use the smithing table for finishing touches.
Templates go in the smithing table. Rare things, templates.
A smithing table never wears out. Unlike my patience.
station.weaponsmith: The grindstone repairs and removes enchantments. Good for a fresh start.
A grindstone near a free resident makes a weaponsmith.
Put two worn swords in the grindstone and you'll get one better one.
The grindstone strips curses off. Most curses.
I spin the grindstone all day. My arms are like iron.
The grindstone gives you a bit of experience back when you strip enchantments.
station.leatherworker: The cauldron holds water, lava or powder snow. I use it for dyeing and washing leather.
A cauldron near a free resident makes a leatherworker.
Wash the dye off leather armor in a cauldron of water.
My cauldron's always full. Rain fills it up for free.
Cauldrons catch drips from pointed dripstone. Clever trick, that.
The cauldron's the oldest tool in my trade.
station.mason: The stonecutter makes stairs, slabs and walls from a single block. No waste.
A stonecutter near a free resident makes a mason.
One stone block in, one stone stair out. The stonecutter's a marvel.
My stonecutter's blade spins so fast you can't see it.
Mind your fingers near the stonecutter.
The stonecutter saves me so much stone.
station.shepherd: The loom turns banners into art. Dye plus a pattern, and you've got a crest.
A loom near a free resident makes a shepherd.
Put a banner and a dye in the loom and pick a pattern. Endless designs.
My loom clacks all day. It's like a heartbeat.
Banner patterns go in the loom too. Creeper faces, flowers, globes.
station.butcher: The smoker cooks food twice as fast as a furnace. Food only.
A smoker near a free resident makes a butcher.
Smoked meat keeps longer and tastes better. Everyone knows that.
Put raw meat and fuel in the smoker and you'll have supper in no time.
The smoker's smoke tells the whole village when dinner's coming.
station.knight: Strike my training dummy to see how hard you hit. It shows your combo too.
The dummy won't break if you hit it. Sneak and swing if you want to move it.
I train on the dummy every working day. A little more skill each time.
Put a training dummy near a free resident and you might make a knight.
The dummy's got a pot for a helmet. Aim for the bullseye on its chest.
A full swing does more damage than a quick tap. The dummy will show you.
station.archer: Shoot the archery target and it'll tell you your score. Ten for the bullseye.
Put an archery target near a free resident and you might make an archer.
I loose practice arrows at the target every working day. Blunt ones; they hurt nobody.
The target's rings go gold, red, blue, black, white. Gold is ten points.
Arrows that clip the edge still earn a point. Everyone deserves a point.
Practice makes the archer. The target never complains.
station.cook: My kitchen stove cooks raw food twice as fast as a campfire. Four pieces at a time.
Put raw meat, fish or potatoes on the stove and they'll pop out cooked.
When I've worked at my stove, there's a dish of the day for every visitor. Just ask.
A kitchen stove near a free resident might make a cook.
The stove's fire glows while something's cooking. Smell that?
One helping of the dish of the day per visitor. I'm generous, but not that generous.
station.tavern_keeper: The drinks barrel takes apples and berries and pours cider into an empty mug.
The tap stand brews cocoa beans into coffee. Bring a mug.
I restock the barrel and the tap every working day.
A drinks barrel or a tap stand near a free resident might make a tavern keeper.
Right-click the barrel with an empty hand to see how many mugs are left.
Cider warms you up and helps you heal a little. Coffee gives you a spring in your step.
station.apothecary: Press three herbs, flowers, berries, ferns or kelp, then bring a glass bottle for an Herbal Tonic.
The alchemical press holds up to twelve herbs at once.
When I work at my press, anyone hurt nearby gets patched up.
An alchemical press near a free resident might make an apothecary.
An Herbal Tonic gives you a few seconds of regeneration. Gentle stuff.
Every flower in the meadow has a little medicine in it.
station.painter: Paint my easel's canvas with a dye to sketch, and a second dye to finish the painting.
The color of the second dye decides the picture: blue for the sea, red for flowers, yellow for a sunset.
Take a finished painting off the easel with an empty hand. It's yours to hang.
A paintbrush on a finished canvas paints it over into a different picture.
I paint a new picture on my easel every working day.
An easel near a free resident might make a painter.
station.bard: Play my music stand and everyone nearby gets Haste for a minute. Music makes the work go faster.
Hold a lute when you play the stand for a guitar sound. A bell rings like chimes.
The stand knows ten songs. Some old, some mine.
I perform at my stand every working day. The neighbors gather round.
A music stand near a free resident might make a bard.
Let a song finish before you start another. Even bards need to breathe.
station.tailor: Mend leather, bows, fishing rods and elytra at my sewing table with string.
Unravel wool into string at the sewing table. Three lengths per block.
Each length of string mends a quarter of the damage. Bring enough.
When I'm sewing, I mend the guards' armor too.
A sewing table near a free resident might make a tailor.
Good thread, good needle, good table. That's all tailoring needs.
station.carpenter: My sawmill turns a log into six planks instead of four. And planks into three sticks.
The sawmill cuts up to sixteen at a time. Saves your arm.
I leave offcuts at the sawmill when I work. Take the sticks if you need them.
A sawmill near a free resident might make a carpenter.
Bamboo blocks saw into planks too.
Sawmills are louder than they look. Mind your ears.
station.scholar: Open the archives with an empty hand to read the village news.
Hold a book to the archives and I'll copy you the whole village chronicle.
Study near me while I'm at the archives and you'll pick up a little experience.
Archives near a free resident might make a scholar.
The chronicle has everything: births, weddings, quarrels, the lot.
Everything that happens in {village} ends up in the archives eventually.

ask: Be honest with me. Are you a sunrise person or a sunset person?
Settle an argument for me. Sunrises or sunsets?

answers.label: Sunrise, always
answers.reply: Me too! The whole village goes pink for a minute and nobody else is awake to see it.

answers.label: Sunset, easily
answers.reply: A sunset person. Then you'd love the view from the bell around six. It's like the sky's on fire.

answers.label: Whichever has breakfast
answers.reply: Ha! A practical answer. I respect that.

ask: Cats or dogs? I need to know who I'm dealing with.
Important question: are you a cat person or a dog person?

answers.label: Cats, obviously
answers.reply: A cat person! Creepers are scared of them, you know. Very sensible choice.

answers.label: Dogs, every time
answers.reply: A dog person! Loyal, brave, a bit muddy. Suits you.

answers.label: Parrots
answers.reply: Parrots! Bold. Noisy. I like it. Teach yours to say my name.

answers.label: Llamas
answers.reply: Llamas? They spit! ...I suppose you'd forgive them anything.

ask: If you could only eat one forever: something sweet or something savory?

answers.label: Sweet. Cake forever.
answers.reply: A cake person. I'll remember that next time there's a party.

answers.label: Savory. Give me stew.
answers.reply: A stew person! You'd get on well with our cook.

answers.label: Bread. Just bread.
answers.reply: Just bread. Simple, honest, perfect. I couldn't agree more.

ask: Do you like the rain, or are you a sunshine sort?

answers.label: I love the rain
answers.reply: You love the rain? Most people run from it! You're a kindred spirit, then.

answers.label: Sunshine, please
answers.reply: Sunshine it is. The village is prettiest in the sun anyway.

answers.label: Snow beats both
answers.reply: Snow! Quiet and white and sparkly. I like how you think.

ask: Where are you from, really? You don't talk like anyone from around here.
Do you have a home somewhere, out there past the hills?

answers.label: A house I built myself
answers.reply: You built it yourself? Then you know what it means to make a place your own.

answers.label: Wherever I sleep tonight
answers.reply: A wanderer at heart. I hope you'll count {village} as one of your homes.

answers.label: Somewhere far away
answers.reply: Far away. You must miss it sometimes. You can always tell me about it.

answers.label: Here, I hope
answers.reply: Here? Oh, that's the nicest thing anyone's said all week.

ask: What's the scariest thing you've ever faced out there?

answers.label: Creepers. Every time.
answers.reply: Creepers! Silent, green and explosive. I'd scream too.

answers.label: The warden
answers.reply: The warden? The one in the deep dark that hears your heartbeat? You're braver than anyone I know.

answers.label: Endermen
answers.reply: Endermen give me the shivers. Don't look them in the eye, they say.

answers.label: Nothing scares me
answers.reply: Nothing at all? Hmm. Even heroes are allowed to be scared, you know.

ask: Out of everywhere you've been, where's the most beautiful place?

answers.label: Cherry groves
answers.reply: Cherry groves! Pink petals everywhere. I'd love to see one someday.

answers.label: The ocean
answers.reply: The ocean. All that blue going on forever. I've only dreamed about it.

answers.label: Snowy mountains
answers.reply: Snowy peaks! Cold and quiet and enormous. You've got good taste.

answers.label: Right here
answers.reply: Right here? In {village}? Oh, you're just saying that. ...Are you? Thank you.

ask: Are you a day person or a night owl, {player}?

answers.label: Up with the sun
answers.reply: Early riser! You'd get on with the farmers. They're up before the roosters.

answers.label: Night owl
answers.reply: A night owl. Be careful out there after dark. The phantoms like sleepy people.

answers.label: I nap whenever I can
answers.reply: Ha! You'd love our nitwit. Naps are his whole philosophy.

ask: What's your favorite thing to eat after a long day?

answers.label: Golden carrots
answers.reply: Golden carrots! Very fancy. Very nourishing. You must be rich.

answers.label: Pumpkin pie
answers.reply: Pumpkin pie! The baker would adore you.

answers.label: Steak, well cooked
answers.reply: A steak person. Hearty and simple. The butcher would approve.

answers.label: Whatever's in my pocket
answers.reply: Whatever's in your pocket? Oh, you poor thing. Come back at supper and I'll feed you properly.

ask: Why do you do it? All the traveling, the danger. What keeps you going?

answers.label: To see everything
answers.reply: To see everything. I understand that. The world's too big to leave unseen.

answers.label: To build something great
answers.reply: To build something great. I'd like to see it when it's done.

answers.label: For the people I meet
answers.reply: For the people. That's the best answer anyone's ever given me.

answers.label: Honestly, I'm not sure
answers.reply: Not sure? That's honest. Maybe you'll find out on the way.

ask: If you could only keep one tool forever, which would it be?

answers.label: My pickaxe
answers.reply: The pickaxe. Of course. Can't get anywhere without digging.

answers.label: My sword
answers.reply: Your sword. Practical, but I hope you need it less and less.

answers.label: My fishing rod
answers.reply: A fishing rod! Peace, patience and supper all in one.

answers.label: A bed
answers.reply: A bed? Ha! Is that a tool? I suppose it is. The best one.

ask: Do you have a lucky number? I'm collecting them.

answers.label: Seven
answers.reply: Seven! Like the days of our week. Lucky indeed.

answers.label: Sixty-four
answers.reply: Sixty-four! A full stack. Very satisfying number.

answers.label: Thirteen
answers.reply: Thirteen? Bold. Most people think that's unlucky. You like to be different.

ask: What's your favorite color? I'm painting something and I need inspiration.

answers.label: Blue, like the sky
answers.reply: Blue! Calm and clear. I'll use a lot of it.

answers.label: Green, like the grass
answers.reply: Green! Like the hills around {village}. Lovely.

answers.label: Red, like redstone
answers.reply: Red! Bold. Like a poppy, or a warning sign.

answers.label: Purple, like amethyst
answers.reply: Purple! Royal and mysterious. I knew you had good taste.

ask: Is {village} the first village you've ever visited?

answers.label: The very first
answers.reply: The first? Then we'd better make a good impression! Welcome, properly.

answers.label: One of many
answers.reply: One of many. I hope we're one of your favorites.

answers.label: My favorite one
answers.reply: Your favorite? Oh, I'm going to tell everyone you said that.

ask: If you tamed a wolf tomorrow, what would you call it?

answers.label: Biscuit
answers.reply: Biscuit! Adorable. Every wolf deserves a snack name.

answers.label: Shadow
answers.reply: Shadow. Very mysterious. Very cool.

answers.label: Sir Barks-a-Lot
answers.reply: Sir Barks-a-Lot! That's the best name I've ever heard. I'm laughing.

answers.label: Wolf
answers.reply: Just "Wolf"? Practical. Very practical. A little sad.

ask: If you could build anything at all, what would it be?

answers.label: A castle in the clouds
answers.reply: A castle in the clouds! You'd need a lot of scaffolding. And courage.

answers.label: A cozy cottage
answers.reply: A cozy cottage. Simple, warm and yours. That's the best dream there is.

answers.label: A giant farm
answers.reply: A giant farm! You'd feed the whole world.

answers.label: A redstone machine
answers.reply: A redstone machine! What would it do? Never mind, I wouldn't understand it.

ask: Do you like music? The bard's always looking for requests.

answers.label: I love a good jig
answers.reply: A jig! Tell the bard. The tavern floor could use the exercise.

answers.label: Something slow and sad
answers.reply: Slow and sad. Sometimes those are the songs that help most.

answers.label: I only like note blocks
answers.reply: Note blocks! You and the redstone folk. Beep boop.

ask: How do you start your mornings? Coffee? Cider? Water from the well?

answers.label: Coffee, strong
answers.reply: Strong coffee! The tavern's tap pours a good mug. Bring your own.

answers.label: Cider, warm
answers.reply: Warm cider in the morning? You're a bit wild, aren't you? I like it.

answers.label: Milk, cold
answers.reply: Cold milk! Good for the bones, they say. And for curing bad potions.

answers.label: Whatever's nearest
answers.reply: Whatever's nearest. A true adventurer.

ask: Would you say you're brave or careful?

answers.label: Brave
answers.reply: Brave. I could tell. Just don't be brave and foolish at the same time.

answers.label: Careful
answers.reply: Careful. Good. The careful ones come home.

answers.label: Both, depending
answers.reply: Both! Brave when it counts, careful when it doesn't. That's wisdom.

ask: Do you collect anything? I have a box of interesting buttons.

answers.label: Music discs
answers.reply: Music discs! Creepers drop them, I hear. Only when skeletons shoot them. Strange world.

answers.label: Flowers
answers.reply: Flowers! Press them in a book and they'll last forever.

answers.label: Ores and gems
answers.reply: Ores and gems. A treasure hunter. I'd love to see your collection.

answers.label: Friends
answers.reply: Friends! Well, you've got one more now. Me.

ask: What's the best day you've ever had? I like to collect those too.

answers.label: The day I found diamonds
answers.reply: Diamonds! I'd have screamed. Did you scream? You screamed.

answers.label: The first night I survived
answers.reply: Your first night! I remember mine. Hiding in a hole in a hill, waiting for dawn.

answers.label: A quiet day here
answers.reply: A quiet day here? In {village}? That makes me so happy.

ask: Where do you sleep when you're on the road?

answers.label: In a bed I carry
answers.reply: A bed in your pack? Very sensible. Phantoms hate people who sleep.

answers.label: Under the stars
answers.reply: Under the stars! Romantic. Also full of spiders.

answers.label: I don't sleep much
answers.reply: You don't sleep much? Please do. The phantoms will come for you.

ask: Are you more of a miner or a builder?

answers.label: Miner, deep down
answers.reply: A miner! You'd love the old mineshafts. Rails and cobwebs everywhere.

answers.label: Builder, up high
answers.reply: A builder! The carpenter would love to talk shop with you.

answers.label: Explorer, far away
answers.reply: An explorer! Never staying put long enough to dig or build. I understand.

answers.label: Farmer, honestly
answers.reply: A farmer at heart! The best kind of person. Don't tell the miners I said so.

ask: What's the hardest lesson the world's taught you?

answers.label: Never dig straight down
answers.reply: Never dig straight down. My grandfather said the same thing, and he learned it the hard way.

answers.label: Always carry a bed
answers.reply: Always carry a bed. Wise. The night comes for everyone.

answers.label: Don't trust gravel
answers.reply: Gravel! Falling on your head when you least expect it. Treacherous stuff.

answers.label: Kindness is worth it
answers.reply: Kindness is worth it. That's a lesson I hope everyone learns.

ask: When you travel, do you like company, or do you go alone?

answers.label: Alone, mostly
answers.reply: Alone. Peaceful, but lonely. You can always take a friend from {village}, you know.

answers.label: With a wolf
answers.reply: With a wolf! A loyal friend who never complains. Lovely.

answers.label: With friends
answers.reply: With friends. Adventures are better shared.

ask: If you could put any enchantment on yourself, which would it be?

answers.label: Mending
answers.reply: Mending! Heal as you learn. That's beautiful, actually.

answers.label: Feather Falling
answers.reply: Feather Falling. Very sensible for someone who climbs things.

answers.label: Fortune
answers.reply: Fortune! Double everything. Greedy, but honest.

answers.label: Unbreaking
answers.reply: Unbreaking. I like that. Being hard to break is a good thing to want.

ask: Can I ask something silly? Are you ever afraid of the dark?

answers.label: Sometimes, yes
answers.reply: Me too. Thank you for saying so. It makes me feel less silly.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never? I envy you. I keep a candle lit all night.

answers.label: Only without a torch
answers.reply: Only without a torch. Fair. Torches make everything braver.

ask: Do you keep a journal of your adventures?

answers.label: Every single day
answers.reply: Every day! I'd love to read it someday. Only the parts you'd let me.

answers.label: I keep it in my head
answers.reply: In your head. Then I hope your head has a very good memory.

answers.label: I draw maps instead
answers.reply: Maps instead of words. A cartographer's soul.

ask: When's your birthday? I keep a list so nobody's ever forgotten.

answers.label: I don't know
answers.reply: You don't know? Then let's say it's Market Day. Every Market Day. More cake that way.

answers.label: Today, actually
answers.reply: Today?! Happy birthday! Why didn't you say? I'll tell everyone.

answers.label: I don't celebrate it
answers.reply: You don't celebrate? Everyone deserves one day that's just theirs. Think about it.

ask: If you could change one thing about {village}, what would it be?

answers.label: More lanterns at night
answers.reply: More lanterns. You're right, the paths get very dark. I'll mention it at the next meeting.

answers.label: A bigger tavern
answers.reply: A bigger tavern! Everyone would agree with that. Especially the bard.

answers.label: Nothing. It's perfect.
